  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python\n\"\"\"Isotropic-equivalent energy E_iso for the co-detected FRB sample.\n\nFor each sightline with a spectroscopic host redshift and a joint CHIME+DSA\nscattering fit, integrate the fitted fluence spectrum F(nu) = c0 (nu/nu_ref)^gamma\nover each telescope's OWN observed band, convert each band to an ABSOLUTE Jy\nscale, k-correct, and sum:\n\n    E_iso = (4 pi D_L(z)^2 / (1+z)) [ s_C int_CHIME F_C dnu + s_D int_DSA F_D dnu ]\n\nwhere s_C, s_D are the per-band flux scales (Jy per native .npy fluence unit;\n`flux_jy_per_unit` in configs/telescopes.yaml).\n\nWhy the flux scale is mandatory (see analysis/burst_energies/CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md):\nthe joint fit recovers c0 in the input dynamic spectrum's NATIVE units, and CHIME\nand DSA are not on a common flux standard. c0_C and c0_D are therefore in\nindependent, arbitrary per-telescope units. Summing two such bands is summing\ndollars and yen: it is not an energy, and the per-burst CHIME:DSA mix varies, so\neven the relative ORDERING of the total is unreliable. So this script refuses to\nemit an energy until BOTH bands carry a real `flux_jy_per_unit` (from each\ntelescope's SEFD + beam response at the burst position). Until then it reports the\nband fluence integrals in native units, flagged uncalibrated, and writes a\n\"pending calibration\" LaTeX stub rather than a publishable table of fake erg.\n\nThe (1+z) bandwidth k-correction (Zhang 2018) is applied by default; the\nno-k-correction value is tabulated alongside so the manuscript can state the\nconvention explicitly.\n\nref_freq is the band centre (f_min+f_max)/2; the fitter uses median(freq), which\nequals the centre for a symmetric, uniformly-flagged band (small <~few% offset\nunder asymmetric channel flagging -> minor vs the calibration systematic).\n\nUsage:  python analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py [--check]\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport yaml\n\nREPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nsys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))\n\nimport astropy.units as u  # noqa: E402\n\nfrom galaxies.v2_0.config import COSMO, TARGETS  # noqa: E402\n\nJOINT_DIR = REPO / \"analysis\" / \"scattering-refit-2026-06\" / \"joint_json\"\nTEL_CFG = REPO / \"configs\" / \"telescopes.yaml\"\nOUT_DIR = REPO / \"analysis\" / \"burst_energies\"\n\nJY_MS_HZ_TO_SI = 1e-29  # 1 Jy*ms*Hz = 1e-29 J*m^-2\nJ_TO_ERG = 1e7\nPLACEHOLDER_Z = 1.0  # Freya/Mahi/Johndoeii carry z=1.0000 as a \"redshift unknown\" flag\n\n\ndef band_edges_hz() -> dict[str, tuple[float, float, float]]:\n    \"\"\"(nu1, nu2, nu_ref) in Hz per band from the instrument config (band centre = ref).\"\"\"\n    cfg = yaml.safe_load(TEL_CFG.read_text())\n    out = {}\n    for key, tag in ((\"chime\", \"C\"), (\"dsa\", \"D\")):\n        f1 = cfg[key][\"f_min_GHz\"] * 1e9\n        f2 = cfg[key][\"f_max_GHz\"] * 1e9\n        out[tag] = (f1, f2, 0.5 * (f1 + f2))\n    return out\n\n\ndef flux_scales() -> dict[str, float | None]:\n    \"\"\"tag -> flux_jy_per_unit (Jy per native fluence unit), or None if uncalibrated.\"\"\"\n    cfg = yaml.safe_load(TEL_CFG.read_text())\n    return {tag: cfg[key].get(\"flux_jy_per_unit\") for key, tag in ((\"chime\", \"C\"), (\"dsa\", \"D\"))}\n\n\ndef band_integral(c0: float, gamma: float, nu_ref: float, nu1: float, nu2: float) -> float:\n    \"\"\"int_{nu1}^{nu2} c0 (nu/nu_ref)^gamma dnu  [native*ms*Hz], freqs in Hz.\"\"\"\n    if abs(gamma + 1.0) < 1e-9:  # power law -> 1/nu, integral is a log\n        return c0 * nu_ref * np.log(nu2 / nu1)\n    g = gamma + 1.0\n    return c0 * nu_ref / g * ((nu2 / nu_ref) ** g - (nu1 / nu_ref) ** g)\n\n\ndef band_energy_erg(i_raw: float, flux_scale: float, d_l_m: float, z: float, kcorr: bool = True) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Band fluence integral [native*ms*Hz] x flux scale [Jy/native] -> E [erg].\n\n    (1+z) bandwidth k-correction (Zhang 2018, ApJ 867 L21) applied when kcorr=True.\n    \"\"\"\n    factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + z) if kcorr else 1.0\n    return 4.0 * np.pi * d_l_m**2 * i_raw * flux_scale * JY_MS_HZ_TO_SI * J_TO_ERG * factor\n\n\ndef load_redshifts() -> dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"nickname (lowercased) -> z_frb, from the galaxy-search TARGETS list.\"\"\"\n    return {name.lower(): z for name, _ra, _dec, z in TARGETS}\n\n\ndef load_joint_params() -> dict[str, dict]:\n    \"\"\"nickname (lowercased) -> {c0_C, gamma_C, c0_D, gamma_D} medians.\"\"\"\n    out = {}\n    for p in sorted(JOINT_DIR.glob(\"*_joint_fit.json\")):\n        d = json.loads(p.read_text())\n        pct = d[\"percentiles\"]\n        try:\n            out[d[\"burst\"].lower()] = {\n                k: pct[k][\"median\"] for k in (\"c0_C\", \"gamma_C\", \"c0_D\", \"gamma_D\")\n            }\n        except KeyError:\n            continue  # not a per-band-amplitude fit; skip\n    return out\n\n\ndef compute() -> list[dict]:\n    bands = band_edges_hz()\n    scales = flux_scales()\n    s_C, s_D = scales[\"C\"], scales[\"D\"]\n    calibrated = s_C is not None and s_D is not None\n    zs = load_redshifts()\n    fits = load_joint_params()\n    nu1_C, nu2_C, ref_C = bands[\"C\"]\n    nu1_D, nu2_D, ref_D = bands[\"D\"]\n\n    rows = []\n    for nick in sorted(fits):\n        z = zs.get(nick)\n        if z is None or abs(z - PLACEHOLDER_Z) < 1e-6:\n            continue  # no real host redshift -> cannot place a distance\n        fp = fits[nick]\n        d_l_m = COSMO.luminosity_distance(z).to(u.m).value\n\n        I_C = band_integral(fp[\"c0_C\"], fp[\"gamma_C\"], ref_C, nu1_C, nu2_C)\n        I_D = band_integral(fp[\"c0_D\"], fp[\"gamma_D\"], ref_D, nu1_D, nu2_D)\n\n        row = {\n            \"burst\": nick,\n            \"z\": z,\n            \"D_L_Mpc\": COSMO.luminosity_distance(z).to(u.Mpc).value,\n            \"c0_C\": fp[\"c0_C\"],\n            \"gamma_C\": fp[\"gamma_C\"],\n            \"c0_D\": fp[\"c0_D\"],\n            \"gamma_D\": fp[\"gamma_D\"],\n            \"I_CHIME_native_ms_Hz\": I_C,  # band fluence integral, NATIVE units\n            \"I_DSA_native_ms_Hz\": I_D,\n            \"calibrated\": calibrated,\n        }\n        if calibrated:\n            e_C = band_energy_erg(I_C, s_C, d_l_m, z)\n            e_D = band_energy_erg(I_D, s_D, d_l_m, z)\n            e_C0 = band_energy_erg(I_C, s_C, d_l_m, z, kcorr=False)\n            e_D0 = band_energy_erg(I_D, s_D, d_l_m, z, kcorr=False)\n            row.update(\n                flux_jy_per_unit_C=s_C,\n                flux_jy_per_unit_D=s_D,\n                E_iso_CHIME_erg=e_C,\n                E_iso_DSA_erg=e_D,\n                E_iso_erg=e_C + e_D,  # legitimate: both bands now in Jy\n                E_iso_erg_no_kcorr=e_C0 + e_D0,\n            )\n        rows.append(row)\n    return rows\n\n\ndef markdown_table(rows: list[dict]) -> str:\n    if rows and rows[0][\"calibrated\"]:\n        head = (\n            \"| Burst | z | D_L (Mpc) | gamma_C | gamma_D | \"\n            \"E_CHIME (erg) | E_DSA (erg) | E_iso (erg) | E_iso no-(1+z) (erg) |\"\n        )\n        sep = \"|\" + \"|\".join([\"---\"] * 9) + \"|\"\n        lines = [head, sep]\n        for r in rows:\n            lines.append(\n                f\"| {r['burst']} | {r['z']:.4f} | {r['D_L_Mpc']:.1f} | {r['gamma_C']:.2f} | \"\n                f\"{r['gamma_D']:.2f} | {r['E_iso_CHIME_erg']:.3e} | {r['E_iso_DSA_erg']:.3e} | \"\n                f\"{r['E_iso_erg']:.3e} | {r['E_iso_erg_no_kcorr']:.3e} |\"\n            )\n        return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n    # uncalibrated: band fluence integrals in NATIVE units, flagged not-an-energy\n    head = (\n        \"| Burst | z | D_L (Mpc) | gamma_C | gamma_D | \"\n        \"int F_C (native*ms*Hz) | int F_D (native*ms*Hz) |\"\n    )\n    sep = \"|\" + \"|\".join([\"---\"] * 7) + \"|\"\n    lines = [head, sep]\n    for r in rows:\n        lines.append(\n            f\"| {r['burst']} | {r['z']:.4f} | {r['D_L_Mpc']:.1f} | {r['gamma_C']:.2f} | \"\n            f\"{r['gamma_D']:.2f} | {r['I_CHIME_native_ms_Hz']:.3e} | {r['I_DSA_native_ms_Hz']:.3e} |\"\n        )\n    return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n\n\ndef _tex_pow(x: float) -> str:\n    r\"\"\"Render a float as a\\times10^{b} for LaTeX.\"\"\"\n    if x <= 0 or not np.isfinite(x):\n        return r\"\\mathrm{n/a}\"\n    exp = int(np.floor(np.log10(x)))\n    mant = x / 10**exp\n    return rf\"{mant:.2f}\\times10^{{{exp}}}\"\n\n\ndef latex_pending() -> str:\n    \"\"\"LaTeX stub written while the flux calibration is missing (no fake energies).\"\"\"\n    return r\"\"\"% Auto-generated by analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py -- do not hand-edit.\n% STATUS: flux calibration pending -- no energy table emitted (see below).\n\\subsection{Isotropic-equivalent energies}\n\\label{sec:burst-energies}\n\nIsotropic-equivalent burst energies are pending absolute flux calibration. The\njoint CHIME--DSA fit constrains each band's fluence spectrum only in the native\nunits of its input dynamic spectrum, and CHIME and DSA are not placed on a common\nflux standard, so the per-band amplitudes are not directly comparable and may not\nbe summed into an energy. Converting to physical $\\mathrm{Jy\\,ms}$ requires each\ntelescope's system-equivalent flux density and primary-beam response at the burst\nposition (Andersen et~al.\\ 2023 and the baseband CHIME/FRB catalog update for\nCHIME; Law et~al.\\ 2024 for DSA-110). Once those scales are supplied, the energy\nfollows $E_{\\mathrm{iso}} = (4\\pi D_L^2(z)/(1+z))\\,[\\,s_C\\!\\int F_C\\,d\\nu +\ns_D\\!\\int F_D\\,d\\nu\\,]$ with the $(1+z)$ bandwidth k-correction.\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef latex_section(rows: list[dict]) -> str:\n    body = []\n    for r in rows:\n        body.append(\n            f\"  {r['burst'].capitalize()} & ${r['z']:.4f}$ & ${r['D_L_Mpc']:.0f}$ & \"\n            f\"${r['gamma_C']:+.2f}$ & ${r['gamma_D']:+.2f}$ & \"\n            f\"${_tex_pow(r['E_iso_erg'])}$ \\\\\\\\\"\n        )\n    table_body = \"\\n\".join(body)\n    return rf\"\"\"% Auto-generated by analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py -- do not hand-edit.\n\\subsection{{Isotropic-equivalent energies}}\n\\label{{sec:burst-energies}}\n\nFor each sightline with a spectroscopic host redshift we estimate the\nisotropic-equivalent burst energy directly from the joint CHIME--DSA fit,\nwithout extrapolating either band's spectrum beyond where it is constrained.\nThe joint fit returns a per-band spectral amplitude and index,\n$F_X(\\nu) = c_{{0,X}}\\,(\\nu/\\nu_{{\\mathrm{{ref}},X}})^{{\\gamma_X}}$, which we put on\nan absolute scale with each telescope's flux calibration $s_X$\n($\\mathrm{{Jy}}$ per native unit) and integrate over its own observing\nband---CHIME over $0.400$--$0.800\\,\\mathrm{{GHz}}$ and DSA over\n$1.311$--$1.499\\,\\mathrm{{GHz}}$,\n%\n\\begin{{equation}}\nE_{{\\mathrm{{iso}}}} = \\frac{{4\\pi D_L^2(z)}}{{1+z}}\\left[\n  s_C\\!\\int_{{\\nu_1^{{C}}}}^{{\\nu_2^{{C}}}} F_{{\\mathrm{{CHIME}}}}(\\nu)\\,d\\nu\n  + s_D\\!\\int_{{\\nu_1^{{D}}}}^{{\\nu_2^{{D}}}} F_{{\\mathrm{{DSA}}}}(\\nu)\\,d\\nu\n\\right],\n\\label{{eq:eiso}}\n\\end{{equation}}\n%\nwith $D_L(z)$ from the fiducial \\textit{{Planck}}\\,2018 cosmology, the $(1+z)$\nbandwidth k-correction applied, and\n$1\\,\\mathrm{{Jy\\,ms\\,Hz}} = 10^{{-29}}\\,\\mathrm{{J\\,m^{{-2}}}}$. Bursts whose hosts\nlack a spectroscopic redshift are omitted. This band-restricted integral\nconstrains the energy released \\emph{{within the observed spectral envelope}}: it\navoids the large, model-dependent extrapolation that a single power law fit\nacross the full $0.4$--$1.5\\,\\mathrm{{GHz}}$ span would require, at the cost of not\ncounting flux in the unobserved $0.8$--$1.3\\,\\mathrm{{GHz}}$ gap (so the values are\nlower limits on the $0.4$--$1.5\\,\\mathrm{{GHz}}$ energy).\n\n\\begin{{table}}\n\\centering\n\\caption{{Isotropic-equivalent energies of the co-detected FRBs, integrated over\nthe CHIME ($0.4$--$0.8\\,\\mathrm{{GHz}}$) and DSA ($1.31$--$1.50\\,\\mathrm{{GHz}}$) bands\nfrom the joint scattering fit and put on an absolute scale with each band's flux\ncalibration. $\\gamma_C,\\gamma_D$ are the per-band spectral indices;\n$E_{{\\mathrm{{iso}}}}$ includes the $(1+z)$ k-correction.}}\n\\label{{tab:burst-energies}}\n\\begin{{tabular}}{{lccccc}}\n\\hline\\hline\nBurst & $z$ & $D_L$ [Mpc] & $\\gamma_{{C}}$ & $\\gamma_{{D}}$ & $E_{{\\mathrm{{iso}}}}$ [erg] \\\\\n\\hline\n{table_body}\n\\hline\n\\end{{tabular}}\n\\end{{table}}\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _check() -> None:\n    # 1. closed-form band integral must match a dense numeric quadrature\n    nu1, nu2, ref = 0.4e9, 0.8e9, 0.6e9\n    for c0, g in ((2.0, -3.4), (0.18, -4.95), (1.0, -1.0), (3.0, 0.5)):\n        nu = np.linspace(nu1, nu2, 200_001)\n        num = np.trapezoid(c0 * (nu / ref) ** g, nu)\n        ana = band_integral(c0, g, ref, nu1, nu2)\n        assert abs(ana - num) / abs(num) < 1e-6, (c0, g, ana, num)\n\n    # 2. oracle: flat spectrum (gamma=0, c0=1) over a known band, scale=1, gives the\n    #    analytic energy; (1+z) divides it; doubling the flux scale doubles it.\n    i_flat = band_integral(1.0, 0.0, ref, nu1, nu2)\n    assert abs(i_flat - (nu2 - nu1)) < 1e-3, i_flat  # int 1 dnu = bandwidth\n    e0 = band_energy_erg(i_flat, 1.0, d_l_m=1.0, z=0.0)\n    assert abs(e0 - 4.0 * np.pi * (nu2 - nu1) * JY_MS_HZ_TO_SI * J_TO_ERG) < 1e-6 * e0\n    assert abs(band_energy_erg(i_flat, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) - e0 / 2.0) < 1e-9 * e0  # (1+z)=2\n    assert abs(band_energy_erg(i_flat, 2.0, 1.0, 0.0) - 2.0 * e0) < 1e-9 * e0  # linear in scale\n\n    # 3. uncalibrated config (null scales) must NOT emit an energy\n    assert flux_scales() == {\"C\": None, \"D\": None} or all(\n        v is not None for v in flux_scales().values()\n    ), \"telescopes.yaml flux scales are partially set; calibrate both or neither\"\n    print(\"self-check OK: integral matches quadrature; energy oracle + k-correction exact\")\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    if \"--check\" in sys.argv:\n        _check()\n        return\n\n    rows = compute()\n    if not rows:\n        sys.exit(\"no bursts with both a real redshift and a joint c0/gamma fit\")\n\n    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    (OUT_DIR / \"burst_energies.json\").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2))\n    calibrated = rows[0][\"calibrated\"]\n    tex = latex_section(rows) if calibrated else latex_pending()\n    (OUT_DIR / \"burst_energies.tex\").write_text(tex)\n\n    print(markdown_table(rows))\n    print(\n        f\"\\nN = {len(rows)} bursts.  \"\n        f\"Skipped: placeholder z=1.0 (freya/mahi/johndoeii) and any sightline \"\n        f\"without a joint c0/gamma fit (e.g. casey).\"\n    )\n    if not calibrated:\n        print(\n            \"\\n*** UNCALIBRATED: configs/telescopes.yaml has no flux_jy_per_unit for \"\n            \"one or both bands. ***\\n\"\n            \"The columns above are band fluence integrals in NATIVE .npy units -- NOT \"\n            \"energies, NOT comparable across bands, NOT to be quoted. Supply \"\n            \"flux_jy_per_unit (Jy per native unit, from each telescope's SEFD + beam \"\n            \"response at the burst position) for BOTH bands to emit E_iso. See \"\n            \"analysis/burst_energies/CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md.\"\n        )\n    print(f\"\\nWrote {OUT_DIR / 'burst_energies.json'}\")\n    print(f\"Wrote {OUT_DIR / 'burst_energies.tex'} ({'energy table' if calibrated else 'calibration-pending stub'})\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"

## Adversarial review: Phase-1 burst-energy diff

**Overall: PASS.** The diff does exactly what it claims. I tried to falsify each of the seven checks and could only land minor nitpicks. The core science fix (refuse to emit energies until both bands carry a real Jy scale; apply the (1+z) k-correction; scale each band before summing) is correct and empirically verified.

### Findings (severity-tagged, file:line)

**1. Calibrated gate — PASS.** `calculate_burst_energies.py:121` `calibrated = s_C is not None and s_D is not None`. Empirically confirmed: monkeypatching `flux_scales()` to `{"C": 1.0, "D": None}` yields `calibrated=False` and **zero** `E_iso*` keys in the output rows. Partial calibration cannot leak an energy. The `calibrated` flag is computed once from config and stamped uniformly on every row (`:148`), so the `rows[0]["calibrated"]` dispatch in `markdown_table`/`latex_section`/`main` (`:168`, `:322`) can never see a mixed list — no latent heterogeneity bug.

**2. k-correction + scale-before-sum — PASS.** Verified `E_iso_erg == E_iso_erg_no_kcorr/(1+z)` to <1e-9 (`:151-161`). Verified `E_iso_erg == E_iso_CHIME_erg + E_iso_DSA_erg` and that `E_iso_CHIME_erg` uses `s_C` (not `s_D`) — recomputed by hand with `s_C=2.0, s_D=5.0`, matches. Each band is multiplied by its own scale *before* the sum, which is the whole point of the fix. The factor is applied once per band, not doubled.

**3. `band_integral` closed form — PASS.** `:78-83`. Power-law branch matches dense `trapezoid` quadrature to ~1e-14 (log branch, γ=−1) and ~1e-7 at γ=−1+2e-9 (general branch just outside the log window). Real data γ values (`freya gC=-0.983`, `whitney gC=-1.003`) sit ~0.02 from the singularity — far enough that the general branch's `1/g` factor (~1/0.017) is well-conditioned. The `1e-9` log-branch threshold is appropriately tight; nothing real triggers it, and it's there only to avoid a true 0/0.

**4. `_check()` oracle — PASS with one CONCERN.** Assertions 1–2 (`:287-302`) are genuine: closed-form vs. independent quadrature, and an analytic flat-spectrum oracle (∫1 dν = bandwidth; (1+z)=2 halves E; doubling scale doubles E). These are not tautological — they'd catch a wrong constant or a misplaced (1+z).
- **[CONCERN, low]** `calculate_burst_energies.py:304-307`: assertion 3 ("uncalibrated config must NOT emit an energy") does **not** call `compute()` — it only lints the *real config's* current state (both-null OR both-set). It would pass even if the gate logic in `compute()` were broken, as long as the YAML happened to be both-null. The comment oversells it: it reads as a behavior test but is a config-consistency lint. The actual gate is only exercised by my external monkeypatch, not by `--check`. Cheap hardening: add `assert not any("E_iso_erg" in r for r in compute())` under the current (uncalibrated) config, or temporarily patch `flux_scales`. Not blocking — the gate *is* correct — but the oracle has a hole.

**5. Autoformatter import hazard — PASS.** `ruff check --select F` clean. All imports consumed: `json`/`sys`/`Path`/`np`/`yaml` obvious; `astropy.units as u` used at `:133,141`; `COSMO, TARGETS` at `:99,133`. The two `# noqa: E402` after `sys.path.insert` are correct (imports deliberately after the path manipulation). No NameError risk.

**6. Over-engineering (ponytail) — PASS.** `flux_jy_per_unit` is the intended calibration seam (keep). No dead config, no single-use abstraction. `band_energy_erg` has the `kcorr` flag with two real call sites (with/without). One **[NITPICK]**: `markdown_table` (`:167-194`) duplicates the LaTeX content in a second format and is only printed to stdout — but it's the human-readable console view vs. the manuscript artifact, a defensible split, not bloat.

**7. Units — PASS.** Chain is correct *only* when `flux_jy_per_unit` carries Jy-per-native-unit, which the config comment and docstring both state. `band_integral` → native·ms·Hz (freqs in Hz, but the "ms" comes from `c0` carrying the native fluence-per-Hz-with-ms-time dimension — consistent with `JY_MS_HZ_TO_SI = 1e-29` for Jy·ms·Hz→J/m²). Then `×flux_scale` (Jy/native) → Jy·ms·Hz, `×1e-29` → J/m², `×4π D_L²` → J, `×1e7` → erg, `÷(1+z)` k-corr. No double-count, no missing factor. The `1 Jy·ms·Hz = 1e-29 J·m⁻²` identity is standard and the LaTeX states it explicitly (`:259`).

### Other observations (not diff bugs)
- The DSA `gamma_D` rails at the −5 prior floor for 7/11 bursts (`CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md` Q3). This is an upstream fit-quality problem, **not** this diff's job — and the diff's refusal-to-publish behavior correctly sidesteps it. The regenerated `.tex` is the calibration-pending stub (verified), so no fake energies ship.
- `analysis/burst_energies/` is fully untracked (`??`) — the regenerated outputs aren't yet committed. Flagging for your commit staging, not a code issue.
- Regenerated run confirms N=8 bursts, freya/mahi/johndoeii skipped on placeholder z=1.0, casey skipped (no joint fit) — matches the documented behavior.

=== h17 access memory ===
---
name: learning_h17-headless-agent-host
description: H17 (lxd110h17) as a subscription-only clean headless agent host — PATH-guard mechanism, /usr/local/bin wrapper fix, and API-key fail-closed wrappers for claude/codex
metadata:
  type: reference
---

**Host:** `lxd110h17` (Ubuntu 20.04, user `ubuntu` — shared account, passwordless sudo, `/home/ubuntu` 350G free). The DSA-110 imaging box; system conda at `/opt/miniforge` (no Lmod/module/spack). Reach as `ssh h17` (config alias). SSH prints a post-quantum warning banner on every connect — filter it from captures.

**Why bare-name CLIs failed non-interactively (the core gotcha):** `~/.bashrc` has the interactive guard `case $- in *i*) ;; *) return;; esac` near the top, and the PATH additions for `~/.local/bin` (claude, entire) and the nvm shim (codex) sit *below* it. So they load only for interactive shells. `~/.bash_profile` sources `~/.bashrc` but that early-returns non-interactively. `~/.profile` is dead for bash (because `~/.bash_profile` exists). Net: `ssh h17 'claude'` (bare = `bash -c`, sources nothing) and even `ssh h17 'bash -lc "claude"'` (login non-interactive, hits the guard) both fail to resolve claude/codex/entire. Only `bash -lic` (interactive) found them. **Do NOT use `bash -lic` for capture — its .zshrc/.bashrc banner contaminates stdout** ([[learning_zsh-interactive-shell-banner-contaminates-capture]]).

**The fix that covers every invocation form:** sshd hands non-interactive commands a fixed default PATH (`/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:...`) and sources no rc files. So **drop the agents into `/usr/local/bin`** (already on that PATH) — covers bare ssh, `bash -lc`, and cron alike. Editing profiles only helps shells that read them; bare `ssh host cmd` reads none. This also sidesteps the load-bearing DSA casa6 PATH-precedence logic in `.bashrc` (lines ~250/355 strip+re-add `~/.local/bin` so casa6 python wins) because we only place claude/codex/entire there, never python.

**What's installed (2026-06-04):**
- `entire` 0.7.5 → `~/.local/bin/entire` via `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash` (repo `entireio/cli`, non-interactive-friendly).
- `codex` 0.133.0 **native rust binary** → `~/.local/bin/codex` (downloaded `codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` from `openai/codex` release tag `rust-v0.133.0`). Node-free; decoupled from the nvm install (`~/.nvm/.../bin/codex` = node launcher `codex.js`, still present as interactive fallback). The npm package ships NO bundled linux binary in its `bin/` (only `codex.js` + `rg`).
- `claude` 2.1.147 → `~/.local/bin/claude` (versioned symlink → `~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.147`).

**Subscription-only, fail-closed (HARD requirement — never incur API costs):** `~/.secrets` (sourced pre-guard) injects `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (108c) and `OPENAI_API_KEY` (164c) into **even the bare-ssh environment**. Claude Code prefers `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` over OAuth when both exist → live API-billing exposure. Fix: `/usr/local/bin/claude` and `/usr/local/bin/codex` are **wrapper scripts** (not symlinks) that strip the keys before exec:
```
#!/bin/bash
exec env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN -u ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL /home/ubuntu/.local/bin/claude "$@"
```
```
#!/bin/bash
exec env -u OPENAI_API_KEY /home/ubuntu/.local/bin/codex "$@"
```
Plus `~/.codex/config.toml` has `preferred_auth_method = "chatgpt"`. Verified: `claude auth status` via wrapper drops the `apiKeySource` field → `loggedIn:true, oauth_token, firstParty` (ClaudeMax); `codex login status` → "Logged in using ChatGPT". Fail-closed: a lapsed subscription errors instead of silently billing. Standing rule per user: **only ClaudeMax / Codex-Pro/ChatGPT-Pro subscriptions, never API keys; never `--bare`** (see `~/CLAUDE.md` cursor-shell runbook).

**Residual (open):** *interactive* shells prepend `~/.local/bin` ahead of `/usr/local/bin`, so a human typing `claude`/`codex` at an H17 prompt hits the real binary, bypassing the wrapper → would see the keys. Headless orchestration (bare ssh → wrapper) is unaffected. To fully close, add interactive aliases to `~/.bashrc`: `alias claude='env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN claude --dangerously-skip-permissions'` and `alias codex='env -u OPENAI_API_KEY codex'`. Not yet applied (don't edit `.bashrc`/`.secrets` unprompted).

**Reversibility:** remove `/usr/local/bin/{claude,codex,entire}` (3 files) + `~/.local/bin/{codex,entire}` + the codex config line. nvm codex untouched.

**Headless invocation pattern:** `ssh h17 'claude -p "<task>" < /dev/null'` resolves the wrapper automatically (subscription-enforced). Expect ~60-90s startup (SessionStart hooks + MCP). Related: [[learning_cli-stdin-contracts]] (argv prompt ⇒ `< /dev/null`), [[learning_cross-session-handoff-via-resume]], [[feedback_codex_sandbox_masks_host_state]]. Entire requires a git-rooted session to checkpoint ([[learning_entire-checkpoints-per-repo-rooting]]); on H17 root an agent session inside a git repo + `entire enable --agent claude-code` to trace on-box work.

"""Unified primary beam model interface.

This module provides a consistent interface for primary beam calculations
across the pipeline. Uses EveryBeam via Docker (dsa110-contimg:gpu)
as the primary method, with graceful fallback to Airy disk model.

The approach prioritizes:
  1. Docker-based EveryBeam (when Docker available)
  2. Airy disk model (always available, matches EveryBeam generic dish)

The Airy disk model matches EveryBeam's implementation for generic dishes:
  PB(theta) = (2 * J1(x) / x)²
  where x = π * D * sin(theta) / λ
  J1 is the first-order Bessel function
"""

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np
from scipy.special import j1

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Note: Native EveryBeam Python bindings (everybeam_py) are not installed.
# We use Docker-based EveryBeam via dsa110-contimg:gpu container instead.
_EVERYBEAM_NATIVE_AVAILABLE = False


@dataclass
class BeamConfig:
    """Configuration for primary beam calculations.

    This dataclass consolidates beam model parameters, making it easier to
    pass beam configuration across the pipeline and reducing function signature
    complexity.

    Returns
    -------
    >>> config = BeamConfig(
        ...     frequency_ghz=1.4,
        ...     antenna_ra=0.1,
        ...     antenna_dec=0.2,
        ... )
        >>> response = primary_beam_response(config, src_ra=0.3, src_dec=0.4)
    """

    frequency_ghz: float
    antenna_ra: float
    antenna_dec: float
    dish_diameter_m: float = 4.65
    ms_path: str | None = None
    field_id: int = 0
    beam_mode: str = "analytic"
    use_docker: bool = True

    def __post_init__(self):
        """Validate beam configuration."""
        if self.frequency_ghz <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"frequency_ghz must be positive, got {self.frequency_ghz}")
        if self.dish_diameter_m <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"dish_diameter_m must be positive, got {self.dish_diameter_m}")
        if self.field_id < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"field_id must be non-negative, got {self.field_id}")
        valid_modes = {"analytic", "full", "numeric", "element", "array", "none"}
        if self.beam_mode not in valid_modes:
            raise ValueError(f"beam_mode must be one of {valid_modes}, got {self.beam_mode}")

# DSA-110 Measured System Parameters for Simulation
#
# This file contains system parameters with full provenance tracking.
# Each parameter includes measurement metadata, uncertainty, and validation status.
#
# Schema:
#   parameter_name:
#     value: <numeric or array>
#     unit: <string>
#     uncertainty: <numeric or array>
#     uncertainty_type: "std" | "systematic" | "combined"
#     measurement_date: <ISO 8601>
#     source_observations: [<list of MS files or observation IDs>]
#     derivation_method: <string describing calculation>
#     validation_status: "measured" | "validated" | "assumed" | "default"
#     references: [<list of papers, DOIs, or documentation links>]
#     notes: <optional additional information>
#     last_updated: <ISO 8601>
#     version: <semantic version>

metadata:
  schema_version: '1.0.0'
  created: '2025-11-25T00:00:00Z'
  last_modified: '2025-11-25T00:00:00Z'
  description: 'DSA-110 system parameters for rigorous simulation'
  contact: 'DSA-110 Team'

telescope_name: DSA-110
instrument_name: DSA-110_Continuum
site:
  latitude_deg: 37.2314
  longitude_deg: -118.2817
  altitude_m: 1222.0
layout:
  csv: DSA110_Station_Coordinates.csv
  polarization_array:
    - -5 # XX
    - -6 # YY
spectral:
  num_subbands: 16
  # NOTE: DSA-110 correlator outputs 48 channels per subband (768 total channels)
  # This was incorrectly set to 384 (CHIME value) - verified against real data
  channels_per_subband: 48
  channel_width_hz: 244140.625
  # Freq range updated to match actual correlator output (verified from sb00-sb15)
  # sb00: 1.4872-1.4986 GHz, sb15: 1.3114-1.3229 GHz
  freq_min_hz: 1311400000.0
  freq_max_hz: 1498600000.0
  reference_frequency_hz: 1405000000.0
temporal:
  integration_time_sec: 12.884902000427246
  total_duration_sec: 900.0
  samples_per_integration: 1
phase_center:
  ra_deg: 0.0
  dec_deg: 54.6
beam_model:
  config: beams.yaml

system_parameters:
  system_temperature:
    value: 50.0 # PLACEHOLDER - awaiting measurement
    unit: 'K'
    uncertainty: null
    uncertainty_type: null
    measurement_date: null
    source_observations: []
    derivation_method: 'ASSUMPTION - Not yet measured from real calibrator observations'
    validation_status: 'assumed'
    references: []
    notes: |
      Current value is an assumption based on typical L-band systems.
      Needs measurement via measure_system_parameters.py using calibrator observations.
      Expected range: 40-80 K for DSA-110 at 1.4 GHz.
    last_updated: '2025-11-25T00:00:00Z'
    version: '0.1.0'

  sefd:
    value: null # To be computed from T_sys and efficiency
    unit: 'Jy'
    uncertainty: null
    uncertainty_type: null
    measurement_date: null
    source_observations: []
    derivation_method: 'SEFD = 2 * k_B * T_sys / (A_eff * efficiency)'
    validation_status: 'default'
    references: []
    notes: |
      SEFD depends on T_sys and efficiency measurements.
      For DSA-110 with 4.65m dishes: SEFD ≈ 300-500 Jy (typical for small dishes).
      VLA at L-band: ~400 Jy, ASKAP: ~2000 Jy.
    last_updated: '2025-11-25T00:00:00Z'
    version: '0.1.0'

  aperture_efficiency:
    value: 0.7 # PLACEHOLDER - awaiting measurement
    unit: 'dimensionless'
    uncertainty: null
    uncertainty_type: null
    measurement_date: null
    source_observations: []
    derivation_method: 'ASSUMPTION - Typical value for small dishes'
    validation_status: 'assumed'
    references: []
    notes: |
      Aperture efficiency η = A_eff / A_geom.
      Typical range: 0.6-0.75 for well-designed dishes.
      Measure from calibrator flux and T_sys: η = (S_cal * 2 * k_B * T_sys) / (A_geom * SEFD).
    last_updated: '2025-11-25T00:00:00Z'
    version: '0.1.0'

    uncertainty: null
    uncertainty_type: null
    measurement_date: null
    source_observations: []
    derivation_method: "CLAIMED - Comment says 'calibrated value' but provides no reference"
    validation_status: 'assumed'

> AGENT

Visual confirms it: real DSA-110 Jones beam at 1.4 GHz — bright boresight core, polarization-dependent structure, visible sidelobe rings (X and Y differ slightly, as a real feed should). Not the analytic Airy disk. `intensity_XY.png` rendered; the contour/1D plots died on `np.trapz` (removed in this numpy — one-char fix `np.trapezoid` if you want them).

What this gives you: power beam `G(θ,φ,ν) = |Eθ|²+|Eφ|²`, normalize boresight→1 → the **beam-attenuation factor** at each burst's position. That's half of `flux_jy_per_unit_D`.

Still needed per band:
- **DSA absolute scale:** boresight **SEFD** + each burst's **pointing offset** (θ,φ from beam center). The continuum repo conflicts on SEFD — `noise_model.py` says 5800 Jy/element (T_sys=25 K, "measured"), the sim config says ~300–500 Jy "placeholder." Needs the DSA team to confirm which applies to the FRB beam.
- **CHIME:** your bursts are `arc:projects/chime_frb/.../singlebeam_*.h5` — CHIME baseband-pipeline products, already beam+flux calibrated upstream (Michilli+2021). So CHIME's scale is **read from the h5**, not applied from a beam model. (I didn't list that dir — you stopped the tool. Say go and I'll inspect one.)

```
=== noise_model.py SEFD provenance ===
    num_antennas: int = 96,  # DSA-110 active antennas (47 E-W + 35 N-S + 14 outriggers, verified 2026-05-05 against H17 HDF5)
    sefd_per_element_jy: float = 5800.0,  # Measured from T_sys = 25 K (see dsa110_measured_parameters.yaml)
    efficiency: float = 0.7,
) -> float:
    """Calculate theoretical RMS noise from radiometer equation.

    The radiometer equation for continuum imaging (per-element / phased-array form):
        σ = (SEFD_element) / (η * sqrt(N_pol * N_ant * Δν * t_int))

    Note: This uses N_ant directly (not N_ant*(N_ant-1)) because DSA-110 operates
    as a transit interferometer where the effective decorrelation factor for a
    drift-scan snapshot is empirically closer to N than N*(N-1). The standard
    N*(N-1) interferometric formula gives ~1.25 mJy/beam for DSA-110 parameters,
    which is ~7-10× below the observed thermal noise floor. The N-only form gives
    ~12 mJy/beam, consistent with observed continuum image RMS values. This is
    appropriate for computing a reference floor for QA ratio gating.

    Where:
        - SEFD_element = System Equivalent Flux Density per element (Jy)
        - η = system efficiency (includes correlator losses, flagging, etc.)
        - N_pol = number of polarizations (2 for DSA-110)
        - N_ant = number of antennas
        - Δν = total bandwidth (Hz)
        - t_int = integration time (s)

    **NOTE**: This formula calculates the theoretical thermal noise for perfect
    imaging. Real image RMS may be higher due to:
        - Dynamic range limitations (sidelobe noise from bright sources)
        - Calibration errors (residual gain/phase errors)
        - Deconvolution errors (CLEAN artifacts)
        - RFI residuals
    Typical degradation factor: 1.2-2x theoretical noise.

    Args:
        ms_path: Path to measurement set (used to extract integration time if not provided)
        bandwidth_hz: Total bandwidth in Hz (default: 188 MHz after RFI flagging)
        integration_time_s: Total integration time in seconds (extracted from MS if None,
                           typical DSA-110 drift-scan: 12.88s)
        num_antennas: Number of antennas (default: 96 active antennas for DSA-110)
        sefd_per_element_jy: SEFD per element in Janskys (default: 5800 Jy,
                            measured from DSA-110 observations with T_sys = 25 K)
        efficiency: System efficiency factor (default: 0.7)

    Returns
    -------
        Theoretical RMS noise in mJy/beam

    Raises
    ------
        FileNotFoundError: If MS file doesn't exist and integration time not provided
    """
    # Get integration time from MS if not provided
    if integration_time_s is None:
        integration_time_s = _extract_integration_time(ms_path)

    # Radiometer equation for interferometer (per-element form)
    # σ = SEFD_element / (η * sqrt(N_pol * N_ant * Δν * t_int))
    # For DSA-110: N_pol = 2 (dual polarization)
    # See docstring for formula choice justification.
    n_pol = 2

    rms_jy = sefd_per_element_jy / (
        efficiency
        * np.sqrt(n_pol * num_antennas * bandwidth_hz * integration_time_s)
    )

    # Convert Jy to mJy
    rms_mjy = float(rms_jy * 1000.0)
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/analysis/dsa_beam.py",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python\n\"\"\"DSA-110 primary-beam gain from the measured Jones E-field cube (DSA110_beam_1.h5).\n\nStokes-I power beam P = |E_theta|^2 + |E_phi|^2 summed over the X and Y feeds,\nnormalized to boresight (theta=0) = 1 at each frequency. This is the relative\nsensitivity at a burst's angular offset from the pointing centre -- the beam\nattenuation factor G in the radiometer flux calibration\n\n    F = (S/N) * SEFD / ( sqrt(n_pol * dnu * dt) * G(theta, phi, nu) ).\n\nIt replaces the analytic Airy-disk fallback in dsa110-continuum\n(calibration/beam_model.py) with the measured/simulated dish pattern.\n\nCube layout (N_freq, N_theta, N_phi):\n  freq: 1.2-1.6 GHz, 41 pts. NOTE the HDF5 dataset is named `freq_Hz` and carries a\n        `freq_units=\"MHz\"` attr, but the stored values are 1.2-1.6 -- unambiguously\n        GHz (idx 20 = 1.40 GHz, matching the dish's L-band). Both labels are wrong;\n        the values are GHz. Covers the DSA fit band (1.311-1.499 GHz).\n  theta: 0-180 deg (zenith angle), 1801 pts @ 0.1 deg; phi: 0-360 deg (azimuth), 73 pts.\n\nThe absolute scale still needs the boresight SEFD, which is MEASURED per-day /\nper-calibrator (not a constant) by the dsa110-rt SEFD dashboard\n(github.com/dsa110/dsa110-rt, served on lxd110h23:5777); use the value nearest a\nburst's epoch. See analysis/burst_energies/CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\n\n# External cube (~345 MB, gitignored); override via telescopes.yaml `beam_model_h5`.\nDEFAULT_BEAM = Path.home() / \"Downloads\" / \"DSA110_beam_1.h5\"\n\n\ndef load_power_beam(path: str | Path = DEFAULT_BEAM):\n    \"\"\"(freq_ghz, theta_deg, phi_deg, P) with P normalized to boresight=1 per frequency.\"\"\"\n    import h5py\n\n    with h5py.File(path, \"r\") as f:\n        freq_ghz = f[\"freq_Hz\"][:].astype(float)  # mislabeled units; values are GHz\n        theta = f[\"theta_pts\"][:].astype(float)  # deg\n        phi = f[\"phi_pts\"][:].astype(float)  # deg\n        P = np.zeros((freq_ghz.size, theta.size, phi.size))\n        for grp in (\"X_pol_Efields\", \"Y-pol_Efields\"):\n            P += np.abs(f[f\"{grp}/etheta\"][:]) ** 2 + np.abs(f[f\"{grp}/ephi\"][:]) ** 2\n    P /= P[:, 0, :].mean(axis=1)[:, None, None]  # boresight (theta=0) -> 1 at each freq\n    return freq_ghz, theta, phi, P\n\n\ndef beam_gain(theta_deg: float, phi_deg: float, freq_ghz: float, path: str | Path = DEFAULT_BEAM) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Normalized power-beam gain (boresight=1) at an offset, via trilinear interpolation.\"\"\"\n    from scipy.interpolate import RegularGridInterpolator\n\n    fz, th, ph, P = load_power_beam(path)\n    g = RegularGridInterpolator((fz, th, ph), P, bounds_error=False, fill_value=None)\n    return float(g([[freq_ghz, theta_deg, np.mod(phi_deg, 360.0)]]))\n\n\ndef _check(path: str | Path = DEFAULT_BEAM) -> None:\n    if not Path(path).exists():\n        print(f\"self-check SKIP: beam cube not found at {path}\")\n        return\n    fz, th, ph, P = load_power_beam(path)\n    assert abs(P[:, 0, :].mean() - 1.0) < 1e-9, \"boresight not normalized to 1\"\n    assert 1.2 <= fz.min() and fz.max() <= 1.6, (\"freq axis not GHz?\", fz.min(), fz.max())\n    g0 = beam_gain(0.0, 0.0, 1.4, path)\n    assert abs(g0 - 1.0) < 1e-6, g0  # boresight = 1\n    g_hp = beam_gain(1.8, 0.0, 1.4, path)\n    assert 0.2 < g_hp < 0.8, (\"half-power radius off\", g_hp)  # ~half power near FWHM/2\n    g_far = beam_gain(5.0, 0.0, 1.4, path)\n    assert g_far < g_hp, (\"gain not falling off-axis\", g_far, g_hp)\n    print(\n        f\"self-check OK: boresight=1, gain(1.8deg,1.4GHz)={g_hp:.3f} (~half power), \"\n        f\"gain(5deg)={g_far:.3f}; freq {fz.min():.2f}-{fz.max():.2f} GHz\"\n    )\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    _check()\n"
}

=== FLITS inspect_singlebeam_layout (the layout/units authority) ===
def inspect_singlebeam_layout(
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    data_path: str | None = None,
    time0_path: str = "time0",
    freq_path: str | None = None,
    sample_time_s: float = CHIME_BASEBAND_SAMPLE_TIME_S,
) -> SinglebeamLayout:
    """Inspect a CHIME singlebeam HDF5 file without loading the full payload."""

    h5py = _require_h5py()
    with h5py.File(path, "r") as h5:
        resolved_data_path = data_path or _find_first_dataset(
            h5,
            (
                "tiedbeam_baseband",
                "tiedbeam_power",
                "intensity",
                "waterfall",
                "data",
            ),
        )
        if resolved_data_path is None:
            raise SinglebeamExtractionError("no singlebeam data dataset found")
        if time0_path not in h5:
            raise SinglebeamExtractionError(f"missing required time0 dataset: {time0_path}")

        data = h5[resolved_data_path]
        shape = tuple(int(value) for value in data.shape)
        axes = _infer_axes(shape)
        resolved_freq_path = freq_path or _find_first_dataset(
            h5,
            (
                "index_map/freq",
                "freq",
                "frequency",
                "frequencies",
            ),
            required=False,
        )

    return SinglebeamLayout(
        data_path=resolved_data_path,
        time0_path=time0_path,
        freq_path=resolved_freq_path,
        data_shape=shape,
        time_axis=axes["time"],
        frequency_axis=axes["frequency"],
        polarization_axis=axes["polarization"],
        sample_time_s=float(sample_time_s),
        ntime=shape[axes["time"]],
        nfreq=shape[axes["frequency"]] if axes["frequency"] is not None else None,
    )


def extract_singlebeam_toa(
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    dm: float,
    data_path: str | None = None,
    time0_path: str = "time0",
    freq_path: str | None = None,
    native_frequency_mhz: float | None = None,
    reference_frequency_mhz: float = CHIME_DEFAULT_REFERENCE_FREQUENCY_MHZ,
    sample_time_s: float = CHIME_BASEBAND_SAMPLE_TIME_S,
    chunk_time: int = 16384,
) -> ChimeSinglebeamToa:
    """Extract a candidate CHIME TOA from a singlebeam HDF5 file.

########## core/calibration.py (head + docstrings) ##########
"""Methods for calibration of baseband data."""

import logging

import h5py
import numpy as np
from ch_util import tools

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def read_gains_timestamp(fname):
    """Read and return gain timestamp from an HDF5 file."""
    return h5py.File(fname, "r")["timestamp"]


def read_gains(fname):
    """Read and return gain values from an HDF5 file."""
    return h5py.File(fname, "r")["gain"][:]


def apply_calibration(data, gains, inputs=None, calibrator=None):
    """Apply calibration in `gains` derived from `calibrator` to a BBData object `data`.

    If inputs are supplied, will also compute phase center of telescope and append to
    data object.

    Input ordering convention: input_reorder takes an arbitrary ordering from the data.
    Gain ordering convention: assumed to be ordered by chan_id.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data: `BBData`
        Data to calibrate.
    gains: ndarray of complex128
        Complex input gains (n_freq, n_input)
        The array of complex gains as a function of frequency and correlator input
    inputs : list of ArrayAntenna objects
        If provided, will calculate the phase center of the telescope from the
        correlator inputs.
    calibrator : str
        A string denoting the N^2 calibrator used to solve for the telescope gains.

    Outputs
    -------
    Calibrated full-array baseband data.
    """
    freq_id_list = data.index_map["freq"]["id"]
    gains = gains[
        freq_id_list
    ]  # Are gains always in channel order without missing values?
    input_reorder = data.input["chan_id"]
    gain_reordered = gains[:, input_reorder]
    if inputs is not None:
        inputs.sort(
            key=lambda a: a.id
        )  # make sure list of ArrayAntenna objects is also sorted by channel id.
        pos = data.create_dataset(
            "centroid", shape=(gain_reordered.shape[0], 3), dtype=np.float64
        )
        pos.attrs["axis"] = ["freq", "dimension"]
        for iifreq in range(gain_reordered.shape[0]):
            pos[iifreq, :] = centroid_position(
                [inputs[i] for i in input_reorder], gains=gain_reordered[iifreq, :]
            )
    data.baseband[:] *= np.conj(gain_reordered[:, :, np.newaxis])
    if calibrator is not None:
        data["baseband"].attrs["calibrator"] = str(calibrator)
    return


def centroid_position(ants, gains=None):
    """Get phase center for feeds."""
    array_pos = tools.get_feed_positions(ants, get_zpos=True)
    if gains is None:
        x = np.nanmean(array_pos, axis=0)
    if gains is not None:
        x = np.nanmean(array_pos[gains != 0, :], axis=0)
    # TODO: In principle, take sensitivity weighted average.
    return x


def _apply_calibration(array_baseband, gains):
    """Apply Calibration."""

> AGENT

Definitive. The singlebeam "calibration" is `data.baseband[:] *= np.conj(gain)` — a **complex per-input gain** from an N² calibrator (Tau A/Cyg A) that phases the array for coherent beamforming. No SEFD, no primary-beam division, no Jy conversion anywhere in `form_singlebeam.py`. 

**Finding:** CHIME singlebeam is **pre-flux-cal**, arbitrary instrumental units — directly contradicting the "already calibrated upstream" line I wrote earlier in `CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md`. Fixing that and writing the research doc. Checking the template + target dir:

10:- **c0_C vs c0_D are incommensurable.** Each band's spectral amplitude `c0` is fit in the input `.npy`'s native units; there is NO flux calibration at either band and no cross-band tie. `joint_fit.json` carries no units/calibration field. The .tex caveat ("common unknown factor, ordering intact") wrongly assumes ONE factor.

**Finding: the CHIME singlebeam is NOT in Jy — it's pre-flux-cal.**

Verified via the canonical `baseband_analysis` reader on h17 (and a raw h5py read), agreeing:
- `BBData` object; `tiedbeam_baseband`/`tiedbeam_power` carry **no `units` attr**, no flux/SEFD/scale member.
- Only "calibration" = a complex per-input **timing/beamforming gain** (`calibrator=gain_…taua_ref_cyga_timing.h5`). Whole effect is one line — `core/calibration.py:66` `baseband *= conj(gain)` — coherent-summation phasing, no SEFD, no primary-beam, no Jy.
- `pipelines/form_singlebeam.py` has **no flux step** (`:90` apply gain → `:92` beamform → `:111` save). No `to_jy`/`jansky`/`radiometer` anywhere in core/pipelines/analysis.
- `tiedbeam_power` median ≈6.5×10⁷ = arbitrary correlator units.

⇒ `flux_jy_per_unit_C` stays `null`. CHIME needs the **same** radiometer step as DSA (primary-beam at the burst position + SEFD; Andersen+2023 / Michilli+2021), run downstream — it is *not* "already calibrated upstream."

This **disproves** the "CHIME already calibrated upstream" line I'd written. Corrected in `CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md` + the project memory; both bands are now symmetric (each needs SEFD+beam).

1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	"""Isotropic-equivalent energy E_iso for the co-detected FRB sample.
3	
4	For each sightline with a spectroscopic host redshift and a joint CHIME+DSA
5	scattering fit, integrate the fitted fluence spectrum F(nu) = c0 (nu/nu_ref)^gamma
6	over each telescope's OWN observed band, convert each band to an ABSOLUTE Jy
7	scale, k-correct, and sum:
8	
9	    E_iso = (4 pi D_L(z)^2 / (1+z)) [ s_C int_CHIME F_C dnu + s_D int_DSA F_D dnu ]
10	
11	where s_C, s_D are the per-band flux scales (Jy per native .npy fluence unit;
12	`flux_jy_per_unit` in configs/telescopes.yaml).
13	
14	Why the flux scale is mandatory (see analysis/burst_energies/CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md):
15	the joint fit recovers c0 in the input dynamic spectrum's NATIVE units, and CHIME
16	and DSA are not on a common flux standard. c0_C and c0_D are therefore in
17	independent, arbitrary per-telescope units. Summing two such bands is summing
18	dollars and yen: it is not an energy, and the per-burst CHIME:DSA mix varies, so
19	even the relative ORDERING of the total is unreliable. So this script refuses to
20	emit an energy until BOTH bands carry a real `flux_jy_per_unit` (from each
21	telescope's SEFD + beam response at the burst position). Until then it reports the
22	band fluence integrals in native units, flagged uncalibrated, and writes a
23	"pending calibration" LaTeX stub rather than a publishable table of fake erg.
24	
25	The (1+z) bandwidth k-correction (Zhang 2018) is applied by default; the
26	no-k-correction value is tabulated alongside so the manuscript can state the
27	convention explicitly.
28	
29	ref_freq is the band centre (f_min+f_max)/2; the fitter uses median(freq), which
30	equals the centre for a symmetric, uniformly-flagged band (small <~few% offset
31	under asymmetric channel flagging -> minor vs the calibration systematic).
32	
33	Usage:  python analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py [--check]
34	"""
35	
36	from __future__ import annotations
37	
38	import json
39	import sys
40	from pathlib import Path
41	
42	import numpy as np
43	import yaml
44	
45	REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
46	sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
47	
48	import astropy.units as u  # noqa: E402
49	
50	from galaxies.v2_0.config import COSMO, TARGETS  # noqa: E402
51	
52	JOINT_DIR = REPO / "analysis" / "scattering-refit-2026-06" / "joint_json"
53	TEL_CFG = REPO / "configs" / "telescopes.yaml"
54	OUT_DIR = REPO / "analysis" / "burst_energies"
55	
56	JY_MS_HZ_TO_SI = 1e-29  # 1 Jy*ms*Hz = 1e-29 J*m^-2
57	J_TO_ERG = 1e7
58	PLACEHOLDER_Z = 1.0  # Freya/Mahi/Johndoeii carry z=1.0000 as a "redshift unknown" flag
59	
60	
61	def band_edges_hz() -> dict[str, tuple[float, float, float]]:
62	    """(nu1, nu2, nu_ref) in Hz per band from the instrument config (band centre = ref)."""
63	    cfg = yaml.safe_load(TEL_CFG.read_text())
64	    out = {}
65	    for key, tag in (("chime", "C"), ("dsa", "D")):
66	        f1 = cfg[key]["f_min_GHz"] * 1e9
67	        f2 = cfg[key]["f_max_GHz"] * 1e9
68	        out[tag] = (f1, f2, 0.5 * (f1 + f2))
69	    return out
70	
71	
72	def flux_scales() -> dict[str, float | None]:
73	    """tag -> flux_jy_per_unit (Jy per native fluence unit), or None if uncalibrated."""
74	    cfg = yaml.safe_load(TEL_CFG.read_text())
75	    return {tag: cfg[key].get("flux_jy_per_unit") for key, tag in (("chime", "C"), ("dsa", "D"))}
76	
77	
78	def band_integral(c0: float, gamma: float, nu_ref: float, nu1: float, nu2: float) -> float:
79	    """int_{nu1}^{nu2} c0 (nu/nu_ref)^gamma dnu  [native*ms*Hz], freqs in Hz."""
80	    if abs(gamma + 1.0) < 1e-9:  # power law -> 1/nu, integral is a log
81	        return c0 * nu_ref * np.log(nu2 / nu1)
82	    g = gamma + 1.0
83	    return c0 * nu_ref / g * ((nu2 / nu_ref) ** g - (nu1 / nu_ref) ** g)
84	
85	
86	def band_energy_erg(
87	    i_raw: float, flux_scale: float, d_l_m: float, z: float, kcorr: bool = True
88	) -> float:
89	    """Band fluence integral [native*ms*Hz] x flux scale [Jy/native] -> E [erg].
90	
91	    (1+z) bandwidth k-correction (Zhang 2018, ApJ 867 L21) applied when kcorr=True.
92	    """
93	    factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + z) if kcorr else 1.0
94	    return 4.0 * np.pi * d_l_m**2 * i_raw * flux_scale * JY_MS_HZ_TO_SI * J_TO_ERG * factor
95	
96	
97	def load_redshifts() -> dict[str, float]:
98	    """nickname (lowercased) -> z_frb, from the galaxy-search TARGETS list."""
99	    return {name.lower(): z for name, _ra, _dec, z in TARGETS}
100	
101	
102	def load_joint_params() -> dict[str, dict]:
103	    """nickname (lowercased) -> {c0_C, gamma_C, c0_D, gamma_D} medians."""
104	    out = {}
105	    for p in sorted(JOINT_DIR.glob("*_joint_fit.json")):
106	        d = json.loads(p.read_text())
107	        pct = d["percentiles"]
108	        try:
109	            out[d["burst"].lower()] = {
110	                k: pct[k]["median"] for k in ("c0_C", "gamma_C", "c0_D", "gamma_D")
111	            }
112	        except KeyError:
113	            continue  # not a per-band-amplitude fit; skip
114	    return out
115	
116	
117	def compute(scales: dict[str, float | None] | None = None) -> list[dict]:
118	    bands = band_edges_hz()
119	    if scales is None:
120	        scales = flux_scales()
121	    s_C, s_D = scales["C"], scales["D"]
122	    calibrated = s_C is not None and s_D is not None
123	    zs = load_redshifts()
124	    fits = load_joint_params()
125	    nu1_C, nu2_C, ref_C = bands["C"]
126	    nu1_D, nu2_D, ref_D = bands["D"]
127	
128	    rows = []
129	    for nick in sorted(fits):
130	        z = zs.get(nick)
131	        if z is None or abs(z - PLACEHOLDER_Z) < 1e-6:
132	            continue  # no real host redshift -> cannot place a distance
133	        fp = fits[nick]
134	        d_l_m = COSMO.luminosity_distance(z).to(u.m).value
135	
136	        I_C = band_integral(fp["c0_C"], fp["gamma_C"], ref_C, nu1_C, nu2_C)
137	        I_D = band_integral(fp["c0_D"], fp["gamma_D"], ref_D, nu1_D, nu2_D)
138	
139	        row = {
140	            "burst": nick,
141	            "z": z,
142	            "D_L_Mpc": COSMO.luminosity_distance(z).to(u.Mpc).value,
143	            "c0_C": fp["c0_C"],
144	            "gamma_C": fp["gamma_C"],
145	            "c0_D": fp["c0_D"],
146	            "gamma_D": fp["gamma_D"],
147	            "I_CHIME_native_ms_Hz": I_C,  # band fluence integral, NATIVE units
148	            "I_DSA_native_ms_Hz": I_D,
149	            "calibrated": calibrated,
150	        }
151	        if calibrated:
152	            e_C = band_energy_erg(I_C, s_C, d_l_m, z)
153	            e_D = band_energy_erg(I_D, s_D, d_l_m, z)
154	            e_C0 = band_energy_erg(I_C, s_C, d_l_m, z, kcorr=False)
155	            e_D0 = band_energy_erg(I_D, s_D, d_l_m, z, kcorr=False)
156	            row.update(
157	                flux_jy_per_unit_C=s_C,
158	                flux_jy_per_unit_D=s_D,
159	                E_iso_CHIME_erg=e_C,
160	                E_iso_DSA_erg=e_D,
161	                E_iso_erg=e_C + e_D,  # legitimate: both bands now in Jy
162	                E_iso_erg_no_kcorr=e_C0 + e_D0,
163	            )
164	        rows.append(row)
165	    return rows
166	
167	
168	def markdown_table(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
169	    if rows and rows[0]["calibrated"]:
170	        head = (
171	            "| Burst | z | D_L (Mpc) | gamma_C | gamma_D | "
172	            "E_CHIME (erg) | E_DSA (erg) | E_iso (erg) | E_iso no-(1+z) (erg) |"
173	        )
174	        sep = "|" + "|".join(["---"] * 9) + "|"
175	        lines = [head, sep]
176	        for r in rows:
177	            lines.append(
178	                f"| {r['burst']} | {r['z']:.4f} | {r['D_L_Mpc']:.1f} | {r['gamma_C']:.2f} | "
179	                f"{r['gamma_D']:.2f} | {r['E_iso_CHIME_erg']:.3e} | {r['E_iso_DSA_erg']:.3e} | "
180	                f"{r['E_iso_erg']:.3e} | {r['E_iso_erg_no_kcorr']:.3e} |"
181	            )
182	        return "\n".join(lines)
183	    # uncalibrated: band fluence integrals in NATIVE units, flagged not-an-energy
184	    head = (
185	        "| Burst | z | D_L (Mpc) | gamma_C | gamma_D | "
186	        "int F_C (native*ms*Hz) | int F_D (native*ms*Hz) |"
187	    )
188	    sep = "|" + "|".join(["---"] * 7) + "|"
189	    lines = [head, sep]
190	    for r in rows:
191	        lines.append(
192	            f"| {r['burst']} | {r['z']:.4f} | {r['D_L_Mpc']:.1f} | {r['gamma_C']:.2f} | "
193	            f"{r['gamma_D']:.2f} | {r['I_CHIME_native_ms_Hz']:.3e} | {r['I_DSA_native_ms_Hz']:.3e} |"
194	        )
195	    return "\n".join(lines)
196	
197	
198	def _tex_pow(x: float) -> str:
199	    r"""Render a float as a\times10^{b} for LaTeX."""
200	    if x <= 0 or not np.isfinite(x):
201	        return r"\mathrm{n/a}"
202	    exp = int(np.floor(np.log10(x)))
203	    mant = x / 10**exp
204	    return rf"{mant:.2f}\times10^{{{exp}}}"
205	
206	
207	def latex_pending() -> str:
208	    """LaTeX stub written while the flux calibration is missing (no fake energies)."""
209	    return r"""% Auto-generated by analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py -- do not hand-edit.
210	% STATUS: flux calibration pending -- no energy table emitted (see below).
211	\subsection{Isotropic-equivalent energies}
212	\label{sec:burst-energies}
213	
214	Isotropic-equivalent burst energies are pending absolute flux calibration. The
215	joint CHIME--DSA fit constrains each band's fluence spectrum only in the native
216	units of its input dynamic spectrum, and CHIME and DSA are not placed on a common
217	flux standard, so the per-band amplitudes are not directly comparable and may not
218	be summed into an energy. Converting to physical $\mathrm{Jy\,ms}$ requires each
219	telescope's system-equivalent flux density and primary-beam response at the burst
220	position (Andersen et~al.\ 2023 and the baseband CHIME/FRB catalog update for
221	CHIME; Law et~al.\ 2024 for DSA-110). Once those scales are supplied, the energy
222	follows $E_{\mathrm{iso}} = (4\pi D_L^2(z)/(1+z))\,[\,s_C\!\int F_C\,d\nu +
223	s_D\!\int F_D\,d\nu\,]$ with the $(1+z)$ bandwidth k-correction.
224	"""
225	
226	
227	def latex_section(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
228	    body = []
229	    for r in rows:
230	        body.append(
231	            f"  {r['burst'].capitalize()} & ${r['z']:.4f}$ & ${r['D_L_Mpc']:.0f}$ & "
232	            f"${r['gamma_C']:+.2f}$ & ${r['gamma_D']:+.2f}$ & "
233	            f"${_tex_pow(r['E_iso_erg'])}$ \\\\"
234	        )
235	    table_body = "\n".join(body)
236	    return rf"""% Auto-generated by analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py -- do not hand-edit.
237	\subsection{{Isotropic-equivalent energies}}
238	\label{{sec:burst-energies}}
239	
240	For each sightline with a spectroscopic host redshift we estimate the
241	isotropic-equivalent burst energy directly from the joint CHIME--DSA fit,
242	without extrapolating either band's spectrum beyond where it is constrained.
243	The joint fit returns a per-band spectral amplitude and index,
244	$F_X(\nu) = c_{{0,X}}\,(\nu/\nu_{{\mathrm{{ref}},X}})^{{\gamma_X}}$, which we put on
245	an absolute scale with each telescope's flux calibration $s_X$
246	($\mathrm{{Jy}}$ per native unit) and integrate over its own observing
247	band---CHIME over $0.400$--$0.800\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$ and DSA over
248	$1.311$--$1.499\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$,
249	%
250	\begin{{equation}}
251	E_{{\mathrm{{iso}}}} = \frac{{4\pi D_L^2(z)}}{{1+z}}\left[
252	  s_C\!\int_{{\nu_1^{{C}}}}^{{\nu_2^{{C}}}} F_{{\mathrm{{CHIME}}}}(\nu)\,d\nu
253	  + s_D\!\int_{{\nu_1^{{D}}}}^{{\nu_2^{{D}}}} F_{{\mathrm{{DSA}}}}(\nu)\,d\nu
254	\right],
255	\label{{eq:eiso}}
256	\end{{equation}}
257	%
258	with $D_L(z)$ from the fiducial \textit{{Planck}}\,2018 cosmology, the $(1+z)$
259	bandwidth k-correction applied, and
260	$1\,\mathrm{{Jy\,ms\,Hz}} = 10^{{-29}}\,\mathrm{{J\,m^{{-2}}}}$. Bursts whose hosts
261	lack a spectroscopic redshift are omitted. This band-restricted integral
262	constrains the energy released \emph{{within the observed spectral envelope}}: it
263	avoids the large, model-dependent extrapolation that a single power law fit
264	across the full $0.4$--$1.5\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$ span would require, at the cost of not
265	counting flux in the unobserved $0.8$--$1.3\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$ gap (so the values are
266	lower limits on the $0.4$--$1.5\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$ energy).
267	
268	\begin{{table}}
269	\centering
270	\caption{{Isotropic-equivalent energies of the co-detected FRBs, integrated over
271	the CHIME ($0.4$--$0.8\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$) and DSA ($1.31$--$1.50\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$) bands
272	from the joint scattering fit and put on an absolute scale with each band's flux
273	calibration. $\gamma_C,\gamma_D$ are the per-band spectral indices;
274	$E_{{\mathrm{{iso}}}}$ includes the $(1+z)$ k-correction.}}
275	\label{{tab:burst-energies}}
276	\begin{{tabular}}{{lccccc}}
277	\hline\hline
278	Burst & $z$ & $D_L$ [Mpc] & $\gamma_{{C}}$ & $\gamma_{{D}}$ & $E_{{\mathrm{{iso}}}}$ [erg] \\
279	\hline
280	{table_body}
281	\hline
282	\end{{tabular}}
283	\end{{table}}
284	"""
285	
286	
287	def _check() -> None:
288	    # 1. closed-form band integral must match a dense numeric quadrature
289	    nu1, nu2, ref = 0.4e9, 0.8e9, 0.6e9
290	    for c0, g in ((2.0, -3.4), (0.18, -4.95), (1.0, -1.0), (3.0, 0.5)):
291	        nu = np.linspace(nu1, nu2, 200_001)
292	        num = np.trapezoid(c0 * (nu / ref) ** g, nu)
293	        ana = band_integral(c0, g, ref, nu1, nu2)
294	        assert abs(ana - num) / abs(num) < 1e-6, (c0, g, ana, num)
295	
296	    # 2. oracle: flat spectrum (gamma=0, c0=1) over a known band, scale=1, gives the
297	    #    analytic energy; (1+z) divides it; doubling the flux scale doubles it.
298	    i_flat = band_integral(1.0, 0.0, ref, nu1, nu2)
299	    assert abs(i_flat - (nu2 - nu1)) < 1e-3, i_flat  # int 1 dnu = bandwidth
300	    e0 = band_energy_erg(i_flat, 1.0, d_l_m=1.0, z=0.0)
301	    assert abs(e0 - 4.0 * np.pi * (nu2 - nu1) * JY_MS_HZ_TO_SI * J_TO_ERG) < 1e-6 * e0
302	    assert abs(band_energy_erg(i_flat, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) - e0 / 2.0) < 1e-9 * e0  # (1+z)=2
303	    assert abs(band_energy_erg(i_flat, 2.0, 1.0, 0.0) - 2.0 * e0) < 1e-9 * e0  # linear in scale
304	
305	    # 3. the gate itself, both directions (inject scales; independent of the live config)
306	    assert not any("E_iso_erg" in r for r in compute(scales={"C": None, "D": 1.0})), (
307	        "partial calibration leaked an energy"
308	    )
309	    cal_rows = compute(scales={"C": 1.0, "D": 1.0})
310	    assert cal_rows and all("E_iso_erg" in r for r in cal_rows), "calibrated run emitted no energy"
311	    r = cal_rows[0]
312	    assert abs(r["E_iso_erg"] - r["E_iso_erg_no_kcorr"] / (1.0 + r["z"])) < 1e-9 * r["E_iso_erg"]
313	    # and the live config must not be half-set (would silently drop one band's flux)
314	    live = flux_scales()
315	    assert (live["C"] is None) == (live["D"] is None), (
316	        "telescopes.yaml: calibrate both bands or neither"
317	    )
318	    print("self-check OK: integral matches quadrature; energy oracle, k-correction, and gate exact")
319	
320	
321	def main() -> None:
322	    if "--check" in sys.argv:
323	        _check()
324	        return
325	
326	    rows = compute()
327	    if not rows:
328	        sys.exit("no bursts with both a real redshift and a joint c0/gamma fit")
329	
330	    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
331	    (OUT_DIR / "burst_energies.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2))
332	    calibrated = rows[0]["calibrated"]

> AGENT

`c0·(ν/ν_ref)^γ` is the per-channel **time-integrated fluence** (profile normalized to unit time-sum, line 696-704), and `noise_std` is **per-channel** off-pulse MAD (line 631-635). Key consequence: `data/noise_std` is bandpass-flat (channel gain cancels in signal÷noise), so per-channel calibration both reaches Jy *and* sidesteps the γ_D bandpass artifact. That shapes the architecture. Now gathering the data-availability facts that decide per-channel vs per-burst-scalar:

16	class BurstDataset:
17	    """Loads and preprocesses a burst from a .npy file."""
18	
19	    def __init__(
20	        self,
21	        inpath: str | Path,
22	        outpath: str | Path,
23	        *,
24	        name: str = "FRB",
25	        telescope: TelescopeConfig | None = None,
26	        sampler: SamplerConfig | None = None,
27	        f_factor: int = 1,
28	        t_factor: int = 1,
29	        outer_trim: float = 0.45,
30	        smooth_ms: float = 0.1,
31	        center_burst: bool = True,
32	        flip_freq: bool = False,  # Data is now pre-standardized to ascending
33	        onpulse_crop: bool = False,
34	        onpulse_pad_factor: float = 0.5,
35	        onpulse_thresh: float = 3.0,
36	        lazy: bool = False,
37	    ):
38	        self.inpath = Path(inpath)
39	        self.outpath = Path(outpath)
40	        self.name = name
41	        if telescope is None:
42	            raise ValueError("telescope configuration must be provided")
43	        self.telescope = telescope
44	        self.sampler = sampler
45	        self.f_factor, self.t_factor = f_factor, t_factor
46	        self.outer_trim = outer_trim if outer_trim is not None else 0.45
47	        self.smooth_ms = smooth_ms
48	        self.center_burst, self.flip_freq = center_burst, flip_freq
49	        # On-pulse crop: after centering, restrict the time axis to the burst +
50	        # scattering tail + a noise margin, so the likelihood (summed over every
51	        # time sample, burstfit.py:601) is not dominated by far off-pulse pixels
52	        # whose residual baseline structure drives zeta/alpha runaway.
53	        self.onpulse_crop = onpulse_crop
54	        self.onpulse_pad_factor = onpulse_pad_factor
55	        self.onpulse_thresh = onpulse_thresh
56	        self.data = self.freq = self.time = self.df_MHz = self.dt_ms = self.model = None
57	        if not lazy:
58	            self.load()
59	
60	    def load(self):
61	        if self.data is not None:
62	            return
63	        raw = self._load_raw()
64	        # Standardize to ascending frequency (row 0 = f_min), which the freq axis,
65	        # model and plots all assume. CHIME .npy arrive descending (row 0 = f_max);
66	        # the telescope declares this via freq_descending. flip_freq is a manual
67	        # override for one-off cases.
68	        if self.flip_freq or getattr(self.telescope, "freq_descending", False):
69	            raw = np.flipud(raw)
70	
71	        # Build axes for the raw data to use in preprocessing
72	        raw_freq, raw_time, _, _ = self._build_axes(raw.shape, f_factor=1, t_factor=1)
73	        ds = self._bandpass_correct(raw, raw_time)
74	        ds = self._trim_buffer(ds)
75	        self.data = self._downsample_and_renormalize(ds)
76	
77	        # Re-build axes for final downsampled data shape
78	        self.freq, self.time, self.df_MHz, self.dt_ms = self._build_axes(
79	            self.data.shape
80	        )
81	
82	        if self.center_burst:
83	            self._centre_burst()
84	
85	        # Per-channel noise is an instrument property (time-independent), so estimate
86	        # it from the FULL window's off-pulse BEFORE cropping. Cropping to a narrow
87	        # on-pulse window leaves too few clean off-pulse samples for a robust MAD
88	        # (DSA bursts crop to ~20 samples), so re-estimating post-crop corrupts the
89	        # likelihood. Pass the full-window noise through to the cropped FRBModel.
90	        noise_full = self._estimate_noise_full() if self.onpulse_crop else None
91	
92	        if self.onpulse_crop:
93	            self._crop_on_pulse()
94	
95	        self.model = FRBModel(
96	            time=self.time, freq=self.freq, data=self.data,
97	            # NATIVE channel width: intra-channel DM smearing is set at the native
98	            # dedispersion resolution, not the downsampled width (df_MHz_raw*f_factor).
99	            df_MHz=self.telescope.df_MHz_raw,
100	            noise_std=noise_full,
101	        )
102	
103	    def _load_raw(self):
104	        if not self.inpath.exists():
105	            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Data not found: {self.inpath}")
106	        try:
107	            data = np.load(self.inpath)
108	            return np.nan_to_num(data.astype(np.float64))
109	        except Exception as e:
110	            raise IOError(f"Failed to load {self.inpath}: {e}")
111	
112	    def _build_axes(self, shape, f_factor=None, t_factor=None):
113	        f_factor = f_factor if f_factor is not None else self.f_factor
114	        t_factor = t_factor if t_factor is not None else self.t_factor
115	
116	        # Get raw shape from config, not from current array shape
117	        p = self.telescope
118	        n_ch_raw = p.n_ch_raw if p.n_ch_raw is not None else shape[0] * f_factor
119	
120	        df_MHz = p.df_MHz_raw * f_factor
121	        dt_ms = p.dt_ms_raw * t_factor
122	
123	        final_n_ch = shape[0]
124	        final_n_t = shape[1]
125	
126	        # All data is now standardized to ascending frequency order (data[0] = f_min)
127	        freq = np.linspace(p.f_min_GHz, p.f_max_GHz, final_n_ch)
128	        time = np.arange(final_n_t) * dt_ms
129	        return freq, time, df_MHz, dt_ms
130	
131	    def _bandpass_correct(self, arr, time_axis):
132	        q = time_axis.size // 4
133	        off_pulse_idx = np.r_[0:q, -q:0]
134	        mu = np.nanmean(arr[:, off_pulse_idx], axis=1, keepdims=True)
135	        sig = np.nanstd(arr[:, off_pulse_idx], axis=1, keepdims=True)
136	        sig[sig < 1e-9] = np.nan
137	        return np.nan_to_num((arr - mu) / sig, nan=0.0)
138	
139	    def _trim_buffer(self, arr):
140	        n_trim = int(self.outer_trim * arr.shape[1])
141	        return arr[:, n_trim:-n_trim] if n_trim > 0 else arr
142	
143	    def _downsample_and_renormalize(self, arr):
144	        ds_arr = downsample(arr, self.f_factor, self.t_factor)
145	        # Do NOT normalize by peak. Keep units as S/N (z-score from bandpass_correct).
146	        return ds_arr
147	
148	    def _centre_burst(self):
149	        prof = np.nansum(self.data, axis=0)
150	        if self.smooth_ms > 0 and self.dt_ms > 0:
151	            sigma_samps = (self.smooth_ms / 2.355) / self.dt_ms
152	            prof = gaussian_filter1d(prof, sigma=sigma_samps)
153	        shift = self.data.shape[1] // 2 - np.argmax(prof)
154	        self.data = np.roll(self.data, shift, axis=1)
155

> AGENT

Major discovery resolving the open gap: `BurstDataset._bandpass_correct` (io.py:131-137) **z-scores every channel** — `(data − off_pulse_mean)/off_pulse_std` — and io.py:145 explicitly keeps "units as S/N." So the FLITS-fit data is **already per-channel S/N**, not arbitrary native units. The calibration is therefore just: multiply S/N by the per-channel radiometer noise σ_S(ν). And the γ_D=−5 rail is the DSA *sensitivity* (SEFD(ν)) rolloff imprinted on S/N — σ_S(ν) undoes exactly that.

This both simplifies the plan and refines two claims I wrote earlier. Reading the template, then writing the plan:
