  "content": "# Implementation Plan: Radiometer flux calibration (S/N → Jy) for FLITS burst energetics\n\n---\n**Date:** 2026-06-22\n**Author:** AI Assistant\n**Status:** Draft\n**Related Documents:**\n- [Research: CHIME singlebeam flux units](research-chime-singlebeam-flux-units.md)\n- [Calibration review](../../../analysis/burst_energies/CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md)\n**Codebase state:** FLITS at `df23cce`.\n\n---\n\n## Overview\n\nThe E_iso table in `analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py` is gated closed because neither\nband carries an absolute flux scale. This plan implements the radiometer step that converts\nFLITS dynamic-spectrum amplitudes to physical Jy, per channel, so the gate can open.\n\nThe enabling discovery (this session): `BurstDataset._bandpass_correct`\n(`scattering/scat_analysis/pipeline/io.py:131-137`) **z-scores every channel** —\n`(data − off_pulse_mean)/off_pulse_std` — and `io.py:145` keeps \"units as S/N.\" So the data\nthe fitter sees is **already per-channel signal-to-noise**, with the arbitrary instrumental\ngain divided out. The only thing standing between FLITS and Jy is the per-channel radiometer\nnoise σ_S(ν): `S_ν(ν,t) [Jy] = (S/N)(ν,t) · σ_S(ν)`, with\n`σ_S(ν) = SEFD(ν) / (√(n_pol·Δν·Δt)·G(θ,φ,ν))`.\n\nBecause the z-score divides out the bandpass gain, what remains in the S/N spectrum is the\n**sensitivity** shape `1/SEFD(ν)` — which is exactly what σ_S(ν) undoes. So per-channel\ncalibration is also the principled fix for the `γ_D ≈ −5` rail flagged in the calibration\nreview (it is the DSA sensitivity rolloff imprinted on S/N, not astrophysics).\n\n**Goal:** A real, per-channel-calibrated DSA-band fluence in Jy·ms for every co-detected burst\nwith local data, feeding a `flux_jy`-calibrated band integral into the energetics script; then\nthe same machinery for CHIME, opening the E_iso gate for a publishable table with the (1+z)\nk-correction and propagated uncertainties.\n\n**Motivation:** Without this, the burst-energy table cannot be published (it is gated to a\n\"calibration pending\" LaTeX stub). The radiometer step is standard radio practice (Andersen+2023\nfor CHIME; Law+2024 for DSA) and is now a single per-channel multiply on data we already have in\nS/N units.\n\n## Current State Analysis\n\n**Existing Implementation:**\n- `scattering/scat_analysis/pipeline/io.py:131-137` — `_bandpass_correct` z-scores each channel\n  by its own off-pulse mean/std; `io.py:143-146` downsamples without renormalizing, keeping\n  \"units as S/N.\" This is the load path every fit uses (`io.py:60-101`).\n- `scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit.py:656-704` — the forward model: `amp = c0·(ν/ν_ref)^γ`\n  with `ref_freq = median(freq)`, multiplying a **time-sum-normalized** profile\n  (`gauss/Σgauss`, `burstfit.py:696-704`), so `amp` is the per-channel **time-integrated S/N**.\n- `scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit.py:619-635` — `_estimate_noise`: per-channel `1.4826·MAD`\n  off-pulse noise (shape `n_freq`).\n- `analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py:78-94` — `band_integral` integrates `c0·(ν/ν_ref)^γ` over\n  the band; `band_energy_erg` multiplies by a **single scalar** `flux_scale` to reach erg.\n- `analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py:117-165` — `compute()` gates on both bands having a\n  non-null `flux_jy_per_unit`; emits energies only when calibrated.\n- `analysis/dsa_beam.py:52-60` — `beam_gain(θ,φ,ν)` from the measured DSA Jones cube,\n  boresight=1 (already wired).\n- `configs/bursts.yaml` (symlink target `configs/bursts.yaml`) — per burst: `mjd`, `utc`,\n  `ra_deg`, `dec_deg`, `chime_id` (epoch + position for SEFD/beam lookup).\n- `scattering/configs/telescopes.yaml:16-31` — `df_MHz_raw`, `dt_ms_raw`, band edges,\n  `flux_jy_per_unit: null`, `beam_model_h5: null` per band.\n\n**Current Behavior:** `python analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py` reports band fluence integrals\nin native units and writes the \"pending calibration\" LaTeX stub; no energy is emitted.\n\n**Current Limitations:**\n- `flux_jy_per_unit` is modeled as one scalar per band in config, but the true scale is\n  **per-burst per-channel** (depends on that burst's epoch SEFD, sky-position beam gain, and the\n  per-channel noise). The config seam cannot express it.\n- The energetics integral uses the smooth fitted `c0/γ`, which (for DSA) is the\n  sensitivity-weighted S/N spectrum — its `γ_D` is railed and not the sky spectrum.\n- No SEFD, beam-position, or radiometer code exists in the energetics path.\n\n## Desired End State\n\n**New Behavior:** A new `analysis/flux_cal.py` computes, per burst per band, the calibrated band\nfluence integral in Jy·ms·Hz by multiplying the per-channel S/N (`data/noise_std`, summed over the\non-pulse) by σ_S(ν). `calculate_burst_energies.py` consumes that integral directly (flux scale\nalready folded in), keeps its both-bands gate, and — once both bands are calibrated — emits the\nE_iso table with the (1+z) k-correction and posterior-propagated error bars.\n\n**Success Looks Like:**\n- `pytest tests/test_flux_cal.py` passes: σ_S and the calibrated band integral match analytic\n  oracles to <1e-6 relative.\n- `python analysis/flux_cal.py --check` prints `self-check OK`.\n- Running the energetics script with DSA calibrated and CHIME still null keeps the E_iso gate\n  closed but reports a **real DSA-band fluence in Jy·ms** per burst (not native units).\n- A committed `analysis/burst_energies/dsa_sefd.csv` carries the per-epoch DSA SEFD for the 12\n  bursts, sourced from dsa110-rt, with provenance.\n- A bandpass diagnostic figure shows the calibrated DSA spectrum vs the fitted `γ_D` power law,\n  answering whether `γ_D` relaxes under calibration.\n- After the CHIME epic: `python analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py` emits\n  `burst_energies.tex` as an **energy table** (not the pending stub), energies in the\n  10^38–10^41 erg FRB range, each with an error bar.\n\n## What We're NOT Doing\n\n- [ ] Re-running the scattering fits. τ/α/zeta science is unchanged; this only adds an amplitude\n      calibration on top of existing fits.\n- [ ] Absolute polarimetric or Stokes calibration — Stokes I fluence only.\n- [ ] A new flux standard or cross-telescope tie beyond each band's own SEFD+beam (the bands stay\n      independently calibrated, then summed only after both are in Jy).\n- [ ] Modeling the SEFD frequency *shape* within a band as more than the dsa110-rt epoch value (a\n      band-representative SEFD is used for the energy; the residual SEFD(ν) shape is treated as a\n      documented systematic and probed by the diagnostic, not fit).\n- [ ] Filling the 0.8–1.3 GHz inter-band gap — energies stay band-restricted lower limits, as the\n      existing LaTeX already states (`calculate_burst_energies.py:261-266`).\n\n**Rationale:** Keep the diff minimal and the science claims defensible; the energy is an\norder-of-magnitude quantity with an explicit uncertainty budget, per the calibration review.\n\n## Implementation Approach\n\n**Technical Strategy:** Add one small pure-physics module (`analysis/flux_cal.py`) with the\nradiometer kernel and the per-channel band-fluence integral, both backed by analytic self-checks.\nResolve per-burst inputs (epoch, position, SEFD, beam gain) from existing sources\n(`bursts.yaml`, `dsa110-rt`, `dsa_beam.py`). Wire the calibrated integral into\n`calculate_burst_energies.py` behind the existing gate so partial calibration never leaks an\nenergy. DSA first (beam wired, SEFD queryable); CHIME second (beam model + SEFD sourced in its\nown epic). The bands remain independent until both are in Jy.\n\n**Key Architectural Decisions:**\n1. **Decision:** Calibrate the per-channel S/N data, not the fitted `c0/γ` spectrum.\n   - **Rationale:** The data is already S/N; multiplying by σ_S(ν) recovers Jy and removes the\n     sensitivity weighting that rails `γ_D`. Using the fitted smooth power law would bake the rail\n     into the energy.\n   - **Trade-offs:** Requires reloading each burst's `.npy` (external data on iacobus/h23) instead\n     of reusing the small `joint_fit.json`.\n   - **Alternatives considered:** Per-burst scalar on the fitted spectrum (rejected by the user;\n     propagates the bandpass artifact and is band-flat).\n2. **Decision:** The calibrated band integral is returned already in Jy·ms·Hz; the energetics\n   script calls `band_energy_erg(I_jy, flux_scale=1.0, …)`.\n   - **Rationale:** Reuses the existing, oracle-tested energy formula and (1+z) k-correction\n     unchanged; the per-channel scale lives entirely in `flux_cal.py`.\n   - **Trade-offs:** `compute()` branches between the native (uncalibrated) and Jy (calibrated)\n     integral source.\n   - **Alternatives considered:** Folding σ_S into a per-band scalar `flux_jy_per_unit` in config —\n     cannot express per-channel/per-burst variation.\n3. **Decision:** Beam gain `G` uses `dsa_beam.py` at the burst's offset from the DSA pointing\n   centre; if per-burst pointing is unavailable, `G=1` (boresight) with an explicit ≤2× (≤0.30 dex)\n   systematic recorded.\n   - **Rationale:** Co-detections sit inside the primary beam; boresight is the right limit and the\n     half-power radius bounds the error. Not an open question — a defined fallback.\n   - **Trade-offs:** Energy uncertainty widens by ≤0.30 dex for bursts lacking pointing metadata.\n   - **Alternatives considered:** Blocking on DSA observing logs (defeats DSA-first).\n\n**Patterns to Follow:**\n- Pure function + `assert`-based `_check()`/`--check`, as in `analysis/dsa_beam.py:63-83` and\n  `analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py:287-318`.\n- Injectable inputs for testing, as `compute(scales=…)` in\n  `analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py:117`.\n\n## Implementation Phases\n\nEach phase is test-first: failing test → run (watch fail) → minimal code → run (watch pass) →\ncommit. Tests run in the `flits` conda env (agent-safe:\n`env -i HOME=\"$HOME\" PATH=\"/opt/anaconda3/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin\" /opt/anaconda3/bin/conda run -n flits pytest …`).\n\n### Phase 1: Radiometer kernel (`analysis/flux_cal.py`)\n\n**Objective:** Pure σ_S and calibrated-band-integral functions, validated against analytic cases.\nNo external data.\n\n**Tasks:**\n- [ ] **Write the failing test** — `tests/test_flux_cal.py` (new):\n\n  ```python\n  import numpy as np\n  from analysis.flux_cal import radiometer_sigma_jy, calibrated_band_integral_jy_ms_hz\n\n  def test_sigma_jy_analytic():\n      # SEFD=2000 Jy, n_pol=2, dnu=1e6 Hz, dt=1e-3 s, G=1 -> 2000/sqrt(2*1e6*1e-3)\n      s = radiometer_sigma_jy(2000.0, n_pol=2, dnu_hz=1e6, dt_s=1e-3, g=1.0)\n      assert abs(s - 2000.0 / np.sqrt(2000.0)) < 1e-9\n      # beam attenuation G=0.5 doubles the noise\n      assert abs(radiometer_sigma_jy(2000.0, 2, 1e6, 1e-3, 0.5) - 2.0 * s) < 1e-9\n\n  def test_band_integral_flat_oracle():\n      # flat S/N integral A per channel, flat sigma_S=s0, band [nu1,nu2]:\n      # integral = A*s0*dt_ms*(nu2-nu1)\n      nf = 64\n      freq_hz = np.linspace(1.311e9, 1.499e9, nf)\n      sn_integrated = np.full(nf, 3.0)            # per-channel sum_onpulse(S/N)\n      sigma_jy = np.full(nf, 5.0)                 # per-channel sigma_S [Jy]\n      dt_ms = 0.131072\n      I = calibrated_band_integral_jy_ms_hz(sn_integrated, sigma_jy, freq_hz, dt_ms)\n      oracle = 3.0 * 5.0 * dt_ms * (freq_hz[-1] - SEFD = 2 k_B T_sys / A_eff; G = beam gain (boresight=1).\"\"\"\n      return sefd_jy / (np.sqrt(n_pol * dnu_hz * dt_s) * g)\n\n  def calibrated_band_integral_jy_ms_hz(sn_integrated, sigma_jy, freq_hz, dt_ms):\n      \"\"\"int_band [ sigma_S(nu) * dt_ms * sum_onpulse(S/N)(nu) ] dnu   [Jy*ms*Hz].\n\n      sn_integrated: per-channel sum over the on-pulse window of (data/noise_std)  [dimensionless]\n      sigma_jy:      per-channel sigma_S [Jy]; freq_hz ascending; dt_ms sample width [ms].\n      \"\"\"\n      chan_fluence_jy_ms = sigma_jy * dt_ms * sn_integrated     # [Jy*ms] per channel\n      return float(np.trapezoid(chan_fluence_jy_ms, freq_hz))   # [Jy*ms*Hz]\n  ```\n\n- [ ] **Run it, watch it pass:** `pytest tests/test_flux_cal.py -v` → PASS.\n- [ ] **Add `--check`** mirroring the tests (assert oracles), `print(\"self-check OK\")`; run\n      `python analysis/flux_cal.py --check`.\n- [ ] **Commit:** `git commit -m \"feat(flux): radiometer kernel (S/N->Jy) with analytic oracles\" -- analysis/flux_cal.py tests/test_flux_cal.py`\n\n**Dependencies:** none.\n\n**Verification:**\n- [ ] `pytest tests/test_flux_cal.py -v` → 2 passed.\n- [ ] `python analysis/flux_cal.py --check` → `self-check OK`.\n\n### Phase 2: Per-burst S/N spectrum from the `.npy` (data-driven)\n\n**Objective:** Given a burst nickname + band, load its dynamic spectrum via `BurstDataset`, and\nreturn `(freq_hz, sn_integrated, dt_ms, dnu_hz)` — the per-channel on-pulse S/N integral.\n\n**Tasks:**\n- [ ] **Write the failing test** — `tests/test_flux_cal.py::test_sn_spectrum_synthetic` using a\n      synthetic `.npy` (no external data): a `(64, 512)` array, unit-noise + a Gaussian pulse in\n      the centre on every channel; assert `sn_integrated` is positive on every channel and the\n      integrated S/N at the known pulse channels exceeds the off-pulse baseline by the injected\n      amplitude within 10%.\n\n  ```python\n  def test_sn_spectrum_synthetic(tmp_path):\n      from analysis.flux_cal import sn_spectrum_from_npy\n      rng = np.random.default_rng(0)\n      nf, nt = 64, 512\n      t = np.arange(nt); prof = np.exp(-0.5*((t-nt//2)/4.0)**2)\n      data = rng.standard_normal((nf, nt)) + 8.0 * prof[None, :]   # Confirmed: the pointing Dec isn't in the repo, but your mechanism is right and the data exists externally — `codetections_manifest.yaml:75` points to `h23:/media/ubuntu/ssd/jfaber/chime_dsa_codetections/localizations`, and `bursts.yaml` already holds the voltage localizations (`ra_deg`/`dec_deg`, sub-arcsec). So it's a real computation, not a fallback. The geometry for a transit array:

- Primary-beam boresight sits at (RA = LST, Dec = pointing_dec); a burst is detected at transit, so HA ≈ 0 → **θ ≈ |Dec_src − Dec_pointing|**, φ along the meridian. With same-RA source and boresight, the astropy separation *is* exactly the Dec difference.
- Your examples cluster at Dec 70–74°, so if the survey pointing Dec is ~71–73° the offsets are ~1–3° — right where the beam falls to ~half power (dsa_beam FWHM≈3.6°). So G genuinely varies and is worth computing, not assuming G=1.

One caveat: the HA offset is only ≈0 if the burst arrived near the source's meridian transit; the primary beam spans ±~6 min in HA, so there's a small E-W term. Dec dominates; I'll treat HA as a documented small correction (addable from burst UTC vs transit time).

Updating Phase 3 to make this the primary path:

**Approach** (both your approved decisions): per-channel data-driven, DSA-first. Core simplification found while planning — FLITS data is *already* per-channel S/N (`io.py` z-score), so calibration is one multiply `S/N × σ_S(ν)`, `σ_S = SEFD/(√(n_pol·Δν·Δt)·G)`. Same multiply also undoes the sensitivity weighting that rails `γ_D`.

**7 phases:**
1. Radiometer kernel (`analysis/flux_cal.py`) — pure, analytic oracles ✓ (verified: σ_S=√2000, band-integral rel-err<1e-9)
2. Per-channel on-pulse S/N from `.npy` via `BurstDataset`
3. Per-burst σ_S inputs — **θ=|Dec_src−Dec_pointing|** (your transit geometry), G from `dsa_beam.py`
4. Acquire DSA SEFD + pointing Dec from h23 → committed CSVs
5. Wire DSA into energetics (gate stays closed, CHIME null) + γ_D bandpass diagnostic
6. CHIME epic — source primary beam + SEFD, `chime_beam.py`
7. Open the E_iso gate — combined table, (1+z) k-corr, error bars, literature cross-check

**Criteria:** 6 automated (pytest/oracles/ruff/file-exists), 3 manual (bandpass diagnostic, SEFD sanity, energy range + 1 literature cross-check), 3 reproducibility. No open questions.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/analysis/flux_cal.py",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python\n\"\"\"Radiometer flux calibration: per-channel S/N -> Jy for FLITS dynamic spectra.\n\nFLITS data is per-channel z-scored S/N (scattering/scat_analysis/pipeline/io.py:131-146:\n_bandpass_correct divides each channel by its own off-pulse mean/std and the loader keeps\n\"units as S/N\"). Physical flux density is therefore one radiometer multiply away:\n\n    S_nu(nu,t) [Jy] = (S/N)(nu,t) * sigma_S(nu),\n    sigma_S(nu) = SEFD(nu) / (sqrt(n_pol * dnu * dt) * G(theta,phi,nu)),\n\nwith SEFD = 2 k_B T_sys / A_eff and G the beam gain (boresight=1). Dividing by the\nper-channel off-pulse noise also cancels the bandpass gain, so the S/N spectrum (and hence\nthis calibration) is free of the band-edge rolloff that rails the fitted gamma_D.\n\nThe band fluence integral (Jy*ms*Hz) returned here feeds\nanalysis/calculate_burst_energies.band_energy_erg with flux_scale=1 -- the per-channel scale\nis already folded in. See docs/rse/specs/plan-radiometer-flux-cal.md.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\n\n\ndef radiometer_sigma_jy(sefd_jy, n_pol, dnu_hz, dt_s, g):\n    \"\"\"Per-sample radiometer noise [Jy]: SEFD / (sqrt(n_pol*dnu*dt) * G).\n\n    sefd_jy: system-equivalent flux density [Jy]; n_pol: summed polarisations;\n    dnu_hz: channel bandwidth [Hz]; dt_s: sample time [s]; g: beam gain (boresight=1).\n    \"\"\"\n    return sefd_jy / (np.sqrt(n_pol * dnu_hz * dt_s) * g)\n\n\ndef calibrated_band_integral_jy_ms_hz(sn_integrated, sigma_jy, freq_hz, dt_ms):\n    \"\"\"int_band [ sigma_S(nu) * dt_ms * sum_onpulse(S/N)(nu) ] dnu   [Jy*ms*Hz].\n\n    sn_integrated: per-channel sum over the on-pulse window of (data/noise_std) [dimensionless];\n    sigma_jy: per-channel sigma_S [Jy]; freq_hz: ascending channel centres [Hz]; dt_ms: sample [ms].\n    \"\"\"\n    chan_fluence_jy_ms = sigma_jy * dt_ms * sn_integrated  # [Jy*ms] per channel\n    return float(np.trapezoid(chan_fluence_jy_ms, freq_hz))  # [Jy*ms*Hz]\n\n\ndef _check() -> None:\n    # 1. radiometer noise vs analytic: 2000/sqrt(2*1e6*1e-3) == sqrt(2000); G=0.5 doubles it\n    s = radiometer_sigma_jy(2000.0, 2, 1e6, 1e-3, 1.0)\n    assert abs(s - np.sqrt(2000.0)) < 1e-9, s\n    assert abs(radiometer_sigma_jy(2000.0, 2, 1e6, 1e-3, 0.5) - 2.0 * s) < 1e-9\n    # 2. flat-band integral oracle: trapz(const) == const*(nu2-nu1)\n    freq_hz = np.linspace(1.311e9, 1.499e9, 64)\n    I = calibrated_band_integral_jy_ms_hz(np.full(64, 3.0), np.full(64, 5.0), freq_hz, 0.131072)\n    oracle = 3.0 * 5.0 * 0.131072 * (freq_hz[-1] - freq_hz[0])\n    assert abs(I - oracle) / oracle < 1e-9, (I, oracle)\n    print(\"self-check OK: radiometer noise + flat-band integral match analytic oracles\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    _check()\n"
}

147	   - **Rationale:** DSA-110 is a transit interferometer; at the burst's meridian transit the
148	     primary-beam offset is dominated by the declination difference, which we have (pointing Dec +
149	     source localization). The bursts cluster at Dec 70–74°, ~1–3° from a survey pointing Dec — a
150	     real, computable G variation near half power, not a negligible boresight case.
151	   - **Trade-offs:** Needs the per-burst pointing Dec (external: filterbank/h23). HA offset is a
152	     small documented correction (primary beam spans ±~6 min in HA).
153	   - **Alternatives considered:** Boresight G=1 for all (rejected — the Dec offsets are non-trivial);
154	     blocking on full per-instant pointing logs (the transit Dec is sufficient).
155	
156	**Patterns to Follow:**
157	- Pure function + `assert`-based `_check()`/`--check`, as in `analysis/dsa_beam.py:63-83` and
158	  `analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py:287-318`.

199	
200	- [ ] **Run it, watch it fail:** `pytest tests/test_flux_cal.py -v` → FAIL (module missing).
201	- [ ] **Implement** — `analysis/flux_cal.py` (new):
202	
203	  ```python
204	  #!/usr/bin/env python
205	  """Radiometer flux calibration: per-channel S/N -> Jy for FLITS dynamic spectra.
206	
207	  FLITS data is per-channel z-scored S/N (io.py:131-145), so physical flux density is
208	      S_nu(nu,t) [Jy] = (S/N)(nu,t) * sigma_S(nu),
209	      sigma_S(nu) = SEFD(nu) / (sqrt(n_pol*dnu*dt) * G(theta,phi,nu))   [Jy, radiometer].
210	  The band fluence integral (Jy*ms*Hz) feeds analysis/calculate_burst_energies.band_energy_erg
211	  with flux_scale=1 (the scale is already folded in here).
212	  """
213	  from __future__ import annotations
214	  import numpy as np
215	
216	  def radiometer_sigma_jy(sefd_jy, n_pol, dnu_hz, dt_s, g):
217	      """Per-sample radiometer noise [Jy]. SEFD = 2 k_B T_sys / A_eff; G = beam gain (boresight=1)."""
218	      return sefd_jy / (np.sqrt(n_pol * dnu_hz * dt_s) * g)
219	
220	  def calibrated_band_integral_jy_ms_hz(sn_integrated, sigma_jy, freq_hz, dt_ms):
221	      """int_band [ sigma_S(nu) * dt_ms * sum_onpulse(S/N)(nu) ] dnu   [Jy*ms*Hz].
222	
223	      sn_integrated: per-channel sum over the on-pulse window of (data/noise_std)  [dimensionless]
224	      sigma_jy:      per-channel sigma_S [Jy]; freq_hz ascending; dt_ms sample width [ms].
225	      """
226	      chan_fluence_jy_ms = sigma_jy * dt_ms * sn_integrated     # [Jy*ms] per channel
227	      return float(np.trapezoid(chan_fluence_jy_ms, freq_hz))   # [Jy*ms*Hz]
228	  ```

BurstDataset z-scores each channel (io.py:131-146), so model.data is already\n    S/N; dividing by the full-window per-channel noise makes the unit explicit and robust to the\n    downsample rescaling.\n    \"\"\"\n    import sys\n    from pathlib import Path\n\n    repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n    sys.path.insert(0, str(repo / \"scattering\"))  # io.py uses package-relative imports (..burstfit)\n    from scat_analysis.config_utils import load_telescope_block\n    from scat_analysis.pipeline.io import BurstDataset\n\n    tel = load_telescope_block(str(repo / \"scattering\" / \"configs\" / \"telescopes.yaml\"), telescope)\n    ds = BurstDataset(\n        inpath, inpath, telescope=tel, f_factor=f_factor, t_factor=t_factor,\n        onpulse_crop=True, onpulse_thresh=onpulse_thresh,\n    )\n    m = ds.model\n    noise = np.clip(m.noise_std, 1e-9, None)  # per-channel full-window noise (n_freq,)\n    sn = m.data / noise[:, None]  # (n_freq, n_time_onpulse) signal-to-noise\n    sn_integrated = np.nansum(sn, axis=1)  # sum over the cropped on-pulse window\n    return m.freq * 1e9, sn_integrated, ds.dt_ms, ds.df_MHz * 1e6\n\n\ndef _check() -> None:"

  "file_path": "/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/analysis/burst_energies/build_dsa_pointing.py",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python\n\"\"\"Build dsa_pointing.csv (burst, pointing_dec_deg, source) from the DSA detection-log\ncompilation of primary-beam pointings (dsa_primary_beam_pointings.csv, \"Dec ibeam\" column).\n\nDSA-110 is a transit array, so the primary-beam pointing Dec is ~constant (~71.6 deg here); the\nbeam offset for each burst is |Dec_src - Dec_pointing| (analysis/flux_cal.dsa_beam_offset). Only\nthe 12 nicknames in configs/bursts.yaml are emitted; the source CSV also lists extra/repeater\nevents (gertrude, pingu, FRB20220912A2) that are out of sample.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport csv\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport yaml\n\nHERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\nREPO = HERE.parents[1]\nSRC = HERE / \"dsa_primary_beam_pointings.csv\"\nOUT = HERE / \"dsa_pointing.csv\"\nALIAS = {\"johndoe (ii)\": \"johndoeii\"}  # CSV label -> bursts.yaml nickname\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    sample = set(yaml.safe_load((REPO / \"configs\" / \"bursts.yaml\").read_text())[\"bursts\"])\n    rows = []\n    for r in csv.DictReader(SRC.open()):\n        name = (r.get(\"Names\") or \"\").strip().lower()\n        nick = ALIAS.get(name, name)\n        dec = (r.get(\"Dec ibeam\") or \"\").strip()\n        if nick in sample and dec:\n            rows.append((nick, float(dec)))\n    rows.sort()\n    missing = sample - {n for n, _ in rows}\n    with OUT.open(\"w\", newline=\"\") as f:\n        w = csv.writer(f)\n        w.writerow([\"burst\", \"pointing_dec_deg\", \"source\"])\n        for nick, dec in rows:\n            w.writerow([nick, dec, \"DSA detection-log compilation (dsa_primary_beam_pointings.csv)\"])\n    print(f\"wrote {OUT} with {len(rows)} bursts; missing from source: {sorted(missing) or 'none'}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
}

> AGENT

Robust DSA SEFD: **median 8016 Jy, scatter ±2144 Jy (27%, ±0.116 dex)** over 129 clean epochs (22 bad ones rejected). This surfaces a genuine **plan/reality mismatch** I need to stop on (per the implementing-plans skill):

**Plan Phase 4 assumed** per-burst-epoch SEFD nearest each burst's MJD from dsa110-rt.
**Reality:** dsa110-rt's SEFD store is a **2026-02/03 measurement campaign** (151 epochs) — *none contemporaneous* with the 2022–2024 bursts. So a per-burst-epoch historical SEFD doesn't exist there. The SEFD also varies ~5150–9000 Jy by calibrator/conditions even within a day.

**Impact:** the DSA SEFD becomes a single representative constant (8016 Jy) with a ±27% epoch systematic, rather than per-epoch. The *per-burst* variation in σ_S is still carried exactly by the beam G (0.2–1.0, already computed) — only the absolute SEFD normalization is shared. A 27% SEFD systematic ≈ ±0.12 dex on energy (subdominant to the beam range).

Each epoch's `full_metrics.median_sefd`\nis SEFD = sigma*sqrt(2*dnu*tau*n_pol) from estimate_sefd.py, median over baselines.\n\nWe therefore use a single epoch-representative DSA SEFD for every burst: the ROBUST MEDIAN over the\nclean epochs (rejecting median_sefd > 15000 Jy, which are flagged/bad solutions), with the robust\nfractional scatter (1.4826*MAD/median ~ 0.27) recorded as a documented systematic. The PER-BURST\nvariation in sigma_S is carried exactly by the beam gain G (analysis/dsa_beam.py + dsa_pointing.csv),\nnot by the SEFD. See docs/rse/specs/plan-radiometer-flux-cal.md and CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md.\n\nRun from the repo root: python analysis/burst_energies/fetch_dsa_sefd.py\n\"\"\"\n\nimport csv\nimport json\nimport statistics\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport yaml\n\nHERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\nREPO = HERE.parents[1]\nSTATE_JSON = \"/media/ubuntu/ssd/vikram/sefd/sefd_dashboard/state.json\"\nSEFD_BAD_JY = 15000.0  # reject flagged/bad epochs above this\nOUT = HERE / \"dsa_sefd.csv\"\n\n\ndef robust_sefd_from_h23():\n    \"\"\"(median_jy, frac_scatter, n_clean, n_total) over the dashboard epochs on h23.\"\"\"\n    raw = subprocess.run(\n        [\"ssh\", \"h23\", f\"cat {STATE_JSON}\"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True\n    ).stdout\n    d = json.loads(raw)\n    xs = [v[\"full_metrics\"][\"median_sefd\"] for v in d.values() if v.get(\"full_metrics\", {}).get(\"median_sefd\")]\n    clean = [x for x in xs if x < SEFD_BAD_JY]\n    med = statistics.median(clean)\n    mad = statistics.median([abs(x - med) for x in clean])\n    return med, 1.4826 * mad / med, len(clean), len(xs)\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    med, frac, n_clean, n_total = robust_sefd_from_h23()\n    src = f\"dsa110-rt dashboard robust median over {n_clean}/{n_total} clean 2026-02/03 epochs (epoch-representative; no contemporaneous SEFD for 2022-2024)\"\n    bursts = yaml.safe_load((REPO / \"configs\" / \"bursts.yaml\").read_text())[\"bursts\"]\n    with OUT.open(\"w\", newline=\"\") as f:\n        w = csv.writer(f)\n        w.writerow([\"burst\", \"mjd\", \"sefd_jy\", \"sefd_frac_err\", \"source\"])\n        for nick in sorted(bursts):\n            w.writerow([nick, bursts[nick][\"mjd\"], round(med, 1), round(frac, 3), src])\n    print(f\"wrote {OUT}: SEFD={med:.0f} Jy +/- {frac:.0%} for {len(bursts)} bursts ({n_clean}/{n_total} epochs)\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
}

```
1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	"""Isotropic-equivalent energy E_iso for the co-detected FRB sample.
3	
4	For each sightline with a spectroscopic host redshift and a joint CHIME+DSA
5	scattering fit, integrate the fitted fluence spectrum F(nu) = c0 (nu/nu_ref)^gamma
6	over each telescope's OWN observed band, convert each band to an ABSOLUTE Jy
7	scale, k-correct, and sum:
8	
9	    E_iso = (4 pi D_L(z)^2 / (1+z)) [ s_C int_CHIME F_C dnu + s_D int_DSA F_D dnu ]
10	
11	where s_C, s_D are the per-band flux scales (Jy per native .npy fluence unit;
12	`flux_jy_per_unit` in configs/telescopes.yaml).
13	
14	Why the flux scale is mandatory (see analysis/burst_energies/CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md):
15	the joint fit recovers c0 in the input dynamic spectrum's NATIVE units, and CHIME
16	and DSA are not on a common flux standard. c0_C and c0_D are therefore in
17	independent, arbitrary per-telescope units. Summing two such bands is summing
18	dollars and yen: it is not an energy, and the per-burst CHIME:DSA mix varies, so
19	even the relative ORDERING of the total is unreliable. So this script refuses to
20	emit an energy until BOTH bands carry a real `flux_jy_per_unit` (from each
21	telescope's SEFD + beam response at the burst position). Until then it reports the
22	band fluence integrals in native units, flagged uncalibrated, and writes a
23	"pending calibration" LaTeX stub rather than a publishable table of fake erg.
24	
25	The (1+z) bandwidth k-correction (Zhang 2018) is applied by default; the
26	no-k-correction value is tabulated alongside so the manuscript can state the
27	convention explicitly.
28	
29	ref_freq is the band centre (f_min+f_max)/2; the fitter uses median(freq), which
30	equals the centre for a symmetric, uniformly-flagged band (small <~few% offset
31	under asymmetric channel flagging -> minor vs the calibration systematic).
32	
33	Usage:  python analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py [--check]
34	"""
35	
36	from __future__ import annotations
37	
38	import json
39	import sys
40	from pathlib import Path
41	
42	import numpy as np
43	import yaml
44	
45	REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
46	sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
47	
48	import astropy.units as u  # noqa: E402
49	
50	from galaxies.v2_0.config import COSMO, TARGETS  # noqa: E402
51	
52	JOINT_DIR = REPO / "analysis" / "scattering-refit-2026-06" / "joint_json"
53	TEL_CFG = REPO / "configs" / "telescopes.yaml"
54	OUT_DIR = REPO / "analysis" / "burst_energies"
55	
56	JY_MS_HZ_TO_SI = 1e-29  # 1 Jy*ms*Hz = 1e-29 J*m^-2
57	J_TO_ERG = 1e7
58	PLACEHOLDER_Z = 1.0  # Freya/Mahi/Johndoeii carry z=1.0000 as a "redshift unknown" flag
59	
60	
61	def band_edges_hz() -> dict[str, tuple[float, float, float]]:
62	    """(nu1, nu2, nu_ref) in Hz per band from the instrument config (band centre = ref)."""
63	    cfg = yaml.safe_load(TEL_CFG.read_text())
64	    out = {}
65	    for key, tag in (("chime", "C"), ("dsa", "D")):
66	        f1 = cfg[key]["f_min_GHz"] * 1e9
67	        f2 = cfg[key]["f_max_GHz"] * 1e9
68	        out[tag] = (f1, f2, 0.5 * (f1 + f2))
69	    return out
70	
71	
72	def flux_scales() -> dict[str, float | None]:
73	    """tag -> flux_jy_per_unit (Jy per native fluence unit), or None if uncalibrated."""
74	    cfg = yaml.safe_load(TEL_CFG.read_text())
75	    return {tag: cfg[key].get("flux_jy_per_unit") for key, tag in (("chime", "C"), ("dsa", "D"))}
76	
77	
78	def band_integral(c0: float, gamma: float, nu_ref: float, nu1: float, nu2: float) -> float:
79	    """int_{nu1}^{nu2} c0 (nu/nu_ref)^gamma dnu  [native*ms*Hz], freqs in Hz."""
80	    if abs(gamma + 1.0) < 1e-9:  # power law -> 1/nu, integral is a log
81	        return c0 * nu_ref * np.log(nu2 / nu1)
82	    g = gamma + 1.0
83	    return c0 * nu_ref / g * ((nu2 / nu_ref) ** g - (nu1 / nu_ref) ** g)
84	
85	
86	def band_energy_erg(
87	    i_raw: float, flux_scale: float, d_l_m: float, z: float, kcorr: bool = True
88	) -> float:
89	    """Band fluence integral [native*ms*Hz] x flux scale [Jy/native] -> E [erg].
90	
91	    (1+z) bandwidth k-correction (Zhang 2018, ApJ 867 L21) applied when kcorr=True.
92	    """
93	    factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + z) if kcorr else 1.0
94	    return 4.0 * np.pi * d_l_m**2 * i_raw * flux_scale * JY_MS_HZ_TO_SI * J_TO_ERG * factor
95	
96	
97	def load_redshifts() -> dict[str, float]:
98	    """nickname (lowercased) -> z_frb, from the galaxy-search TARGETS list."""
99	    return {name.lower(): z for name, _ra, _dec, z in TARGETS}
100	
101	
102	def load_joint_params() -> dict[str, dict]:
103	    """nickname (lowercased) -> {c0_C, gamma_C, c0_D, gamma_D} medians."""
104	    out = {}
105	    for p in sorted(JOINT_DIR.glob("*_joint_fit.json")):
106	        d = json.loads(p.read_text())
107	        pct = d["percentiles"]
108	        try:
109	            out[d["burst"].lower()] = {
110	                k: pct[k]["median"] for k in ("c0_C", "gamma_C", "c0_D", "gamma_D")
111	            }
112	        except KeyError:
113	            continue  # not a per-band-amplitude fit; skip
114	    return out
115	
116	
117	def compute(scales: dict[str, float | None] | None = None) -> list[dict]:
118	    bands = band_edges_hz()
119	    if scales is None:
120	        scales = flux_scales()
121	    s_C, s_D = scales["C"], scales["D"]
122	    calibrated = s_C is not None and s_D is not None
123	    zs = load_redshifts()
124	    fits = load_joint_params()
125	    nu1_C, nu2_C, ref_C = bands["C"]
126	    nu1_D, nu2_D, ref_D = bands["D"]
127	
128	    rows = []
129	    for nick in sorted(fits):
130	        z = zs.get(nick)
131	        if z is None or abs(z - PLACEHOLDER_Z) < 1e-6:
132	            continue  # no real host redshift -> cannot place a distance
133	        fp = fits[nick]
134	        d_l_m = COSMO.luminosity_distance(z).to(u.m).value
135	
136	        I_C = band_integral(fp["c0_C"], fp["gamma_C"], ref_C, nu1_C, nu2_C)
137	        I_D = band_integral(fp["c0_D"], fp["gamma_D"], ref_D, nu1_D, nu2_D)
138	
139	        row = {
140	            "burst": nick,
141	            "z": z,
142	            "D_L_Mpc": COSMO.luminosity_distance(z).to(u.Mpc).value,
143	            "c0_C": fp["c0_C"],
144	            "gamma_C": fp["gamma_C"],
145	            "c0_D": fp["c0_D"],
146	            "gamma_D": fp["gamma_D"],
147	            "I_CHIME_native_ms_Hz": I_C,  # band fluence integral, NATIVE units
148	            "I_DSA_native_ms_Hz": I_D,
149	            "calibrated": calibrated,
150	        }
151	        if calibrated:
152	            e_C = band_energy_erg(I_C, s_C, d_l_m, z)
153	            e_D = band_energy_erg(I_D, s_D, d_l_m, z)
154	            e_C0 = band_energy_erg(I_C, s_C, d_l_m, z, kcorr=False)
155	            e_D0 = band_energy_erg(I_D, s_D, d_l_m, z, kcorr=False)
156	            row.update(
157	                flux_jy_per_unit_C=s_C,
158	                flux_jy_per_unit_D=s_D,
159	                E_iso_CHIME_erg=e_C,
160	                E_iso_DSA_erg=e_D,
161	                E_iso_erg=e_C + e_D,  # legitimate: both bands now in Jy
162	                E_iso_erg_no_kcorr=e_C0 + e_D0,
163	            )
164	        rows.append(row)
165	    return rows
166	
167	
168	def markdown_table(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
169	    if rows and rows[0]["calibrated"]:
170	        head = (
171	            "| Burst | z | D_L (Mpc) | gamma_C | gamma_D | "
172	            "E_CHIME (erg) | E_DSA (erg) | E_iso (erg) | E_iso no-(1+z) (erg) |"
173	        )
174	        sep = "|" + "|".join(["---"] * 9) + "|"
175	        lines = [head, sep]
176	        for r in rows:
177	            lines.append(
178	                f"| {r['burst']} | {r['z']:.4f} | {r['D_L_Mpc']:.1f} | {r['gamma_C']:.2f} | "
179	                f"{r['gamma_D']:.2f} | {r['E_iso_CHIME_erg']:.3e} | {r['E_iso_DSA_erg']:.3e} | "
180	                f"{r['E_iso_erg']:.3e} | {r['E_iso_erg_no_kcorr']:.3e} |"
181	            )
182	        return "\n".join(lines)
183	    # uncalibrated: band fluence integrals in NATIVE units, flagged not-an-energy
184	    head = (
185	        "| Burst | z | D_L (Mpc) | gamma_C | gamma_D | "
186	        "int F_C (native*ms*Hz) | int F_D (native*ms*Hz) |"
187	    )
188	    sep = "|" + "|".join(["---"] * 7) + "|"
189	    lines = [head, sep]
190	    for r in rows:
191	        lines.append(
192	            f"| {r['burst']} | {r['z']:.4f} | {r['D_L_Mpc']:.1f} | {r['gamma_C']:.2f} | "
193	            f"{r['gamma_D']:.2f} | {r['I_CHIME_native_ms_Hz']:.3e} | {r['I_DSA_native_ms_Hz']:.3e} |"
194	        )
195	    return "\n".join(lines)
196	
197	
198	def _tex_pow(x: float) -> str:
199	    r"""Render a float as a\times10^{b} for LaTeX."""
200	    if x <= 0 or not np.isfinite(x):
201	        return r"\mathrm{n/a}"
202	    exp = int(np.floor(np.log10(x)))
203	    mant = x / 10**exp
204	    return rf"{mant:.2f}\times10^{{{exp}}}"
205	
206	
207	def latex_pending() -> str:
208	    """LaTeX stub written while the flux calibration is missing (no fake energies)."""
209	    return r"""% Auto-generated by analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py -- do not hand-edit.
210	% STATUS: flux calibration pending -- no energy table emitted (see below).
211	\subsection{Isotropic-equivalent energies}
212	\label{sec:burst-energies}
213	
214	Isotropic-equivalent burst energies are pending absolute flux calibration. The
215	joint CHIME--DSA fit constrains each band's fluence spectrum only in the native
216	units of its input dynamic spectrum, and CHIME and DSA are not placed on a common
217	flux standard, so the per-band amplitudes are not directly comparable and may not
218	be summed into an energy. Converting to physical $\mathrm{Jy\,ms}$ requires each
219	telescope's system-equivalent flux density and primary-beam response at the burst
220	position (Andersen et~al.\ 2023 and the baseband CHIME/FRB catalog update for
221	CHIME; Law et~al.\ 2024 for DSA-110). Once those scales are supplied, the energy
222	follows $E_{\mathrm{iso}} = (4\pi D_L^2(z)/(1+z))\,[\,s_C\!\int F_C\,d\nu +
223	s_D\!\int F_D\,d\nu\,]$ with the $(1+z)$ bandwidth k-correction.
224	"""
225	
226	
227	def latex_section(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
228	    body = []
229	    for r in rows:
230	        body.append(
231	            f"  {r['burst'].capitalize()} & ${r['z']:.4f}$ & ${r['D_L_Mpc']:.0f}$ & "
232	            f"${r['gamma_C']:+.2f}$ & ${r['gamma_D']:+.2f}$ & "
233	            f"${_tex_pow(r['E_iso_erg'])}$ \\\\"
234	        )
235	    table_body = "\n".join(body)
236	    return rf"""% Auto-generated by analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py -- do not hand-edit.
237	\subsection{{Isotropic-equivalent energies}}
238	\label{{sec:burst-energies}}
239	
240	For each sightline with a spectroscopic host redshift we estimate the
241	isotropic-equivalent burst energy directly from the joint CHIME--DSA fit,
242	without extrapolating either band's spectrum beyond where it is constrained.
243	The joint fit returns a per-band spectral amplitude and index,
244	$F_X(\nu) = c_{{0,X}}\,(\nu/\nu_{{\mathrm{{ref}},X}})^{{\gamma_X}}$, which we put on
245	an absolute scale with each telescope's flux calibration $s_X$
246	($\mathrm{{Jy}}$ per native unit) and integrate over its own observing
247	band---CHIME over $0.400$--$0.800\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$ and DSA over
248	$1.311$--$1.499\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$,
249	%
250	\begin{{equation}}
251	E_{{\mathrm{{iso}}}} = \frac{{4\pi D_L^2(z)}}{{1+z}}\left[
252	  s_C\!\int_{{\nu_1^{{C}}}}^{{\nu_2^{{C}}}} F_{{\mathrm{{CHIME}}}}(\nu)\,d\nu
253	  + s_D\!\int_{{\nu_1^{{D}}}}^{{\nu_2^{{D}}}} F_{{\mathrm{{DSA}}}}(\nu)\,d\nu
254	\right],
255	\label{{eq:eiso}}
256	\end{{equation}}
257	%
258	with $D_L(z)$ from the fiducial \textit{{Planck}}\,2018 cosmology, the $(1+z)$
259	bandwidth k-correction applied, and
260	$1\,\mathrm{{Jy\,ms\,Hz}} = 10^{{-29}}\,\mathrm{{J\,m^{{-2}}}}$. Bursts whose hosts
261	lack a spectroscopic redshift are omitted. This band-restricted integral
262	constrains the energy released \emph{{within the observed spectral envelope}}: it
263	avoids the large, model-dependent extrapolation that a single power law fit
264	across the full $0.4$--$1.5\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$ span would require, at the cost of not
265	counting flux in the unobserved $0.8$--$1.3\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$ gap (so the values are
266	lower limits on the $0.4$--$1.5\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$ energy).
267	
268	\begin{{table}}
269	\centering
270	\caption{{Isotropic-equivalent energies of the co-detected FRBs, integrated over
271	the CHIME ($0.4$--$0.8\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$) and DSA ($1.31$--$1.50\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$) bands
272	from the joint scattering fit and put on an absolute scale with each band's flux
273	calibration. $\gamma_C,\gamma_D$ are the per-band spectral indices;
274	$E_{{\mathrm{{iso}}}}$ includes the $(1+z)$ k-correction.}}
275	\label{{tab:burst-energies}}
276	\begin{{tabular}}{{lccccc}}
277	\hline\hline
278	Burst & $z$ & $D_L$ [Mpc] & $\gamma_{{C}}$ & $\gamma_{{D}}$ & $E_{{\mathrm{{iso}}}}$ [erg] \\
279	\hline
280	{table_body}
281	\hline
282	\end{{tabular}}
283	\end{{table}}
284	"""
285	
286	
287	def _check() -> None:
288	    # 1. closed-form band integral must match a dense numeric quadrature
289	    nu1, nu2, ref = 0.4e9, 0.8e9, 0.6e9
290	    for c0, g in ((2.0, -3.4), (0.18, -4.95), (1.0, -1.0), (3.0, 0.5)):
291	        nu = np.linspace(nu1, nu2, 200_001)
292	        num = np.trapezoid(c0 * (nu / ref) ** g, nu)
293	        ana = band_integral(c0, g, ref, nu1, nu2)
294	        assert abs(ana - num) / abs(num) < 1e-6, (c0, g, ana, num)
295	
296	    # 2. oracle: flat spectrum (gamma=0, c0=1) over a known band, scale=1, gives the
297	    #    analytic energy; (1+z) divides it; doubling the flux scale doubles it.
298	    i_flat = band_integral(1.0, 0.0, ref, nu1, nu2)
299	    assert abs(i_flat - (nu2 - nu1)) < 1e-3, i_flat  # int 1 dnu = bandwidth
300	    e0 = band_energy_erg(i_flat, 1.0, d_l_m=1.0, z=0.0)
301	    assert abs(e0 - 4.0 * np.pi * (nu2 - nu1) * JY_MS_HZ_TO_SI * J_TO_ERG) < 1e-6 * e0
302	    assert abs(band_energy_erg(i_flat, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) - e0 / 2.0) < 1e-9 * e0  # (1+z)=2
303	    assert abs(band_energy_erg(i_flat, 2.0, 1.0, 0.0) - 2.0 * e0) < 1e-9 * e0  # linear in scale
304	
305	    # 3. the gate itself, both directions (inject scales; independent of the live config)
306	    assert not any("E_iso_erg" in r for r in compute(scales={"C": None, "D": 1.0})), (
307	        "partial calibration leaked an energy"
308	    )
309	    cal_rows = compute(scales={"C": 1.0, "D": 1.0})
310	    assert cal_rows and all("E_iso_erg" in r for r in cal_rows), "calibrated run emitted no energy"
311	    r = cal_rows[0]
312	    assert abs(r["E_iso_erg"] - r["E_iso_erg_no_kcorr"] / (1.0 + r["z"])) < 1e-9 * r["E_iso_erg"]
313	    # and the live config must not be half-set (would silently drop one band's flux)
314	    live = flux_scales()
315	    assert (live["C"] is None) == (live["D"] is None), (
316	        "telescopes.yaml: calibrate both bands or neither"
317	    )
318	    print("self-check OK: integral matches quadrature; energy oracle, k-correction, and gate exact")
319	
320	
321	def main() -> None:
322	    if "--check" in sys.argv:
323	        _check()
324	        return
325	
326	    rows = compute()
327	    if not rows:
328	        sys.exit("no bursts with both a real redshift and a joint c0/gamma fit")
329	
330	    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
331	    (OUT_DIR / "burst_energies.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2))
332	    calibrated = rows[0]["calibrated"]
333	    tex = latex_section(rows) if calibrated else latex_pending()
334	    (OUT_DIR / "burst_energies.tex").write_text(tex)
335	
336	    print(markdown_table(rows))
337	    print(
338	        f"\nN = {len(rows)} bursts.  "
339	        f"Skipped: placeholder z=1.0 (freya/mahi/johndoeii) and any sightline "
340	        f"without a joint c0/gamma fit (e.g. casey)."
341	    )
342	    if not calibrated:
343	        print(
344	            "\n*** UNCALIBRATED: configs/telescopes.yaml has no flux_jy_per_unit for "
345	            "one or both bands. ***\n"
346	            "The columns above are band fluence integrals in NATIVE .npy units -- NOT "
347	            "energies, NOT comparable across bands, NOT to be quoted. Supply "
348	            "flux_jy_per_unit (Jy per native unit, from each telescope's SEFD + beam "
349	            "response at the burst position) for BOTH bands to emit E_iso. See "
350	            "analysis/burst_energies/CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md."
351	        )
352	    print(f"\nWrote {OUT_DIR / 'burst_energies.json'}")
353	    print(
354	        f"Wrote {OUT_DIR / 'burst_energies.tex'} ({'energy table' if calibrated else 'calibration-pending stub'})"
355	    )
356	
357	
358	if __name__ == "__main__":
359	    main()
360	
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	"""Radiometer flux calibration: per-channel S/N -> Jy for FLITS dynamic spectra.
3	
4	FLITS data is per-channel z-scored S/N (scattering/scat_analysis/pipeline/io.py:131-146:
5	_bandpass_correct divides each channel by its own off-pulse mean/std and the loader keeps
6	"units as S/N"). Physical flux density is therefore one radiometer multiply away:
7	
8	    S_nu(nu,t) [Jy] = (S/N)(nu,t) * sigma_S(nu),
9	    sigma_S(nu) = SEFD(nu) / (sqrt(n_pol * dnu * dt) * G(theta,phi,nu)),
10	
11	with SEFD = 2 k_B T_sys / A_eff and G the beam gain (boresight=1). Dividing by the
12	per-channel off-pulse noise also cancels the bandpass gain, so the S/N spectrum (and hence
13	this calibration) is free of the band-edge rolloff that rails the fitted gamma_D.
14	
15	The band fluence integral (Jy*ms*Hz) returned here feeds
16	analysis/calculate_burst_energies.band_energy_erg with flux_scale=1 -- the per-channel scale
17	is already folded in. See docs/rse/specs/plan-radiometer-flux-cal.md.
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	import numpy as np
23	
24	
25	def radiometer_sigma_jy(sefd_jy, n_pol, dnu_hz, dt_s, g):
26	    """Per-sample radiometer noise [Jy]: SEFD / (sqrt(n_pol*dnu*dt) * G).
27	
28	    sefd_jy: system-equivalent flux density [Jy]; n_pol: summed polarisations;
29	    dnu_hz: channel bandwidth [Hz]; dt_s: sample time [s]; g: beam gain (boresight=1).
30	    """
31	    return sefd_jy / (np.sqrt(n_pol * dnu_hz * dt_s) * g)
32	
33	
34	def calibrated_band_integral_jy_ms_hz(sn_integrated, sigma_jy, freq_hz, dt_ms):
35	    """int_band [ sigma_S(nu) * dt_ms * sum_onpulse(S/N)(nu) ] dnu   [Jy*ms*Hz].
36	
37	    sn_integrated: per-channel sum over the on-pulse window of (data/noise_std) [dimensionless];
38	    sigma_jy: per-channel sigma_S [Jy]; freq_hz: ascending channel centres [Hz]; dt_ms: sample [ms].
39	    """
40	    chan_fluence_jy_ms = sigma_jy * dt_ms * sn_integrated  # [Jy*ms] per channel
41	    return float(np.trapezoid(chan_fluence_jy_ms, freq_hz))  # [Jy*ms*Hz]
42	
43	
44	def sn_spectrum_from_npy(inpath, telescope, f_factor=1, t_factor=1, onpulse_thresh=3.0):
45	    """Per-channel on-pulse S/N spectrum from a burst .npy via the FLITS loader.
46	
47	    Returns (freq_hz ascending, sn_integrated [per channel, sum over on-pulse of data/noise_std],
48	    dt_ms, dnu_hz). BurstDataset z-scores each channel (io.py:131-146), so model.data is already
49	    S/N; dividing by the full-window per-channel noise makes the unit explicit and robust to the
50	    downsample rescaling.
51	    """
52	    import sys
53	    from pathlib import Path
54	
55	    repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
56	    sys.path.insert(0, str(repo / "scattering"))  # io.py uses package-relative imports (..burstfit)
57	    from scat_analysis.config_utils import load_telescope_block
58	    from scat_analysis.pipeline.io import BurstDataset
59	
60	    tel = load_telescope_block(str(repo / "scattering" / "configs" / "telescopes.yaml"), telescope)
61	    ds = BurstDataset(
62	        inpath,
63	        inpath,
64	        telescope=tel,
65	        f_factor=f_factor,
66	        t_factor=t_factor,
67	        onpulse_crop=True,
68	        onpulse_thresh=onpulse_thresh,
69	    )
70	    m = ds.model
71	    noise = np.clip(m.noise_std, 1e-9, None)  # per-channel full-window noise (n_freq,)
72	    sn = m.data / noise[:, None]  # (n_freq, n_time_onpulse) signal-to-noise
73	    sn_integrated = np.nansum(sn, axis=1)  # sum over the cropped on-pulse window
74	    return m.freq * 1e9, sn_integrated, ds.dt_ms, ds.df_MHz * 1e6
75	
76	
77	def dsa_sigma_jy(freq_hz, dnu_hz, sefd_jy, dt_s, theta_deg, phi_deg, beam_gain_fn):
78	    """Per-channel radiometer noise sigma_S(nu) [Jy] for DSA (n_pol=2) at a beam offset.
79	
80	    beam_gain_fn(theta_deg, phi_deg, freq_ghz) -> normalized power-beam gain (boresight=1);
81	    dnu_hz is the channel bandwidth (downsampled ds.df_MHz*1e6), dt_s the sample time [s].
82	    """
83	    g = np.array([beam_gain_fn(theta_deg, phi_deg, f / 1e9) for f in freq_hz])
84	    return radiometer_sigma_jy(sefd_jy, 2, dnu_hz, dt_s, g)
85	
86	
87	def dsa_beam_offset(dec_src, dec_pointing):
88	    """(theta_deg, phi_deg) of the source from the DSA primary-beam boresight.
89	
90	    DSA-110 is a transit array: at the burst's meridian transit (HA~0) the boresight sits at the
91	    source RA, so the angular separation is exactly the declination difference; phi=0 (meridian).
92	    HA refinement (small E-W term) is out of scope -- see the plan.
93	    """
94	    return abs(dec_src - dec_pointing), 0.0
95	
96	
97	def burst_epoch_position(nick):
98	    """(mjd, ra_deg, dec_deg) for a burst nickname from configs/bursts.yaml."""
99	    from pathlib import Path
100	
101	    import yaml
102	
103	    b = yaml.safe_load(
104	        (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "configs" / "bursts.yaml").read_text()
105	    )
106	    e = b["bursts"][nick]
107	    return float(e["mjd"]), float(e["ra_deg"]), float(e["dec_deg"])
108	
109	
110	def _csv_lookup(filename, key, key_col="burst", val_col=None):
111	    import csv
112	    from pathlib import Path
113	
114	    p = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "analysis" / "burst_energies" / filename
115	    if not p.exists():
116	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{p} missing -- run the Phase 4 acquisition")
117	    for row in csv.DictReader(p.open()):
118	        if row[key_col] == key:
119	            return row[val_col]
120	    raise KeyError(f"{key} not in {p}")
121	
122	
123	def load_dsa_sefd(nick):
124	    """Measured DSA SEFD [Jy] nearest the burst epoch, from dsa_sefd.csv (Phase 4)."""
125	    return float(_csv_lookup("dsa_sefd.csv", nick, val_col="sefd_jy"))
126	
127	
128	def dsa_pointing_dec(nick):
129	    """DSA primary-beam pointing declination [deg] for a burst, from dsa_pointing.csv (Phase 4)."""
130	    return float(_csv_lookup("dsa_pointing.csv", nick, val_col="pointing_dec_deg"))
131	
132	
133	def _check() -> None:
134	    # 1. radiometer noise vs analytic: 2000/sqrt(2*1e6*1e-3) == sqrt(2000); G=0.5 doubles it
135	    s = radiometer_sigma_jy(2000.0, 2, 1e6, 1e-3, 1.0)
136	    assert abs(s - np.sqrt(2000.0)) < 1e-9, s
137	    assert abs(radiometer_sigma_jy(2000.0, 2, 1e6, 1e-3, 0.5) - 2.0 * s) < 1e-9
138	    # 2. flat-band integral oracle: trapz(const) == const*(nu2-nu1)
139	    freq_hz = np.linspace(1.311e9, 1.499e9, 64)
140	    i_band = calibrated_band_integral_jy_ms_hz(
141	        np.full(64, 3.0), np.full(64, 5.0), freq_hz, 0.131072
142	    )
143	    oracle = 3.0 * 5.0 * 0.131072 * (freq_hz[-1] - freq_hz[0])
144	    assert abs(i_band - oracle) / oracle < 1e-9, (i_band, oracle)
145	    print("self-check OK: radiometer noise + flat-band integral match analytic oracles")
146	
147	
148	if __name__ == "__main__":
149	    _check()
150	
```

PLACEHOLDER_Z) < 1e-6:\n            continue  # no real host redshift -> cannot place a distance\n        fp = fits[nick]\n        d_l_m = COSMO.luminosity_distance(z).to(u.m).value\n\n        I_C = band_integral(fp[\"c0_C\"], fp[\"gamma_C\"], ref_C, nu1_C, nu2_C)\n        I_D = band_integral(fp[\"c0_D\"], fp[\"gamma_D\"], ref_D, nu1_D, nu2_D)\n\n        I_C_jy, cal_C = _band_jy(s_C, I_C, nick, None)  # CHIME fluxcal: Phase 6\n        I_D_jy, cal_D = _band_jy(s_D, I_D, nick, dsa_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz)\n        calibrated = cal_C and cal_D\n\n        row = {\n            \"burst\": nick,\n            \"z\": z,\n            \"D_L_Mpc\": COSMO.luminosity_distance(z).to(u.Mpc).value,\n            \"c0_C\": fp[\"c0_C\"],\n            \"gamma_C\": fp[\"gamma_C\"],\n            \"c0_D\": fp[\"c0_D\"],\n            \"gamma_D\": fp[\"gamma_D\"],\n            \"I_CHIME_native_ms_Hz\": I_C,  # band fluence integral, NATIVE units\n            \"I_DSA_native_ms_Hz\": I_D,\n            \"calibrated\": calibrated,\n        }\n        if I_C_jy is not None:\n            row[\"I_CHIME_jy_ms_hz\"] = I_C_jy\n        if I_D_jy is not None:\n            row[\"I_DSA_jy_ms_hz\"] = I_D_jy\n        if calibrated:\n            e_C = band_energy_erg(I_C_jy, 1.0, d_l_m, z)  # scale already folded into I_*_jy\n            e_D = band_energy_erg(I_D_jy, 1.0, d_l_m, z)\n            e_C0 = band_energy_erg(I_C_jy, 1.0, d_l_m, z, kcorr=False)\n            e_D0 = band_energy_erg(I_D_jy, 1.0, d_l_m, z, kcorr=False)\n            row.update(\n                flux_jy_per_unit_C=s_C,\n                flux_jy_per_unit_D=s_D,\n                E_iso_CHIME_erg=e_C,\n                E_iso_DSA_erg=e_D,\n                E_iso_erg=e_C + e_D,  # legitimate: both bands now in Jy\n                E_iso_erg_no_kcorr=e_C0 + e_D0,\n            )\n        rows.append(row)\n    return rows"

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py",
  "old_string": "    # uncalibrated: band fluence integrals in NATIVE units, flagged not-an-energy\n    head = (\n        \"| Burst | z | D_L (Mpc) | gamma_C | gamma_D | \"\n        \"int F_C (native*ms*Hz) | int F_D (native*ms*Hz) |\"\n    )\n    sep = \"|\" + \"|\".join([\"---\"] * 7) + \"|\"\n    lines = [head, sep]\n    for r in rows:\n        lines.append(\n            f\"| {r['burst']} | {r['z']:.4f} | {r['D_L_Mpc']:.1f} | {r['gamma_C']:.2f} | \"\n            f\"{r['gamma_D']:.2f} | {r['I_CHIME_native_ms_Hz']:.3e} | {r['I_DSA_native_ms_Hz']:.3e} |\"\n        )\n    return \"\\n\".join(lines)",
  "new_string": "    # uncalibrated: band fluence integrals in NATIVE units, flagged not-an-energy. When a band is\n    # flux-calibrated but the other is not (gate closed), also surface its Jy*ms*Hz integral.\n    has_dsa_jy = any(\"I_DSA_jy_ms_hz\" in r for r in rows)\n    head = (\n        \"| Burst | z | D_L (Mpc) | gamma_C | gamma_D | \"\n        \"int F_C (native*ms*Hz) | int F_D (native*ms*Hz) |\"\n    )\n    if has_dsa_jy:\n        head += \" int F_D (Jy*ms*Hz) |\"\n    sep = \"|\" + \"|\".join([\"---\"] * (8 if has_dsa_jy else 7)) + \"|\"\n    lines = [head, sep]\n    for r in rows:\n        line = (\n            f\"| {r['burst']} | {r['z']:.4f} | {r['D_L_Mpc']:.1f} | {r['gamma_C']:.2f} | \"\n            f\"{r['gamma_D']:.2f} | {r['I_CHIME_native_ms_Hz']:.3e} | {r['I_DSA_native_ms_Hz']:.3e} |\"\n        )\n        if has_dsa_jy:\n            jy = r.get(\"I_DSA_jy_ms_hz\")\n            line += f\" {jy:.3e} |\" if jy is not None else \" -- |\"\n        lines.append(line)\n    return \"\\n\".join(lines)"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Phase 5: DSA-band flux calibration wired into the energetics gate.\n\nThe \"fluxcal\" sentinel routes a band through the data-driven radiometer integral\n(analysis.flux_cal.dsa_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz) instead of native-units x scalar, while the\nboth-bands-or-nothing gate stays closed until CHIME is calibrated too (Phase 6).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport analysis.calculate_burst_energies as E\n\n\ndef test_dsa_calibrated_but_gate_closed(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.setattr(E, \"dsa_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz\", lambda nick: 1.234e6)\n    rows = E.compute(scales={\"C\": None, \"D\": \"fluxcal\"})  # D via flux_cal, C still uncalibrated\n    assert rows\n    assert all(\"E_iso_erg\" not in r for r in rows)  # gate closed -> no summed energy\n    assert any(abs(r.get(\"I_DSA_jy_ms_hz\", 0) - 1.234e6) < 1 for r in rows)  # DSA Jy on the row\n\n\ndef test_both_bands_fluxcal_opens_gate(monkeypatch):\n    # when CHIME is also flux-calibrated, the gate opens and E_iso is summed from both Jy integrals\n    monkeypatch.setattr(E, \"dsa_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz\", lambda nick: 2.0e6)\n    rows = E.compute(scales={\"C\": 5.0, \"D\": \"fluxcal\"})  # C legacy scalar, D data-driven\n    assert rows and all(\"E_iso_erg\" in r for r in rows)\n    r = rows[0]\n    # k-correction halves the (1+z) relation exactly\n    assert abs(r[\"E_iso_erg\"] - r[\"E_iso_erg_no_kcorr\"] / (1.0 + r[\"z\"])) < 1e-9 * r[\"E_iso_erg\"]\n    assert abs(r[\"E_iso_DSA_erg\"] - r[\"E_iso_erg_no_kcorr_components_dsa\"]) > -1  # field presence noop\n\n\ndef test_dsa_burst_config_resolves():\n    # data-independent: the batch config maps nick -> the canonical .npy name + the fit's binning\n    from analysis.flux_cal import _dsa_burst_config\n\n    npy, f_factor, t_factor = _dsa_burst_config(\"chromatica\")\n    assert npy.name == \"chromatica_dsa_I_272_368_2500b_cntr_bpc.npy\"\n    assert f_factor == 384 and t_factor == 2\n"
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	"""DSA-110 primary-beam gain from the measured Jones E-field cube (DSA110_beam_1.h5).
3	
4	Stokes-I power beam P = |E_theta|^2 + |E_phi|^2 summed over the X and Y feeds,
5	normalized to boresight (theta=0) = 1 at each frequency. This is the relative
6	sensitivity at a burst's angular offset from the pointing centre -- the beam
7	attenuation factor G in the radiometer flux calibration
8	
9	    F = (S/N) * SEFD / ( sqrt(n_pol * dnu * dt) * G(theta, phi, nu) ).
10	
11	It replaces the analytic Airy-disk fallback in dsa110-continuum
12	(calibration/beam_model.py) with the measured/simulated dish pattern.
13	
14	Cube layout (N_freq, N_theta, N_phi):
15	  freq: 1.2-1.6 GHz, 41 pts. NOTE the HDF5 dataset is named `freq_Hz` and carries a
16	        `freq_units="MHz"` attr, but the stored values are 1.2-1.6 -- unambiguously
17	        GHz (idx 20 = 1.40 GHz, matching the dish's L-band). Both labels are wrong;
18	        the values are GHz. Covers the DSA fit band (1.311-1.499 GHz).
19	  theta: 0-180 deg (zenith angle), 1801 pts @ 0.1 deg; phi: 0-360 deg (azimuth), 73 pts.
20	
21	The absolute scale still needs the boresight SEFD, which is MEASURED per-day /
22	per-calibrator (not a constant) by the dsa110-rt SEFD dashboard
23	(github.com/dsa110/dsa110-rt, served on lxd110h23:5777); use the value nearest a
24	burst's epoch. See analysis/burst_energies/CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md.
25	"""
26	
27	from __future__ import annotations
28	
29	from pathlib import Path
30	
31	import numpy as np
32	
33	# External cube (~345 MB, gitignored); override via telescopes.yaml `beam_model_h5`.
34	DEFAULT_BEAM = Path.home() / "Downloads" / "DSA110_beam_1.h5"
35	
36	
37	def load_power_beam(path: str | Path = DEFAULT_BEAM):
38	    """(freq_ghz, theta_deg, phi_deg, P) with P normalized to boresight=1 per frequency."""
39	    import h5py
40	
41	    with h5py.File(path, "r") as f:
42	        freq_ghz = f["freq_Hz"][:].astype(float)  # mislabeled units; values are GHz
43	        theta = f["theta_pts"][:].astype(float)  # deg
44	        phi = f["phi_pts"][:].astype(float)  # deg
45	        P = np.zeros((freq_ghz.size, theta.size, phi.size))
46	        for grp in ("X_pol_Efields", "Y-pol_Efields"):
47	            P += np.abs(f[f"{grp}/etheta"][:]) ** 2 + np.abs(f[f"{grp}/ephi"][:]) ** 2
48	    P /= P[:, 0, :].mean(axis=1)[:, None, None]  # boresight (theta=0) -> 1 at each freq
49	    return freq_ghz, theta, phi, P
50	
51	
52	def beam_gain(
53	    theta_deg: float, phi_deg: float, freq_ghz: float, path: str | Path = DEFAULT_BEAM
54	) -> float:
55	    """Normalized power-beam gain (boresight=1) at an offset, via trilinear interpolation."""
56	    from scipy.interpolate import RegularGridInterpolator
57	
58	    fz, th, ph, P = load_power_beam(path)
59	    g = RegularGridInterpolator((fz, th, ph), P, bounds_error=False, fill_value=None)
60	    return float(g([[freq_ghz, theta_deg, np.mod(phi_deg, 360.0)]])[0])
61	
62	
63	def _check(path: str | Path = DEFAULT_BEAM) -> None:
64	    if not Path(path).exists():
65	        print(f"self-check SKIP: beam cube not found at {path}")
66	        return
67	    fz, th, ph, P = load_power_beam(path)
68	    assert abs(P[:, 0, :].mean() - 1.0) < 1e-9, "boresight not normalized to 1"
69	    assert 1.2 <= fz.min() and fz.max() <= 1.6, ("freq axis not GHz?", fz.min(), fz.max())
70	    g0 = beam_gain(0.0, 0.0, 1.4, path)
71	    assert abs(g0 - 1.0) < 1e-6, g0  # boresight = 1
72	    g_hp = beam_gain(1.8, 0.0, 1.4, path)
73	    assert 0.2 < g_hp < 0.8, ("half-power radius off", g_hp)  # ~half power near FWHM/2
74	    g_far = beam_gain(5.0, 0.0, 1.4, path)
75	    assert g_far < g_hp, ("gain not falling off-axis", g_far, g_hp)
76	    print(
77	        f"self-check OK: boresight=1, gain(1.8deg,1.4GHz)={g_hp:.3f} (~half power), "
78	        f"gain(5deg)={g_far:.3f}; freq {fz.min():.2f}-{fz.max():.2f} GHz"
79	    )
80	
81	
82	if __name__ == "__main__":
83	    _check()
84	
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Stop hook: block end-of-turn while generated figures have not been VISUALLY assessed.
3	#
4	# Contract: a figure-producing run writes <dir>/figures.manifest.json listing each PNG
5	# and the expectation it should satisfy. The review step (figure-reviewer subagent, or
6	# inline) Reads each PNG and writes <dir>/figures.review.json with per-figure verdicts.
7	# If any manifest is newer than its review (or has no review), the figures were produced
8	# but not looked at -> block, so "I made a plot" can never silently become "validated".
9	#
10	# Pure mtime check (no transcript parsing). No-op when no manifests exist.
11	set -uo pipefail
12	
13	ROOT="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}"
14	
15	unreviewed=()
16	while IFS= read -r man; do
17	  [ -n "$man" ] || continue
18	  rev="$(dirname "$man")/figures.review.json"
19	  # -nt is true if man is newer than rev OR rev does not exist
20	  if [ "$man" -nt "$rev" ]; then
21	    unreviewed+=("$(dirname "$man")")
22	  fi
23	done < <(find "$ROOT" -name figures.manifest.json -not -path '*/.git/*' 2>/dev/null)
24	
25	# Nothing produced-but-unreviewed -> allow stop.
26	[ "${#unreviewed[@]}" -eq 0 ] && exit 0
27	
28	dirs="$(printf '%s\n' "${unreviewed[@]}")"
29	read -r -d '' REASON <<EOF || true
30	FIGURE-REVIEW GATE: figures were produced but not visually assessed.
31	
32	Before finishing you MUST actually LOOK at each PNG (Read the image file so it renders)
33	and compare it to the stated expectation in that dir's figures.manifest.json, the way a
34	person reviewing a colleague's plots would. Check: axes/units sane, expected features
35	present (peaks, tails, scales), no artifacts/empty panels/wrong ranges, and that annotated
36	numbers match the visual.
37	
38	Then write figures.review.json in the same dir:
39	  {"reviewed_by": "...", "verdicts": [
40	     {"path": "<png>", "verdict": "match" | "anomaly" | "skipped:<why>", "notes": "<what you SAW>"}]}
41	
42	Fastest path: dispatch the figure-reviewer subagent (Agent tool, subagent_type "figure-reviewer")
43	on each dir below. Escape hatch: if a figure genuinely cannot be assessed, record
44	verdict "skipped:<reason>" so the gate can clear.
45	
46	Unreviewed figure dirs:
47	${dirs}
48	EOF
49	
50	# Emit the block decision as JSON (python stdlib is hook-PATH-safe for json.dumps).
51	python3 - "$REASON" <<'PY' 2>/dev/null || printf '{"decision":"block","reason":"Figures produced but unreviewed; see figures.manifest.json and write figures.review.json."}\n'
52	import json, sys
53	print(json.dumps({"decision": "block", "reason": sys.argv[1]}))
54	PY
55	exit 0
56	
```

A calibrated slope that still\ntracks gamma_D would instead support a genuine steep spectrum.\n\nRun from the repo root: python analysis/burst_energies/plot_bandpass_check.py\n\"\"\"\n\nimport json\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport matplotlib\n\nmatplotlib.use(\"Agg\")\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402\nimport numpy as np  # noqa: E402\n\nREPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]\nsys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))\n\nfrom analysis.dsa_beam import beam_gain  # noqa: E402\nfrom analysis.flux_cal import (  # noqa: E402\n    _dsa_burst_config,\n    burst_epoch_position,\n    dsa_beam_offset,\n    dsa_pointing_dec,\n    dsa_sigma_jy,\n    load_dsa_sefd,\n    sn_spectrum_from_npy,\n)\n\nJOINT_DIR = REPO / \"analysis\" / \"scattering-refit-2026-06\" / \"joint_json\"\nOUT_DIR = REPO / \"analysis\" / \"burst_energies\"\nNU_REF = 1.405e9  # DSA band centre [Hz] (matches calculate_burst_energies)\n\n\ndef joint_dsa_params():\n    \"\"\"nick (lower) -> (c0_D, gamma_D) median, for bursts whose joint fit has per-band amplitudes.\"\"\"\n    out = {}\n    for p in sorted(JOINT_DIR.glob(\"*_joint_fit.json\")):\n        d = json.loads(p.read_text())\n        pct = d.get(\"percentiles\", {})\n        if \"c0_D\" in pct and \"gamma_D\" in pct:\n            out[d[\"burst\"].lower()] = (pct[\"c0_D\"][\"median\"], pct[\"gamma_D\"][\"median\"])\n    return out\n\n\ndef loglog_slope(freq_hz, y):\n    \"\"\"Effective power-law slope of y(nu) over channels where y>0 (log-log least squares).\"\"\"\n    m = np.isfinite(y) & (y > 0)\n    if m.sum() < 3:\n        return np.nan\n    return float(np.polyfit(np.log(freq_hz[m]), np.log(y[m]), 1)[0])\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    fits = joint_dsa_params()\n    nicks = []\n    for cfg in sorted((REPO / \"configs\" / \"batch\" / \"dsa\").glob(\"*_dsa.yaml\")):\n        nick = cfg.name[: -len(\"_dsa.yaml\")]\n        npy, _, _ = _dsa_burst_config(nick)\n        if nick in fits and npy.exists():\n            nicks.append(nick)\n    if not nicks:\n        sys.exit(\"no bursts with both a joint gamma_D fit and a staged DSA .npy (data/dsa/)\")\n\n    ncol = 3\n    nrow = -(-len(nicks) // ncol)\n    fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrow, ncol, figsize=(4.2 * ncol, 3.1 * nrow), squeeze=False)\n    summary = []\n    for ax, nick in zip(axes.flat, nicks):\n        c0_D, gamma_D = fits[nick]\n        npy, ff, tf = _dsa_burst_config(nick)\n        freq_hz, sn_int, dt_ms, dnu_hz = sn_spectrum_from_npy(npy, \"dsa\", ff, tf)\n        _, _, dec = burst_epoch_position(nick)\n        theta, phi = dsa_beam_offset(dec, dsa_pointing_dec(nick))\n        g_ref = beam_gain(theta, phi, NU_REF / 1e9)\n        sigma = dsa_sigma_jy(freq_hz, dnu_hz, load_dsa_sefd(nick), dt_ms / 1e3, theta, phi, beam_gain)\n        cal = sigma * dt_ms * sn_int  # per-channel fluence [Jy*ms]\n        model = c0_D * (freq_hz / NU_REF) ** gamma_D  # fitted S/N power law\n\n        f_ghz = freq_hz / 1e9\n        sn_slope = loglog_slope(freq_hz, sn_int)\n        cal_slope = loglog_slope(freq_hz, cal)\n        nrm = lambda a: a / np.nanmax(np.abs(a))  # noqa: E731 peak-normalize for shape comparison\n        ax.plot(f_ghz, nrm(sn_int), \"o\", ms=3, color=\"0.45\", label=\"S/N spectrum (fit)\")\n        ax.plot(f_ghz, nrm(model), \"--\", color=\"0.45\", lw=1.2, label=rf\"$\\nu^{{{gamma_D:.1f}}}$ fit\")\n        ax.plot(f_ghz, nrm(cal), \"s\", ms=3, color=\"C3\", label=\"flux-calibrated\")\n        ax.set_title(\n            f\"{nick}  θ={theta:.1f}° G={g_ref:.2f}\\n\"\n            rf\"$\\gamma_D$={gamma_D:.1f}  cal slope={cal_slope:.1f}\",\n            fontsize=8,\n        )\n        ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)\n        ax.axhline(0, color=\"0.85\", lw=0.6, zorder=0)\n        summary.append(\n            {\"burst\": nick, \"theta_deg\": round(theta, 2), \"G_ref\": round(g_ref, 3),\n             \"gamma_D\": round(gamma_D, 2), \"sn_slope\": round(sn_slope, 2),\n             \"cal_slope\": round(cal_slope, 2), \"flatter\": abs(cal_slope) < abs(gamma_D)}\n        )\n    for ax in axes.flat[len(nicks):]:\n        ax.set_visible(False)\n    axes.flat[0].legend(fontsize=6, loc=\"upper right\")\n    fig.supxlabel(\"frequency [GHz]\", fontsize=9)\n    fig.supylabel(\"peak-normalized per-channel amplitude\", fontsize=9)\n    fig.tight_layout()\n    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    png = OUT_DIR / \"bandpass_check.png\"\n    fig.savefig(png, dpi=130)\n    print(f\"wrote {png}\")\n\n    n_flatter = sum(s[\"flatter\"] for s in summary)\n    expectation = (\n        \"Per burst, the red flux-calibrated squares vs the grey S/N points + dashed nu^gamma_D \"\n        \"fit. HYPOTHESIS: if gamma_D~-5 is a DSA sensitivity/bandpass artifact, the calibrated \"\n        \"spectrum is FLATTER -- its 'cal slope' is markedly less negative than gamma_D (esp. for \"\n        \"the railed bursts chromatica/oran/phineas/zach). Annotated cal slope should match the \"\n        \"visual red trend; axes 1.31-1.50 GHz; no empty panels.\"\n    )\n    manifest = {\n        \"generated_by\": \"analysis/burst_energies/plot_bandpass_check.py\",\n        \"figures\": [{\"path\": \"bandpass_check.png\", \"expectation\": expectation}],\n        \"per_burst\": summary,\n        \"n_flatter_than_gammaD\": f\"{n_flatter}/{len(summary)}\",\n        \"caveat_absolute_scale\": (\n            \"SHAPE/slope comparison is robust; ABSOLUTE Jy scale (band-avg fluences 218-6860 Jy*ms) \"\n            \"is high vs published DSA fluences and is a separate cross-check (SEFD/n_pol/beam), not \"\n            \"asserted here.\"\n        ),\n    }\n    (OUT_DIR / \"figures.manifest.json\").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2))\n    print(f\"wrote {OUT_DIR / 'figures.manifest.json'}; flatter-than-gamma_D: {n_flatter}/{len(summary)}\")\n    for s in summary:\n        print(s)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"

> AGENT

Ran, but two issues to fix: ruff `B905` (zip without `strict`), and my "flatter" metric compares `cal_slope` (naive log-log) against `γ_D` (MCMC 2D fit) — apples-to-oranges. The honest calibration effect is `cal_slope − sn_slope` (the slope of `σ_S(ν)` itself). The result is actually cleaner that way: off-axis bursts flatten (freya −3.65→−1.08), on-axis don't (phineas −9.1→−9.1, G=0.997). Also dropping the `θ` glyph (missing from font → renders as tofu). Reading the current file then fixing:

**Confirmed against the authoritative code:** `estimate_sefd.py` on h23 is `compute_sefd_per_baseline` — `SEFD = sigma·sqrt(2·Δν·τ·n_pol)` computed **per baseline**, median reported. A per-baseline SEFD ≈ the per-**antenna** SEFD (√(SEFD_i·SEFD_j)). But the `cntr_bpc` arrays are the **coherent detection beam** (phased sum of N_ant antennas), whose SEFD = SEFD_ant/N_ant. So σ_S is too large by ~N_ant.

Sanity: dividing my fluences by N_ant≈63 gives zach 27, freya 109, mahi 3.5, hamilton 3.7 Jy·ms — all physical DSA values. To anchor N_ant, cross-checking against the published fluences (these are published DSA FRBs):

This is the decisive anchor. From Law et al. 2024 (arXiv:2307.03344), Table 1 — **and the detection S/N matches my bursts exactly** (60.0, 68.4, 48.9), confirming identity:

| burst (TNS in catalog) | published fluence | my code | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| zach (FRB 20220207C) | **16.2** Jy·ms | 1680 | **104×** |
| whitney (FRB 20220310F) | **26.2** Jy·ms | 2728 | **104×** |
| oran (FRB 20220506D) | **13.2** Jy·ms | 570 | **43×** |

The audit is conclusive, and cleaner than I expected. The published fluences are reproduced **exactly** by the standard matched-filter radiometer `F = (S/N)·SEFD·√W / √(n_pol·Δν)` with a **single coherent-beam SEFD ≈ 234 Jy** (zach→234, whitney→235, oran→234). Two distinct errors in my per-channel code:

1. **Absolute scale (~34–48×):** σ_S uses the **per-element** SEFD (~8016 Jy, verified = `compute_sefd_per_baseline` on h23) instead of the **coherent-beam** SEFD. The catalog states **"48 antennas"** coherently combined; SEFD_beam = SEFD_element/N_ant ≈ 8016/48 ≈ 167 Jy (empirically 234 Jy). This is the dominant error.
2. **Residual ~2× burst-dependent:** my per-channel `Σ_onpulse(S/N)` band-integration doesn't reproduce the matched-filter fluence's burst-to-burst scaling (zach/oran = 2.95 in my code vs 1.23 published) — the on-pulse-window definition vs the fitted matched-filter width.

The kernel physics is right; the SEFD *input* is the wrong one, and the data-driven integral needs reconciling with the matched filter. Note also a **data-hygiene flag**: the local detection-log TNS suffixes (`...207A/310A/506A`) disagree with the catalog/TNS (`...207C/310F/506D`) — same bursts by S/N, but the local CSV suffix looks wrong.

This directly bears on your "not convinced" on the diagnostic too: the per-channel integration has real issues, so the **absolute** energy can't rest on it. The **shape/slope** (γ_D) result is scale-independent, but your beam-model and negative-channel concerns remain to address separately.

> AGENT

The residual is now precisely located: my on-pulse crop is **11.9× wider than the catalog boxcar for zach** (5.96 ms vs 0.5 ms), 1.6× for whitney, 2.8× for oran. The decisive question for the window fix is whether zach's wide window is **real scattering tail** (these are scattered bursts — the catalog boxcar would under-count) or **crop runaway into noise**. Checking where zach's flux actually sits:

  "description": "Profile cumulative-flux check: scattering tail vs crop runaway"
}

> AGENT

Now the picture is complete and it's deeper than a window bug:

- **oran** is compact (95% of flux in ±0.5 ms) → my window ≈ catalog → matches (0.9×).
- **whitney** is also compact (98.7% in ±0.5 ms), yet 2.2× high — so the window is *not* the cause.
- **zach** has 58% central + a chunk at ±2–3 ms (crop reaching into structure/noise).

The real issue: my **linear band integral** `∫S dt dν` (the true fluence) and the **catalog's boxcar matched-filter fluence** are *different estimators*. For a peaked/structured burst they differ by the burst's structure factor (~1–3×) — not a constant, not a simple window crop. With SEFD_beam=167 Jy (8016/48) the gross 100× is fixed; the residual is this estimator difference. That's a methodology finding, not a coding bug.

Let me implement the decided SEFD_beam fix cleanly (it's unambiguous and the dominant correction), then I'll surface the estimator subtlety. Reading the current composing function:

=== tail of CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md ===
E_iso = 4*pi*D_L(z)^2 / (1+z) * F_nu * d_nu          (flat-spectrum form; the 1/(1+z) is the
                                                       bandwidth k-correction)
```

For a power law F ∝ nu^beta the k-correction generalizes to
`K = integral_rest nu^beta d_nu / integral_obs nu^beta d_nu` with nu_rest = (1+z) nu_obs.
Best practice for two bands is a **joint spectral fit on a common absolute (Jy) scale**, then one
integrated `E_iso` — *not* two independently-scaled per-band energies added together. FLITS
already does a joint fit; it just needs calibrated inputs. (z-from-DM via Macquart+ 2020,
Nature 581, 391, is not needed here — these sightlines have spectroscopic z.)

**Two concrete errors this surfaces in the current `burst_energies.tex`:** (i) it applies **no
`(1+z)`** k-correction; (ii) it **sums** two uncalibrated bands (compounding the Q2 problem).

(clusters contribute DM at Mpc impact; galaxies need <100 kpc for scattering) and the user
validated it — out of scope for this energetics review.

Plan updated through Phase 5c. I've reached a substantial milestone and a genuine phase boundary — pausing here for your direction before the heavy lift (5c-B re-fit needs new burstfit infrastructure + MCMC runs).

## Status — DSA calibration + absolute-scale audit complete

**Committed on `feature/radiometer-flux-cal` (8 commits):** kernel → S/N spectrum → σ_S inputs → pointing → SEFD → energetics wiring (5a) → real fluences + bandpass diagnostic (5b) → **coherent-beam SEFD fix + audit (5c-A, `8ca87f7`)**. Separate lanes untouched throughout.

**The absolute-scale audit landed cleanly.** The ~100× error was the SEFD: σ_S used the dsa110-rt **per-element** value (8016 Jy, verified = `compute_sefd_per_baseline`) but the data is the **coherent 48-antenna beam** → SEFD_beam = 8016/48 ≈ 167 Jy. Fluences are now physical (4.6–143 Jy·ms) and validated against Law et al. 2024 (zach 16.2 / whitney 26.2 / oran 13.2 Jy·ms, matched by Heimdall S/N). A factor-3 catalog-scale test now guards it.

**Two things remain open, both needing your call:**

**1. Estimator reconciliation (5c-A residual).** After the SEFD fix, a burst-dependent ~1–3× persists (oran 0.90×, whitney/zach 2.2×). I proved it's **not** a window bug — oran and whitney are both compact yet differ 2.4×. It's that my per-channel **linear integral** `∫S dt dν` and the catalog **boxcar matched-filter** are genuinely different estimators. Decision: which is canonical for E_iso (or report both)? My lean: the linear integral is the more complete fluence (captures scattered tail the boxcar misses), but the catalog is the published standard — worth reporting both with the ratio.

**2. The rigorous γ_D re-fit (5c-B) — you chose this, and it's the next real phase.** The right mechanism is cleaner than my proxy: feed the **flux-calibrated** spectrum to the fitter so its per-channel noise becomes σ_S(ν), which **down-weights the beam-edge channels** — exactly what the naive slope couldn't do. Catch: `BurstDataset` re-z-scores on load, so this needs a calibrated-input path into `burstfit` (modest infra) plus MCMC re-runs for the 5 railed bursts. That's a focused chunk of work.

Want me to (a) build 5c-B now, (b) settle the estimator question first, or (c) checkpoint here and resume 5c-B fresh? I'd recommend **(b) then (a)** — the estimator choice is quick and the re-fit is the scientifically decisive piece. Nothing ships until both are done (the E_iso gate stays closed).

    def __init__(
        self,
        time: NDArray[np.floating],
        freq: NDArray[np.floating],
        *,
        data: NDArray[np.floating] | None = None,
        dm_init: float = 0.0,
        df_MHz: float = 0.390625,  # 0.03051757812, #Channel width is needed for smearing
        beta: float = 2.0,
        noise_std: NDArray[np.floating] | None = None,
        off_pulse: slice | Sequence[int] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.time = np.asarray(time, dtype=float)
        self.freq = np.asarray(freq, dtype=float)
        self.df_MHz = float(df_MHz)

        if data is not None:
            self.data = np.asarray(data, dtype=float)
            if self.data.shape != (self.freq.size, self.time.size):
                raise ValueError("data must have shape (nfreq, ntime)")
        else:
            self.data = None

        self.dm_init = float(dm_init)
        self.beta = float(beta)

        if not np.allclose(np.diff(self.time), self.time[1] - self.time[0]):
            raise ValueError("time axis must be uniform")
        self.dt = self.time[1] - self.time[0]

        if noise_std is None and self.data is not None:
            self.noise_std = self._estimate_noise(off_pulse)
        else:
            self.noise_std = noise_std

        # Pre-calculate validity mask (exclude dead channels and NaNs)
        if self.data is not None and self.noise_std is not None:
            self.valid = (self.noise_std > 1e-9) & (np.isfinite(np.nanmean(self.data, axis=1)))
        else:
            self.valid = None

    def _dispersion_delay(
        self, dm_err: float = 0.0, ref_freq: float | None = None
    ) -> NDArray[np.floating]:
        if ref_freq is None:
            ref_freq = self.freq.max()
        return DM_DELAY_MS * dm_err * (self.freq**-self.beta - ref_freq**-self.beta)
