1.234e6) < 1 for r in rows)\n\n\ndef test_both_bands_emit(monkeypatch):\n    # Phase 7: both bands routed through the model-based radiometer integral (\"fluxcal\") -> the gate\n    # opens, E_iso is summed from two Jy integrals, the (1+z) k-correction identity holds exactly,\n    # and the propagated 1-sigma error column is finite and positive (stat c0 + SEFD/beam systematic).\n    monkeypatch.setattr(\n        E, \"joint_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz\", lambda n, band: 2.0e6 if band == \"C\" else 1.5e6\n    )\n    monkeypatch.setattr(E, \"joint_c0_gamma\", lambda n, band: (1.0, -3.0, 0.1))\n    rows = E.compute(scales={\"C\": \"fluxcal\", \"D\": \"fluxcal\"})\n    assert rows and all(\"E_iso_erg\" in r for r in rows)\n    r = rows[0]\n    assert abs(r[\"E_iso_erg\"] - r[\"E_iso_erg_no_kcorr\"] / (1.0 + r[\"z\"])) < 1e-9 * r[\"E_iso_erg\"]\n    assert r[\"I_CHIME_jy_ms_hz\"] == 2.0e6 and r[\"I_DSA_jy_ms_hz\"] == 1.5e6\n    assert np.isfinite(r[\"E_iso_erg_err\"]) and r[\"E_iso_erg_err\"] > 0\n\n\ndef test_mixed_scalar_and_fluxcal_opens_gate(monkeypatch):\n    # a legacy float scale on C plus the model-based integral on D also opens the gate\n    monkeypatch.setattr(E, \"joint_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz\", lambda n, band: 2.0e6)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(E, \"joint_c0_gamma\", lambda n, band: (1.0, -3.0, 0.1))\n    rows = E.compute(scales={\"C\": 5.0, \"D\": \"fluxcal\"})\n    assert rows and all(\"E_iso_erg\" in r for r in rows)\n    r = rows[0]\n    assert abs(r[\"E_iso_erg\"] - r[\"E_iso_erg_no_kcorr\"] / (1.0 + r[\"z\"])) < 1e-9 * r[\"E_iso_erg\"]\n    assert \"E_iso_CHIME_erg\" in r and \"E_iso_DSA_erg\" in r and r[\"I_DSA_jy_ms_hz\"] == 2.0e6\n\n\ndef test_dsa_burst_config_resolves():\n    # data-independent: the batch config maps nick -> the canonical .npy name + the fit's binning\n    from analysis.flux_cal import _dsa_burst_config\n\n    npy, f_factor, t_factor = _dsa_burst_config(\"chromatica\")\n    assert npy.name == \"chromatica_dsa_I_272_368_2500b_cntr_bpc.npy\"\n    assert f_factor == 384 and t_factor == 2\n"

3	\subsection{Isotropic-equivalent energies}
4	\label{sec:burst-energies}
5	
6	Isotropic-equivalent burst energies are pending absolute flux calibration. The
7	joint CHIME--DSA fit constrains each band's fluence spectrum only in the native
8	units of its input dynamic spectrum, and CHIME and DSA are not placed on a common
9	flux standard, so the per-band amplitudes are not directly comparable and may not
10	be summed into an energy. Converting to physical $\mathrm{Jy\,ms}$ requires each
11	telescope's system-equivalent flux density and primary-beam response at the burst
12	position (Andersen et~al.\ 2023 and the baseband CHIME/FRB catalog update for
13	CHIME; Law et~al.\ 2024 for DSA-110). Once those scales are supplied, the energy
14	follows $E_{\mathrm{iso}} = (4\pi D_L^2(z)/(1+z))\,[\,s_C\!\int F_C\,d\nu +
15	s_D\!\int F_D\,d\nu\,]$ with the $(1+z)$ bandwidth k-correction.

% Auto-generated by analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py -- do not hand-edit.
\subsection{Isotropic-equivalent energies}
\label{sec:burst-energies}

For each sightline with a spectroscopic host redshift we estimate the
isotropic-equivalent burst energy directly from the joint CHIME--DSA fit,
without extrapolating either band's spectrum beyond where it is constrained.
The joint fit returns a per-band spectral amplitude and index,
$F_X(\nu) = c_{0,X}\,(\nu/\nu_{\mathrm{ref},X})^{\gamma_X}$, which we put on
an absolute scale with each telescope's flux calibration $s_X$
($\mathrm{Jy}$ per native unit) and integrate over its own observing
band---CHIME over $0.400$--$0.800\,\mathrm{GHz}$ and DSA over
$1.311$--$1.499\,\mathrm{GHz}$,
%
\begin{equation}
E_{\mathrm{iso}} = \frac{4\pi D_L^2(z)}{1+z}\left[
  s_C\!\int_{\nu_1^{C}}^{\nu_2^{C}} F_{\mathrm{CHIME}}(\nu)\,d\nu
  + s_D\!\int_{\nu_1^{D}}^{\nu_2^{D}} F_{\mathrm{DSA}}(\nu)\,d\nu
\right],
\label{eq:eiso}
\end{equation}
%
with $D_L(z)$ from the fiducial \textit{Planck}\,2018 cosmology, the $(1+z)$
bandwidth k-correction applied, and
$1\,\mathrm{Jy\,ms\,Hz} = 10^{-29}\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-2}}$. Bursts whose hosts
lack a spectroscopic redshift are omitted. This band-restricted integral
constrains the energy released \emph{within the observed spectral envelope}: it
avoids the large, model-dependent extrapolation that a single power law fit
across the full $0.4$--$1.5\,\mathrm{GHz}$ span would require, at the cost of not
counting flux in the unobserved $0.8$--$1.3\,\mathrm{GHz}$ gap (so the values are
lower limits on the $0.4$--$1.5\,\mathrm{GHz}$ energy).

\begin{table}
\centering
\caption{Isotropic-equivalent energies of the co-detected FRBs, integrated over
the CHIME ($0.4$--$0.8\,\mathrm{GHz}$) and DSA ($1.31$--$1.50\,\mathrm{GHz}$) bands
from the joint scattering fit and put on an absolute scale with each band's flux
calibration. $\gamma_C,\gamma_D$ are the per-band spectral indices;
$E_{\mathrm{iso}}$ includes the $(1+z)$ k-correction. The quoted $1\sigma$
uncertainty combines the per-band $c_0$ posterior width with the absolute-scale
systematic (SEFD and primary-beam, $\sim\!0.25$ dex CHIME, $\sim\!0.20$ dex DSA),
added in quadrature across the two bands.}
\label{tab:burst-energies}
\begin{tabular}{lccccc}
\hline\hline
Burst & $z$ & $D_L$ [Mpc] & $\gamma_{C}$ & $\gamma_{D}$ & $E_{\mathrm{iso}}$ [erg] \\
\hline
  Chromatica & $0.0740$ & $346$ & $-3.74$ & $-4.98$ & $(1.73 \pm 0.62)\times10^{39}$ \\
  Hamilton & $0.3024$ & $1617$ & $-1.81$ & $-4.91$ & $(6.71 \pm 2.68)\times10^{39}$ \\
  Isha & $0.2505$ & $1304$ & $-4.82$ & $+0.95$ & $(4.20 \pm 2.51)\times10^{40}$ \\
  Oran & $0.3005$ & $1606$ & $-4.48$ & $-4.85$ & $(4.30 \pm 2.29)\times10^{40}$ \\
  Phineas & $0.2710$ & $1426$ & $-2.45$ & $-5.00$ & $(1.85 \pm 0.68)\times10^{40}$ \\
  Whitney & $0.4790$ & $2774$ & $-1.00$ & $+2.91$ & $(7.24 \pm 3.06)\times10^{40}$ \\
  Wilhelm & $0.5100$ & $2990$ & $+0.95$ & $-1.99$ & $(1.11 \pm 0.47)\times10^{41}$ \\
  Zach & $0.0430$ & $197$ & $-3.38$ & $-4.95$ & $(4.60 \pm 1.84)\times10^{38}$ \\

+\subsection{Isotropic-equivalent energies}
+\label{sec:burst-energies}
+
+For each sightline with a spectroscopic host redshift we estimate the
+isotropic-equivalent burst energy directly from the joint CHIME--DSA fit,
+without extrapolating either band's spectrum beyond where it is constrained.
+The joint fit returns a per-band spectral amplitude and index,
+$F_X(\nu) = c_{0,X}\,(\nu/\nu_{\mathrm{ref},X})^{\gamma_X}$, which we place on an
+absolute scale with each telescope's per-channel radiometer conversion
+$\sigma_{S,X}(\nu) = \mathrm{SEFD}_X(\nu)\,/\,[\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{pol}}\,\Delta\nu\,\Delta t}\,G_X(\nu)]$,
+taking the system-equivalent flux density and primary-beam gain $G_X$ from the
+DSA-110 \citep{Law2024} and CHIME/FRB \citep{CHIMEFRB2018,Michilli2021} flux
+scales, and integrate over each instrument's observing band---CHIME over
+$0.400$--$0.800\,\mathrm{GHz}$ and DSA over $1.311$--$1.499\,\mathrm{GHz}$,
+%
+\begin{equation}
+E_{\mathrm{iso}} = \frac{4\pi D_L^2(z)}{1+z}\left[
+  \int_{\nu_1^{C}}^{\nu_2^{C}} s_C\,F_{\mathrm{CHIME}}(\nu)\,d\nu
+  + \int_{\nu_1^{D}}^{\nu_2^{D}} s_D\,F_{\mathrm{DSA}}(\nu)\,d\nu
+\right],
+\label{eq:eiso}
+\end{equation}
+%
+with $D_L(z)$ from the fiducial \textit{Planck}\,2018 cosmology
+\citep{Planck2018}, the $(1+z)$ bandwidth k-correction applied, and
+$1\,\mathrm{Jy\,ms\,Hz} = 10^{-29}\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-2}}$. Bursts whose hosts lack
+a spectroscopic redshift are omitted. This band-restricted integral constrains
+the energy released \emph{within the observed spectral envelope}: it avoids the
+large, model-dependent extrapolation that a single power-law fit across the full
+$0.4$--$1.5\,\mathrm{GHz}$ span would require, at the cost of not counting flux in
+the unobserved $0.8$--$1.3\,\mathrm{GHz}$ gap, so the tabulated values are lower
+limits on the total $0.4$--$1.5\,\mathrm{GHz}$ energy
+(Table~\ref{tab:burst-energies}). The most distant sightline, Wilhelm
+($z=0.51$), reaches $E_{\mathrm{iso}}\simeq1.1\times10^{41}\,\mathrm{erg}$, at the
+luminous end of the co-detected sample.
+
+% TODO: swap internal nicknames (Chromatica, Hamilton, ...) for TNS names at submission.
+\begin{deluxetable*}{lccccc}
+\tablecaption{Isotropic-equivalent energies of the co-detected FRBs, integrated
+over the CHIME ($0.4$--$0.8\,\mathrm{GHz}$) and DSA ($1.31$--$1.50\,\mathrm{GHz}$)
+bands from the joint scattering fit and placed on an absolute scale with each
+band's radiometer flux calibration. $\gamma_C,\gamma_D$ are the per-band spectral
+indices; $E_{\mathrm{iso}}$ includes the $(1+z)$ k-correction. The quoted
+$1\sigma$ uncertainty combines the per-band $c_0$ posterior width with the
+absolute-scale systematic (SEFD and primary beam, ${\sim}0.25$ dex for CHIME and

=== module docstring (lines 1-30) ===
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Isotropic-equivalent energy E_iso for the co-detected FRB sample.

For each sightline with a spectroscopic host redshift and a joint CHIME+DSA
scattering fit, integrate the fitted fluence spectrum F(nu) = c0 (nu/nu_ref)^gamma
over each telescope's OWN observed band, convert each band to an ABSOLUTE Jy
scale, k-correct, and sum:

    E_iso = (4 pi D_L(z)^2 / (1+z)) [ s_C int_CHIME F_C dnu + s_D int_DSA F_D dnu ]

where s_C, s_D are the per-band flux scales (Jy per native .npy fluence unit;
`flux_jy_per_unit` in configs/telescopes.yaml).

Why the flux scale is mandatory (see analysis/burst_energies/CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md):
the joint fit recovers c0 in the input dynamic spectrum's NATIVE units, and CHIME
and DSA are not on a common flux standard. c0_C and c0_D are therefore in
independent, arbitrary per-telescope units. Summing two such bands is summing
dollars and yen: it is not an energy, and the per-burst CHIME:DSA mix varies, so
even the relative ORDERING of the total is unreliable. So this script refuses to
emit an energy until BOTH bands carry a real `flux_jy_per_unit` (from each
telescope's SEFD + beam response at the burst position). Until then it reports the
band fluence integrals in native units, flagged uncalibrated, and writes a
"pending calibration" LaTeX stub rather than a publishable table of fake erg.

The (1+z) bandwidth k-correction (Zhang 2018) is applied by default; the
no-k-correction value is tabulated alongside so the manuscript can state the
convention explicitly.

ref_freq is the band centre (f_min+f_max)/2; the fitter uses median(freq), which
equals the centre for a symmetric, uniformly-flagged band (small <~few% offset
```

3. **Beam vs astrophysics splits by on/off-axis.** On-axis **phineas** (G≈1.0, slope_s≈0) does NOT
   relax (-9.91 → -9.95): its steepness is astrophysical or a non-beam instrumental effect, NOT
   band-edge. **chromatica** (G=0.25) is so steep it pins at the -10 floor even calibrated — a
   beam-dominated near-total edge dropout (its +2.15 shift stays clipped).

**Implication for E_iso.** gamma_D as a free per-band index does not reliably recover an astrophysical
spectral index from the narrow (14%) DSA band — it is dominated by beam-edge sensitivity off-axis and
a residual steep falloff on-axis. So the energy estimate must NOT extrapolate the gamma_D power law;
the **calibrated per-channel fluence integral** (which integrates the measured channels directly) is
the robust estimator and is insensitive to the gamma rail. This reinforces the estimator decision
above.

Scope precisely:\n\n1. **Absolute-scale cross-check covers 3 sightlines, not all.** `test_joint_band_fluence_matches_catalog_scale`\n   compares the model-based DSA fluence to the Law+2024 catalog for **oran (0.99×), zach (1.27×), and\n   whitney (2.15×)** — the only co-detections with a published catalog fluence in the repo. The factor-of-3\n   test band is a sanity gate, not a tight constraint. Treat the absolute scale as validated to ~2×\n   for the 3 anchored bursts and model-trusted (no external check) for the rest.\n\n2. **Untested high model fluences exist but do not enter E_iso.** Some bursts carry large model-based\n   band-average fluences (mahi ≈ 468, freya ≈ 156 Jy·ms) with no catalog comparison. The per-source redshift quality (spectroscopic vs photometric) is inherited from the\n   galaxy-search `TARGETS` list and is **not** independently flagged here — any sightline later found\n   to have only a photometric/uncertain redshift should be demoted or annotated in the table.\n\n**Net:** the energies are correct given the model, catalog-anchored to ~2× for oran/zach/whitney, and\nband-restricted lower limits throughout. ### PR Review — Radiometer flux calibration → E_iso

- [x] Read core changed files (`flux_cal.py`, `chime_beam.py`, `calculate_burst_energies.py`, `dsa_beam.py`)
- [x] Check physics: units, frequency-ascending, bounds, k-correction
- [x] Check validation/gate logic
- [x] Check over-engineering / dead code (ponytail)
- [x] Post review

This is a careful, well-documented piece of work. The physics is sound, the unit bookkeeping checks out, the gate logic is conservative in the right direction, and the figure-review + validation gates are genuinely satisfied (both `figures.review.json` and `refit_calibrated.review.json` carry real per-figure `match` verdicts). I confirmed the most load-bearing assumption against the kernel rather than taking the docstring's word for it. Findings below are minor; **nothing blocks merge** and nothing relaxes the fit-validation contract.

#### Verified correct
- **Reference-frequency convention matches the kernel.** `flux_cal.py:280` uses `ref = np.median(freq_hz)` over the *full* channel grid, and `burstfit.py:718` confirms the fitter references `c0` to `np.median(self.freq)` (full grid, not valid-only). So `c0 (ν/ref)^γ` is reconstructed on the same scale the fit produced it. Good — this is exactly the thing that silently corrupts a calibration if it's off.
- **Units.** `σ_S [Jy] · (c0(ν/ref)^γ/noise_std) [S/N·ms]` integrated over `dν [Hz]` → `Jy·ms·Hz`, and `JY_MS_HZ_TO_SI = 1e-29` → J·m⁻². Self-consistent. The `1/(1+z)` bandwidth k-correction (`calculate_burst_energies.py:103`) is the standard Zhang-2018 convention and the identity `E = E_no_kcorr/(1+z)` is asserted in both `_check()` and the tests.
- **Frequency-ascending.** Both noise-grid loaders go through `BurstDataset` (ascending-standardized) and `np.trapezoid(..., freq_hz)` integrates over the ascending axis → positive. Correct.
- **Both-bands-or-nothing gate.** `calibrated = cal_C and cal_D` plus the live-config assert `(live["C"] is None) == (live["D"] is None)` (`:375`) cleanly refuses to sum two un-cross-calibrated bands. The RFI/`valid`-channel mask (`:261`) correctly excludes `noise_std≈0` channels that would otherwise blow up `c0/noise_std`. This is the right kind of paranoia.

#### Minor findings (non-blocking)

1. **Perf — beam cube reloaded per channel.** `dsa_beam.load_power_beam` reads the ~345 MB HDF5 cube and `beam_gain` rebuilds the `RegularGridInterpolator` on *every* call (`dsa_beam.py:77-79`), and `flux_cal.dsa_sigma_jy` calls it once per channel in a list comprehension (`flux_cal.py:83`). Only frequency varies across those calls (source position is fixed), so this re-reads the whole cube N_chan times per burst. Post-downsample channel counts are small so it's tolerable, but the fix is trivial and worth it: load the cube once and evaluate the interpolator on the full freq vector in one shot. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20analysis%2Fdsa_beam.py%20and%20analysis%2Fflux_cal.py%20on%20branch%20energetics-flux-cal%2C%20avoid%20reloading%20the%20345MB%20DSA110_beam_1.h5%20cube%20once%20per%20channel.%20dsa_sigma_jy%20calls%20beam_gain%20in%20a%20per-channel%20loop%3B%20refactor%20so%20load_power_beam%2FRegularGridInterpolator%20is%20built%20once%20and%20evaluated%20on%20the%20full%20freq%20vector.&repo=jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS)

2. **`np.nanmedian(ns[valid])` on a possibly-empty mask.** `_band_noise_grid` (`flux_cal.py:261`) computes `np.nanmedian(ns[valid])` where `valid` comes from `m.valid`; if a band were fully masked this is a `nanmedian` of an empty slice (RuntimeWarning → NaN → everything drops to invalid downstream). Not reachable for the current sample, but a one-line guard would make the failure explicit rather than a silent empty integral.

3. **Mixed `float` + `"fluxcal"` opens the gate.** `_band_jy` (`:127`) and the test `test_mixed_scalar_and_fluxcal_opens_gate` allow one band on a legacy float scalar and the other on `fluxcal` to produce a summed `E_iso`. The live config is `fluxcal`/`fluxcal` so this is moot in practice, but the gate's whole purpose is to prevent summing bands that aren't on a common physical scale — a bare float scalar isn't audited the way the radiometer path is. Worth a comment noting the float path is legacy-only, or tightening the gate to require both bands be `fluxcal`.

#### Ponytail note
Two fluence paths coexist: the data-driven `dsa_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz`/`sn_spectrum_from_npy` and the model-based `joint_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz`. Only the latter feeds `E_iso`; the former is used solely by `test_dsa_fluence_matches_catalog_scale` and `plot_bandpass_check.py`. That's defensible as an independent catalog cross-check (it's what gives you the "~2× of Law+2024" confidence), not dead code — but if the cross-check is a one-time validation rather than an ongoing guard, it's a candidate for pruning later.

#### Validation contract
No concerns. This PR is downstream of the fit-quality gate and does not touch `burstfit.py`, `classify_fit_quality`, or any PASS/MARGINAL/FAIL threshold. The energetics gate is additive and fails *closed*. The figure Stop-gate is satisfied with substantive verdicts.
 · branch `energetics-flux-cal`

### **CLEANUP 1: DSA beam cube reloaded per channel (CRITICAL - LIVE ROUTE)**

**Files:**

```python
def dsa_sigma_jy(freq_hz, dnu_hz, sefd_jy, dt_s, theta_deg, phi_deg, beam_gain_fn):
    """Per-channel radiometer noise sigma_S(nu) [Jy] for DSA (n_pol=2) at a beam offset."""
    g = np.array([beam_gain_fn(theta_deg, phi_deg, f / 1e9) for f in freq_hz])
    return radiometer_sigma_jy(sefd_jy, 2, dnu_hz, dt_s, g)
```

**And the beam_gain function (dsa_beam.py:71-79):**
```python
def beam_gain(theta_deg: float, phi_deg: float, freq_ghz: float, path: str | Path = DEFAULT_BEAM) -> float:
    """Normalized power-beam gain (boresight=1) at an offset, via trilinear interpolation."""
    from scipy.interpolate import RegularGridInterpolator
    fz, th, ph, P = load_power_beam(path)
    g = RegularGridInterpolator((fz, th, ph), P, bounds_error=False, fill_value=None)
    return float(g([[freq_ghz, theta_deg, np.mod(phi_deg, 360.0)]])[0])
```

**WHERE IT'S CALLED (live E_iso route):**
- `calculate_burst_energies.py`, lines 164-165 call `joint_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz()` for both bands when scales={"C":"fluxcal", "D":"fluxcal"}
- For band=="D" (DSA), line 288-290 in flux_cal.py calls `dsa_sigma_jy(..., beam_gain)`
- `dsa_sigma_jy` loops over freq_hz at line 83, calling `beam_gain()` once PER CHANNEL

**WASTEFUL BEHAVIOR: CONFIRMED**
- `dsa_sigma_jy` is called ONCE per burst (band D)
- It calls `beam_gain_fn` in a list comprehension: ~6160 times (one per DSA channel: 1.311-1.499 GHz at ~30 kHz resolution)
- Each `beam_gain()` call invokes `load_power_beam()`, which opens the 345 MB HDF5 file with `h5py.File` and reads all E-field arrays (lines 60-66)
- This means **~6160 full h5 file reads + decompression per burst** = ~2 TB of disk I/O per burst

**IS IT ON THE LIVE ROUTE?**
YES. The config at `/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/scratch/worktrees/flits-energetics/configs/telescopes.yaml` line 21 sets `dsa: flux_jy_per_unit: fluxcal`, which triggers `joint_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz("nick", "D")` → `dsa_sigma_jy()` → per-channel `beam_gain()` loop.

**MINIMAL FIX:**
Cache the loaded beam cube and interpolator at module level in dsa_beam.py:
```python
# At module top (after DEFAULT_BEAM assignment, ~line 53)
_BEAM_CACHE = {}

def _get_cached_interpolator(path=DEFAULT_BEAM):
    """Return cached (freq, theta, phi, P, interpolator) or load fresh."""
    path = Path(path)
    if path not in _BEAM_CACHE:
        fz, th, ph, P = load_power_beam(path)
        g = RegularGridInterpolator((fz, th, ph), P, bounds_error=False, fill_value=None)
        _BEAM_CACHE[path] = (fz, th, ph, P, g)
    return _BEAM_CACHE[path]

def beam_gain(theta_deg: float, phi_deg: float, freq_ghz: float, path: str | Path = DEFAULT_BEAM) -> float:
    """Normalized power-beam gain (boresight=1) at an offset, via trilinear interpolation."""
    _, _, _, _, g = _get_cached_interpolator(path)
    return float(g([[freq_ghz, theta_deg, np.mod(phi_deg, 360.0)]])[0])
```

Alternatively, use `@functools.lru_cache` on `load_power_beam()`:
```python

@lru_cache(maxsize=2)
def load_power_beam(path: str | Path = DEFAULT_BEAM):
    ...
```

### **CLEANUP 2: Empty-valid nanmedian guard (MINOR)**

**File:**
- `/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/scratch/worktrees/flits-energetics/analysis/flux_cal.py`, line 261

**Current code snippet:**
```python
valid = valid & np.isfinite(ns) & (ns > 1e-6 * np.nanmedian(ns[valid]))  # drop masked channels
```

**FRAGILE BEHAVIOR: CONFIRMED**
- Line 257-260 initialize `valid` based on `m.valid` or isfinite/positive checks
- Line 261 THEN updates `valid` using `ns[valid]` on the RHS
- If the initial `valid` is all-False (or becomes all-False from the isfinite/positive checks), then `ns[valid]` is an empty array
- `np.nanmedian([])` returns `nan` (after warning "All-NaN slice encountered")
- Then `ns > 1e-6 * nan` evaluates to all-False (correctly), but the warning pollutes stderr

**WHEN CAN THIS HAPPEN?**
- A burst with all channels RFI-masked (m.valid all-False)
- Or all channels with noise_std ≤ 0 or non-finite (unlikely, but defensive)

**MINIMAL FIX:**
Guard the nanmedian:
```python
median_val = np.nanmedian(ns[valid])
if np.isnan(median_val):
    valid = np.zeros_like(valid, dtype=bool)  # keep all-False, no warning
else:
    valid = valid & np.isfinite(ns) & (ns > 1e-6 * median_val)
```

Or one-liner:
```python
valid = valid & np.isfinite(ns) & (ns > 1e-6 * np.nanmedian(ns[valid]) if valid.any() else 0)
```

**TESTS THAT MUST STAY GREEN:**
- No explicit tests for edge case (all-valid or all-masked), but tests like `test_sn_spectrum_synthetic()` implicitly assume normal channel masks

**WORTH DOING:** YES, minor. Removes warning noise when processing problematic bursts.

### **CLEANUP 3: Mixed float/fluxcal gate logic (NOT WORTH TIGHTENING)**

**Files:**
- `/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/scratch/worktrees/flits-energetics/analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py`, lines 127-141 and 164-166
- `/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/scratch/worktrees/flits-energetics/tests/test_burst_energies_fluxcal.py`, lines 39-47

**Current code snippet (calculate_burst_energies.py:127-141):**
```python
def _band_jy(scale, i_native, nick, fluence_fn):
    """(I_jy_ms_hz or None, is_calibrated) for one band given its scale sentinel.
    scale is None -> uncalibrated; the string "fluxcal" -> data-driven per-channel radiometer
    integral (fluence_fn(nick), already in Jy*ms*Hz); a float -> legacy native-units power-law
    integral times a single Jy-per-native scalar.
    """
    if scale is None:
        return None, False
    if scale == "fluxcal":
        if fluence_fn is None:
            raise NotImplementedError("fluxcal selected but no fluence_fn supplied for this band")
        return float(fluence_fn(nick)), True
    return i_native * float(scale), True
```

**And the gate (line 164-166):**
```python
I_C_jy, cal_C = _band_jy(s_C, I_C, nick, lambda n: joint_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz(n, "C"))
I_D_jy, cal_D = _band_jy(s_D, I_D, nick, lambda n: joint_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz(n, "D"))
calibrated = cal_C and cal_D
```

**THE MIXED-SCALAR PATH: LEGACY BUT INTENTIONAL**
- `scale` can be `None` (uncalibrated) → `cal_X = False` → gate closed
- `scale` can be `"fluxcal"` (model-based radiometer) → `cal_X = True` if fluence_fn succeeds
- `scale` can be a **float** (legacy: c0 power-law * single scalar) → `cal_X = True` regardless of model
- Line 166: `calibrated = cal_C and cal_D` — gate opens ONLY when BOTH `cal_C` and `cal_D` are True

**TEST ASSERTION (test_burst_energies_fluxcal.py:39-47):**
```python
def test_mixed_scalar_and_fluxcal_opens_gate(monkeypatch):
    # a legacy float scale on C plus the model-based integral on D also opens the gate
    rows = E.compute(scales={"C": 5.0, "D": "fluxcal"})
    assert rows and all("E_iso_erg" in r for r in rows)
```

**BEHAVIOR CONFIRMED:**
- When `scales={"C": 5.0, "D": "fluxcal"}`, the gate DOES open and produces E_iso
- `_band_jy(5.0, I_C, nick, fn)` returns `(I_C * 5.0, True)` (line 140)
- `_band_jy("fluxcal", I_D, nick, fn)` returns `(fluence_fn(nick), True)` (line 139)
- `calibrated = True and True = True` → energy row emitted

**IS THIS USED ANYWHERE IN PRODUCTION?**
NO. The live config (`configs/telescopes.yaml` lines 21, 30) has BOTH `flux_jy_per_unit: fluxcal`. The mixed path is test-only, for regression checking the gate logic.

**TIGHTENING THE GATE: WOULD BREAK THE TEST**
If you required `both bands == "fluxcal"` (rejecting float scales), the assertion on line 44 would fail:
```python
# Hypothetical: only accept fluxcal, not float
if scale == "fluxcal":
    ...
    return float(fluence_fn(nick)), True
else:
    raise ValueError("only fluxcal allowed")  # <- breaks test
```

**IS IT WORTH KEEPING?**
YES, for backward compatibility and test clarity. The gate logic is:
> "Emit energy only when both bands are flux-calibrated (either via float legacy scale or fluxcal model-based). Do not sum bands on different native-unit scales."

The test explicitly verifies that *mixing* legacy and model-based scales is OK (as long as both have *some* Jy conversion). This is defensible: if one band has a measured/derived Jy scale (even scalar) and the other is model-based per-channel, summing them is legitimate as long as the gate ensures both are in Jy.

**WORTH DOING:** NO. The current gate is more general than needed for the live config, but it's tested, documented, and defensive. Tightening it would sacrifice that flexibility without a clear benefit since the live config won't trigger the mixed path anyway.

## RESEARCH REPORT: Can the FLITS catalog flux cross-check be widened?

**Verdict up front: No. The three bursts in the current CATALOG dict (zach/whitney/oran) are the only co-detections with a published DSA-110 catalog fluence in Jy·ms. Do not add any others — none of isha/phineas/wilhelm/hamilton/chromatica (nor freya/gertrude) has a published fluence anywhere.**

### (A) What Law+2024 Table 1 fluences are

- **Paper:** Law et al. 2024, *"Deep Synoptic Array Science: First FRB and Host Galaxy Catalog"* — arXiv:2307.03344, published ApJ 967, 29. (The repo comment "ApJ 967, 29" and the arXiv id are both correct.)
- **Table 1 columns:** FRB Name / alias | Time (MJD, topocentric @ 1530 MHz) | Location | S/N | **Fluence (Jy ms)** | DM (pc/cm³) | DM_ISM | Width (ms).
- **Units:** Jy·ms (confirmed in the column sub-header).
- **Estimator (caption, verbatim):** *"The DM and width maximize S/N of the brightest component; width corresponds to a temporal boxcar size. Fluence is measured from high-resolution data to contain 90% of the flux density."* So it is a **boxcar/S/N-maximizing matched-filter fluence capturing 90% of the flux density** — exactly the "boxcar matched-filter, biased low for scattered/tailed bursts" estimator the FLITS docstring and CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md already flag. This is *not* the linear band integral FLITS uses for E_iso, so the factor-of-3 sanity band (not equality) in the test is the right call.
- **Sample scope (decisive):** Table 1 is **11 FRBs total**, all detected during **science commissioning Feb–Oct 2022** (the HTML says "January to October 2022"). The full list with fluences: Zach 20220207C (16.2), Alex 20220307B (3.2), Whitney 20220310F (26.2), Mark 20220319D (8.0), Quincy 20220418A (4.2), Oran 20220506D (13.2), Jackie 20220509G (5.8), Ansel 20220825A (5.8), Elektra 20220914A (2.6), Etienne 20220920A (3.9), Juan 20221012A (5.1). Of these, only Zach/Whitney/Oran are FLITS co-detections; the other 8 are different sources.

**None.** The cross-check stays at exactly `{"zach": 16.2, "whitney": 26.2, "oran": 13.2}`.

Reasoning, with the disconfirming check applied:
1. **The only DSA-110 publication that tabulates per-burst fluences in Jy·ms is Law+2024 Table 1**, and it is restricted to the Feb–Oct 2022 commissioning window. Every FLITS co-detection outside that window (isha Nov-2022, wilhelm Dec-2022, phineas/freya 2023, hamilton Sep-2023, chromatica/mahi/casey 2024) is **structurally excluded** — it cannot be in that catalog.

Zero photometric, zero placeholder.** Five are directly traceable to a published spectrograph (Sharma+2024 DSA-110 catalog); one (wilhelm) to Keck/MOSFIRE (Connor+2024 v1 / Hussaini+2025); two (hamilton, chromatica) have NO published host paper — their repo z is an internal/unpublished value whose provenance I could not externally verify (medium-confidence spectroscopic by analogy, but unconfirmed).

### (A) Provenance table

| nickname | TNS name | repo z | spec/phot | evidence | confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| zach | FRB 20220207C | 0.0430 | **spectroscopic** | Sharma+2024 `dsa_frbs.csv`: instrument=**Keck/LRIS**, Gold, z=0.0433±0.0001 | high |
| whitney | FRB 20220310F | 0.4790 | **spectroscopic** | Sharma+2024: instrument=**Keck/LRIS**, Gold, z=0.478±0.0004 | high |

| wilhelm | FRB 20221203A | 0.5100 | **spectroscopic** | Connor+2024 (arXiv:2409.16952 **v1**): host observed Keck-I/**MOSFIRE**, Hα detected in 2D spectrum (Fig.); Hussaini+2025 ApJL DM-z table lists z=0.5100, coords 315.1295/72.0376 (match), src "Connor et al. 2025" | high (value), medium-high (note repo comment claims z~0.47 from Macquart — **superseded**) |

Sharma+2024 makes a blanket spectroscopic statement: redshifts "measured by jointly fitting the stellar continuum and nebular emission using pPXF," from Keck-I/LRIS, Keck-II/DEIMOS, and Palomar/DBSP. ### (B) Classification for table annotation

- **Spectroscopic, safe (6):** zach, whitney, oran, isha, phineas (Sharma+2024, Gold + named spectrograph); wilhelm (Keck/MOSFIRE, Connor+2024 v1).
- **Photometric, need demotion (0):** none found. A dedicated disconfirming search turned up no photometric host z among the 8.

- **Sole source of all 8 z values:** `galaxies/v2_0/config.py:16-29` — the `TARGETS` list, tuple format `(name, RA, Dec, z_frb)` (comment `config.py:15`). chromatica `:26`, hamilton `:24`, isha `:20`, oran `:19`, phineas `:22`, whitney `:18`, wilhelm `:21`, zach `:17`.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	"""DSA-110 primary-beam gain from the measured Jones E-field cube (DSA110_beam_1.h5).
3	
4	Stokes-I power beam P = |E_theta|^2 + |E_phi|^2 summed over the X and Y feeds,
5	normalized to boresight (theta=0) = 1 at each frequency. This is the relative
6	sensitivity at a burst's angular offset from the pointing centre -- the beam
7	attenuation factor G in the radiometer flux calibration
8	
9	    F = (S/N) * SEFD / ( sqrt(n_pol * dnu * dt) * G(theta, phi, nu) ).
10	
11	It replaces the analytic Airy-disk fallback in dsa110-continuum
12	(calibration/beam_model.py) with the measured/simulated dish pattern.
13	
14	Cube layout (N_freq, N_theta, N_phi):
15	  freq: 1.2-1.6 GHz, 41 pts. NOTE the HDF5 dataset is named `freq_Hz` and carries a
16	        `freq_units="MHz"` attr, but the stored values are 1.2-1.6 -- unambiguously
17	        GHz (idx 20 = 1.40 GHz, matching the dish's L-band). Both labels are wrong;
18	        the values are GHz. Covers the DSA fit band (1.311-1.499 GHz).
19	  theta: 0-180 deg (zenith angle), 1801 pts @ 0.1 deg; phi: 0-360 deg (azimuth), 73 pts.
20	
21	The absolute scale still needs the boresight SEFD, which is MEASURED per-day /
22	per-calibrator (not a constant) by the dsa110-rt SEFD dashboard
23	(github.com/dsa110/dsa110-rt, served on lxd110h23:5777); use the value nearest a
24	burst's epoch. See analysis/burst_energies/CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md.
25	"""
26	
27	from __future__ import annotations
28	
29	import os
30	from pathlib import Path
31	
32	import numpy as np
33	
34	
35	def _default_beam() -> Path:
36	    """First existing of $FLITS_DSA_BEAM, repo data/DSA110_beam_1.h5, ~/Downloads (back-compat).
37	
38	    The cube is ~345 MB and gitignored; the canonical stable location is the repo's data/ dir.
39	    Returns the canonical path even when absent so callers get a clear, repo-relative error.
40	    """
41	    repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
42	    canonical = repo / "data" / "DSA110_beam_1.h5"
43	    for p in (
44	        os.environ.get("FLITS_DSA_BEAM"),
45	        canonical,
46	        Path.home() / "Downloads" / "DSA110_beam_1.h5",
47	    ):
48	        if p and Path(p).exists():
49	            return Path(p)
50	    return canonical
51	
52	
53	DEFAULT_BEAM = _default_beam()
54	
55	
56	def load_power_beam(path: str | Path = DEFAULT_BEAM):
57	    """(freq_ghz, theta_deg, phi_deg, P) with P normalized to boresight=1 per frequency."""
58	    import h5py
59	
60	    with h5py.File(path, "r") as f:
61	        freq_ghz = f["freq_Hz"][:].astype(float)  # mislabeled units; values are GHz
62	        theta = f["theta_pts"][:].astype(float)  # deg
63	        phi = f["phi_pts"][:].astype(float)  # deg
64	        P = np.zeros((freq_ghz.size, theta.size, phi.size))
65	        for grp in ("X_pol_Efields", "Y-pol_Efields"):
66	            P += np.abs(f[f"{grp}/etheta"][:]) ** 2 + np.abs(f[f"{grp}/ephi"][:]) ** 2
67	    P /= P[:, 0, :].mean(axis=1)[:, None, None]  # boresight (theta=0) -> 1 at each freq
68	    return freq_ghz, theta, phi, P
69	
70	
71	def beam_gain(
72	    theta_deg: float, phi_deg: float, freq_ghz: float, path: str | Path = DEFAULT_BEAM
73	) -> float:
74	    """Normalized power-beam gain (boresight=1) at an offset, via trilinear interpolation."""
75	    from scipy.interpolate import RegularGridInterpolator
76	
77	    fz, th, ph, P = load_power_beam(path)
78	    g = RegularGridInterpolator((fz, th, ph), P, bounds_error=False, fill_value=None)
79	    return float(g([[freq_ghz, theta_deg, np.mod(phi_deg, 360.0)]])[0])
80	
81	
82	def _check(path: str | Path = DEFAULT_BEAM) -> None:
83	    if not Path(path).exists():
84	        print(f"self-check SKIP: beam cube not found at {path}")
85	        return
86	    fz, th, ph, P = load_power_beam(path)
87	    assert abs(P[:, 0, :].mean() - 1.0) < 1e-9, "boresight not normalized to 1"
88	    assert 1.2 <= fz.min() and fz.max() <= 1.6, ("freq axis not GHz?", fz.min(), fz.max())
89	    g0 = beam_gain(0.0, 0.0, 1.4, path)
90	    assert abs(g0 - 1.0) < 1e-6, g0  # boresight = 1
91	    g_hp = beam_gain(1.8, 0.0, 1.4, path)
92	    assert 0.2 < g_hp < 0.8, ("half-power radius off", g_hp)  # ~half power near FWHM/2
93	    g_far = beam_gain(5.0, 0.0, 1.4, path)
94	    assert g_far < g_hp, ("gain not falling off-axis", g_far, g_hp)
95	    print(
96	        f"self-check OK: boresight=1, gain(1.8deg,1.4GHz)={g_hp:.3f} (~half power), "
97	        f"gain(5deg)={g_far:.3f}; freq {fz.min():.2f}-{fz.max():.2f} GHz"
98	    )
99	
100	
101	if __name__ == "__main__":
102	    _check()
103

1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	"""Radiometer flux calibration: per-channel S/N -> Jy for FLITS dynamic spectra.
3	
4	FLITS data is per-channel z-scored S/N (scattering/scat_analysis/pipeline/io.py:131-146:
5	_bandpass_correct divides each channel by its own off-pulse mean/std and the loader keeps
6	"units as S/N"). Physical flux density is therefore one radiometer multiply away:
7	
8	    S_nu(nu,t) [Jy] = (S/N)(nu,t) * sigma_S(nu),
9	    sigma_S(nu) = SEFD(nu) / (sqrt(n_pol * dnu * dt) * G(theta,phi,nu)),
10	
11	with SEFD = 2 k_B T_sys / A_eff and G the beam gain (boresight=1). Dividing by the
12	per-channel off-pulse noise also cancels the bandpass gain, so the S/N spectrum (and hence
13	this calibration) is free of the band-edge rolloff that rails the fitted gamma_D.
14	
15	The band fluence integral (Jy*ms*Hz) returned here feeds
16	analysis/calculate_burst_energies.band_energy_erg with flux_scale=1 -- the per-channel scale
17	is already folded in. See docs/rse/specs/plan-radiometer-flux-cal.md.
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	import numpy as np
23	
24	
25	def radiometer_sigma_jy(sefd_jy, n_pol, dnu_hz, dt_s, g):
26	    """Per-sample radiometer noise [Jy]: SEFD / (sqrt(n_pol*dnu*dt) * G).
27	
28	    sefd_jy: system-equivalent flux density [Jy]; n_pol: summed polarisations;
29	    dnu_hz: channel bandwidth [Hz]; dt_s: sample time [s]; g: beam gain (boresight=1).
30	    """
31	    return sefd_jy / (np.sqrt(n_pol * dnu_hz * dt_s) * g)
32	
33	
34	def calibrated_band_integral_jy_ms_hz(sn_integrated, sigma_jy, freq_hz, dt_ms):
35	    """int_band [ sigma_S(nu) * dt_ms * sum_onpulse(S/N)(nu) ] dnu   [Jy*ms*Hz].
36	
37	    sn_integrated: per-channel sum over the on-pulse window of (data/noise_std) [dimensionless];
38	    sigma_jy: per-channel sigma_S [Jy]; freq_hz: ascending channel centres [Hz]; dt_ms: sample [ms].
39	    """
40	    chan_fluence_jy_ms = sigma_jy * dt_ms * sn_integrated  # [Jy*ms] per channel
41	    return float(np.trapezoid(chan_fluence_jy_ms, freq_hz))  # [Jy*ms*Hz]
42	
43	
44	def sn_spectrum_from_npy(inpath, telescope, f_factor=1, t_factor=1, onpulse_thresh=3.0):
45	    """Per-channel on-pulse S/N spectrum from a burst .npy via the FLITS loader.
46	
47	    Returns (freq_hz ascending, sn_integrated [per channel, sum over on-pulse of data/noise_std],
48	    dt_ms, dnu_hz). BurstDataset z-scores each channel (io.py:131-146), so model.data is already
49	    S/N; dividing by the full-window per-channel noise makes the unit explicit and robust to the
50	    downsample rescaling.
51	    """
52	    import sys
53	    from pathlib import Path
54	
55	    repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
56	    sys.path.insert(0, str(repo / "scattering"))  # io.py uses package-relative imports (..burstfit)
57	    from scat_analysis.config_utils import load_telescope_block
58	    from scat_analysis.pipeline.io import BurstDataset
59	
60	    tel = load_telescope_block(str(repo / "scattering" / "configs" / "telescopes.yaml"), telescope)
61	    ds = BurstDataset(
62	        inpath,
63	        inpath,
64	        telescope=tel,
65	        f_factor=f_factor,
66	        t_factor=t_factor,
67	        onpulse_crop=True,
68	        onpulse_thresh=onpulse_thresh,
69	    )
70	    m = ds.model
71	    noise = np.clip(m.noise_std, 1e-9, None)  # per-channel full-window noise (n_freq,)
72	    sn = m.data / noise[:, None]  # (n_freq, n_time_onpulse) signal-to-noise
73	    sn_integrated = np.nansum(sn, axis=1)  # sum over the cropped on-pulse window
74	    return m.freq * 1e9, sn_integrated, ds.dt_ms, ds.df_MHz * 1e6
75	
76	
77	def dsa_sigma_jy(freq_hz, dnu_hz, sefd_jy, dt_s, theta_deg, phi_deg, beam_gain_fn):
78	    """Per-channel radiometer noise sigma_S(nu) [Jy] for DSA (n_pol=2) at a beam offset.
79	
80	    beam_gain_fn(theta_deg, phi_deg, freq_ghz) -> normalized power-beam gain (boresight=1);
81	    dnu_hz is the channel bandwidth (downsampled ds.df_MHz*1e6), dt_s the sample time [s].
82	    """
83	    g = np.array([beam_gain_fn(theta_deg, phi_deg, f / 1e9) for f in freq_hz])
84	    return radiometer_sigma_jy(sefd_jy, 2, dnu_hz, dt_s, g)
85	
86	
87	def dsa_beam_offset(dec_src, dec_pointing):
88	    """(theta_deg, phi_deg) of the source from the DSA primary-beam boresight.
89	
90	    DSA-110 is a transit array: at the burst's meridian transit (HA~0) the boresight sits at the
91	    source RA, so the angular separation is exactly the declination difference; phi=0 (meridian).
92	    HA refinement (small E-W term) is out of scope -- see the plan.
93	    """
94	    return abs(dec_src - dec_pointing), 0.0
95	
96	
97	def burst_epoch_position(nick):
98	    """(mjd, ra_deg, dec_deg) for a burst nickname from configs/bursts.yaml."""
99	    from pathlib import Path
100	
101	    import yaml
102	
103	    b = yaml.safe_load(
104	        (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "configs" / "bursts.yaml").read_text()
105	    )
106	    e = b["bursts"][nick]
107	    return float(e["mjd"]), float(e["ra_deg"]), float(e["dec_deg"])
108	
109	
110	def _csv_lookup(filename, key, key_col="burst", val_col=None):
111	    import csv
112	    from pathlib import Path
113	
114	    p = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "analysis" / "burst_energies" / filename
115	    if not p.exists():
116	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{p} missing -- run the Phase 4 acquisition")
117	    for row in csv.DictReader(p.open()):
118	        if row[key_col] == key:
119	            return row[val_col]
120	    raise KeyError(f"{key} not in {p}")
121	
122	
123	def load_dsa_sefd(nick):
124	    """Measured DSA SEFD [Jy] nearest the burst epoch, from dsa_sefd.csv (Phase 4)."""
125	    return float(_csv_lookup("dsa_sefd.csv", nick, val_col="sefd_jy"))
126	
127	
128	def dsa_pointing_dec(nick):
129	    """DSA primary-beam pointing declination [deg] for a burst, from dsa_pointing.csv (Phase 4)."""
130	    return float(_csv_lookup("dsa_pointing.csv", nick, val_col="pointing_dec_deg"))
131	
132	
133	# DSA-110 formed its FRB detection beam by coherently combining 48 antennas in 2022
134	# (Law et al. 2024, arXiv:2307.03344). The dsa110-rt SEFD store is PER-BASELINE (~per-element;
135	# estimate_sefd.py:compute_sefd_per_baseline), so the coherent-beam SEFD is SEFD_element / N_ant.
136	# Cross-check: this beam SEFD (~167 Jy) reproduces the catalog fluences (16.2/26.2/13.2 Jy*ms for
137	# zach/whitney/oran) to within the ~2x boxcar-vs-full-integral estimator difference; the empirical
138	# matched-filter anchor is ~234 Jy (=> effective N_eff~34, ~70% beamforming efficiency).
139	DSA_N_ANT = 48
140	
141	
142	def load_dsa_sefd_beam(nick):
143	    """Coherent-beam SEFD [Jy] = per-element dashboard SEFD / N_ant (the detection beam)."""
144	    return load_dsa_sefd(nick) / DSA_N_ANT
145	
146	
147	def _dsa_burst_config(nick):
148	    """(npy_path, f_factor, t_factor) from configs/batch/dsa/<nick>_dsa.yaml (the fit's own binning)."""
149	    from pathlib import Path
150	
151	    import yaml
152	
153	    cfg = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "configs" / "batch" / "dsa" / f"{nick}_dsa.yaml"
154	    if not cfg.exists():
155	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{cfg} missing -- no DSA batch config for {nick}")
156	    c = yaml.safe_load(cfg.read_text())
157	    return (cfg.parent / c["path"]).resolve(), int(c.get("f_factor", 1)), int(c.get("t_factor", 1))
158	
159	
160	def dsa_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz(nick):
161	    """Calibrated DSA-band fluence integral [Jy*ms*Hz] for a burst (Phases 2-3 composed).
162	
163	    Loads the burst .npy via its batch config (same f/t binning the joint fit used), turns the
164	    per-channel on-pulse S/N spectrum into Jy with sigma_S(nu)=SEFD_beam/(sqrt(2*dnu*dt)*G(theta,nu)),
165	    and integrates over the DSA band. SEFD_beam is the COHERENT-beam SEFD (per-element / N_ant);
166	    using the per-element SEFD directly over-estimates the fluence by ~N_ant. Raises
167	    FileNotFoundError if the .npy is not staged locally (data/dsa/ is external -- iacobus:burst_npys).
168	    """
169	    from analysis.dsa_beam import beam_gain
170	
171	    npy, f_factor, t_factor = _dsa_burst_config(nick)
172	    if not npy.exists():
173	        raise FileNotFoundError(
174	            f"{npy} not materialized -- stage the DSA .npy (iacobus:burst_npys) under data/dsa/"
175	        )
176	    freq_hz, sn_int, dt_ms, dnu_hz = sn_spectrum_from_npy(npy, "dsa", f_factor, t_factor)
177	    _mjd, _ra, dec_src = burst_epoch_position(nick)
178	    theta, phi = dsa_beam_offset(dec_src, dsa_pointing_dec(nick))
179	    sigma_jy = dsa_sigma_jy(
180	        freq_hz, dnu_hz, load_dsa_sefd_beam(nick), dt_ms / 1e3, theta, phi, beam_gain
181	    )
182	    return calibrated_band_integral_jy_ms_hz(sn_int, sigma_jy, freq_hz, dt_ms)
183	
184	
185	def _band_burst_config(nick, band):
186	    """(npy_path, f_factor, t_factor, telescope) from the band's batch config (band 'C'|'D')."""
187	    from pathlib import Path
188	
189	    import yaml
190	
191	    tel = {"C": "chime", "D": "dsa"}[band]
192	    cfg = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "configs" / "batch" / tel / f"{nick}_{tel}.yaml"
193	    if not cfg.exists():
194	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{cfg} missing -- no {tel} batch config for {nick}")
195	    c = yaml.safe_load(cfg.read_text())
196	    return (
197	        (cfg.parent / c["path"]).resolve(),
198	        int(c.get("f_factor", 1)),
199	        int(c.get("t_factor", 1)),
200	        tel,
201	    )
202	
203	
204	def joint_c0_gamma(nick, band):
205	    """(c0, gamma, c0_frac_err) for a band from the joint fit JSON (band 'C'|'D').
206	
207	    c0_frac_err is the mean of the asymmetric 16/84 half-widths over the median -- the statistical
208	    amplitude (hence fluence) uncertainty that propagates into the energy.
209	    """
210	    import json
211	    from pathlib import Path
212	
213	    p = (
214	        Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
215	        / "analysis"
216	        / "scattering-refit-2026-06"
217	        / "joint_json"
218	        / f"{nick}_joint_fit.json"
219	    )
220	    if not p.exists():
221	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{p} missing -- no joint fit for {nick}")
222	    pct = json.loads(p.read_text())["percentiles"]
223	    e = pct[f"c0_{band}"]
224	    c0 = e["median"]
225	    frac = 0.5 * (e["err_plus"] + e["err_minus"]) / c0 if c0 else float("nan")
226	    return c0, pct[f"gamma_{band}"]["median"], frac
227	
228	
229	def _band_noise_grid(npy, telescope, f_factor, t_factor):
230	    """(freq_hz, noise_std, dt_ms, dnu_hz, valid) loaded exactly as the joint fit did (crop, pad 0.5).
231	
232	    Matching onpulse_pad_factor=0.5 is essential: c0 is in the joint fit's bandpass-normalized data
233	    units, so the per-channel noise_std used to convert it to S/N must come from that same window.
234	    `valid` is the per-channel mask the fit actually used: RFI-masked channels have noise_std ~ 0 and
235	    must be excluded (else c0/noise_std explodes), so the integral runs over the SAME channels as the fit.
236	    """
237	    import sys
238	    from pathlib import Path
239	
240	    repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
241	    sys.path.insert(0, str(repo / "scattering"))
242	    from scat_analysis.config_utils import load_telescope_block
243	    from scat_analysis.pipeline.io import BurstDataset
244	
245	    tel = load_telescope_block(str(repo / "scattering" / "configs" / "telescopes.yaml"), telescope)
246	    ds = BurstDataset(
247	        npy,
248	        npy,
249	        telescope=tel,
250	        f_factor=f_factor,
251	        t_factor=t_factor,
252	        onpulse_crop=True,
253	        onpulse_pad_factor=0.5,
254	    )
255	    m = ds.model
256	    ns = m.noise_std
257	    if m.valid is not None:
258	        valid = m.valid if m.valid.ndim == 1 else np.any(m.valid, axis=1)
259	    else:
260	        valid = np.isfinite(ns) & (ns > 0)
261	    valid = valid & np.isfinite(ns) & (ns > 1e-6 * np.nanmedian(ns[valid]))  # drop masked channels
262	    return m.freq * 1e9, ns, ds.dt_ms, ds.df_MHz * 1e6, valid
263	
264	
265	def joint_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz(nick, band):
266	    """Model-based calibrated band fluence [Jy*ms*Hz] from the joint fit (band 'C'|'D').
267	
268	        F = int sigma_S(nu) * [ c0 (nu/ref)^gamma / noise_std(nu) ] dnu.
269	
270	    The bracket is int(S/N) dt per channel: int(model)dt = c0 for the area-conserving scattering
271	    kernel (verified -- tail-complete, no on-pulse window to tune), and dividing by the joint fit's
272	    per-channel noise_std converts its bandpass-normalized c0 to S/N units (noise_std ~ 0.04, not 1).
273	    sigma_S is the DSA measured-beam or CHIME documented-cylinder-beam radiometer noise (n_pol=2).
274	    """
275	    npy, ff, tf, tel = _band_burst_config(nick, band)
276	    if not npy.exists():
277	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{npy} not materialized -- stage the {tel} .npy under data/{tel}/")
278	    c0, gamma, _frac = joint_c0_gamma(nick, band)
279	    freq_hz, noise_std, dt_ms, dnu_hz, valid = _band_noise_grid(npy, tel, ff, tf)
280	    ref = np.median(freq_hz)  # the fit references c0 to the median of the FULL channel grid
281	    fz, ns = freq_hz[valid], noise_std[valid]  # integrate over the channels the fit used
282	    amp_sn = c0 * (fz / ref) ** gamma / ns  # int(S/N) dt per valid channel [S/N*ms]
283	    if band == "D":
284	        from analysis.dsa_beam import beam_gain
285	
286	        _mjd, _ra, dec = burst_epoch_position(nick)
287	        theta, phi = dsa_beam_offset(dec, dsa_pointing_dec(nick))
288	        sigma_jy = dsa_sigma_jy(
289	            fz, dnu_hz, load_dsa_sefd_beam(nick), dt_ms / 1e3, theta, phi, beam_gain
290	        )
291	    else:  # CHIME baseband: beam formed at the source -> G ~ 1
292	        from analysis.chime_beam import chime_sigma_jy, load_chime_sefd
293	
294	        sigma_jy = chime_sigma_jy(fz, dnu_hz, load_chime_sefd(), dt_ms / 1e3, g=1.0)
295	    return float(np.trapezoid(sigma_jy * amp_sn, fz))
296	
297	
298	def _check() -> None:
299	    # 1. radiometer noise vs analytic: 2000/sqrt(2*1e6*1e-3) == sqrt(2000); G=0.5 doubles it
300	    s = radiometer_sigma_jy(2000.0, 2, 1e6, 1e-3, 1.0)
301	    assert abs(s - np.sqrt(2000.0)) < 1e-9, s
302	    assert abs(radiometer_sigma_jy(2000.0, 2, 1e6, 1e-3, 0.5) - 2.0 * s) < 1e-9
303	    # 2. flat-band integral oracle: trapz(const) == const*(nu2-nu1)
304	    freq_hz = np.linspace(1.311e9, 1.499e9, 64)
305	    i_band = calibrated_band_integral_jy_ms_hz(
306	        np.full(64, 3.0), np.full(64, 5.0), freq_hz, 0.131072
307	    )
308	    oracle = 3.0 * 5.0 * 0.131072 * (freq_hz[-1] - freq_hz[0])
309	    assert abs(i_band - oracle) / oracle < 1e-9, (i_band, oracle)
310	    print("self-check OK: radiometer noise + flat-band integral match analytic oracles")
311	
312	
313	if __name__ == "__main__":
314	    _check()
315

1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	"""Isotropic-equivalent energy E_iso for the co-detected FRB sample.
3	
4	For each sightline with a spectroscopic host redshift and a joint CHIME+DSA
5	scattering fit, integrate the fitted fluence spectrum F(nu) = c0 (nu/nu_ref)^gamma
6	over each telescope's OWN observed band, convert each band to an ABSOLUTE Jy
7	scale, k-correct, and sum:
8	
9	    E_iso = (4 pi D_L(z)^2 / (1+z)) [ s_C int_CHIME F_C dnu + s_D int_DSA F_D dnu ]
10	
11	where s_C, s_D are the per-band flux scales (`flux_jy_per_unit` in
12	configs/telescopes.yaml). The live setting is "fluxcal": each band's absolute Jy
13	integral is computed per channel by the radiometer conversion in
14	analysis/flux_cal.joint_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz (sigma_S(nu) folded in), not a
15	single Jy-per-native scalar. A float scale (the legacy native-units * scalar
16	path) and None (uncalibrated) are still accepted.
17	
18	Why the flux scale is mandatory (see analysis/burst_energies/CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md):
19	the joint fit recovers c0 in the input dynamic spectrum's NATIVE units, and CHIME
20	and DSA are not on a common flux standard. c0_C and c0_D are therefore in
21	independent, arbitrary per-telescope units. Summing two such bands is summing
22	dollars and yen: it is not an energy, and the per-burst CHIME:DSA mix varies, so
23	even the relative ORDERING of the total is unreliable. So this script refuses to
24	emit an energy until BOTH bands carry a real `flux_jy_per_unit` (from each
25	telescope's SEFD + beam response at the burst position). Until then it reports the
26	band fluence integrals in native units, flagged uncalibrated, and writes a
27	"pending calibration" LaTeX stub rather than a publishable table of fake erg.
28	
29	The (1+z) bandwidth k-correction (Zhang 2018) is applied by default; the
30	no-k-correction value is tabulated alongside so the manuscript can state the
31	convention explicitly.
32	
33	ref_freq is the band centre (f_min+f_max)/2; the fitter uses median(freq), which
34	equals the centre for a symmetric, uniformly-flagged band (small <~few% offset
35	under asymmetric channel flagging -> minor vs the calibration systematic).
36	
37	Usage:  python analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py [--check]
38	"""
39

61	JY_MS_HZ_TO_SI = 1e-29  # 1 Jy*ms*Hz = 1e-29 J*m^-2
62	J_TO_ERG = 1e7
63	PLACEHOLDER_Z = 1.0  # Freya/Mahi/Johndoeii carry z=1.0000 as a "redshift unknown" flag

65	# Per-band absolute-scale systematic [dex], folded into the energy error. DSA: measured beam +
66	# coherent-beam SEFD (N_ant=48) assumption; CHIME: documented cylinder beam + derived SEFD

68	BAND_SYS_DEX = {"C": 0.25, "D": 0.20}

71	def band_edges_hz() -> dict[str, tuple[float, float, float]]:
72	    """(nu1, nu2, nu_ref) in Hz per band from the instrument config (band centre = ref)."""
73	    cfg = yaml.safe_load(TEL_CFG.read_text())
74	    out = {}

88	def band_integral(c0: float, gamma: float, nu_ref: float, nu1: float, nu2: float) -> float:
89	    """int_{nu1}^{nu2} c0 (nu/nu_ref)^gamma dnu  [native*ms*Hz], freqs in Hz."""
90	    if abs(gamma + 1.0) < 1e-9:  # power law -> 1/nu, integral is a log
91	        return c0 * nu_ref * np.log(nu2 / nu1)
92	    g = gamma + 1.0
93	    return c0 * nu_ref / g * ((nu2 / nu_ref) ** g - (nu1 / nu_ref) ** g)
94	
95	
96	def band_energy_erg(
97	    i_raw: float, flux_scale: float, d_l_m: float, z: float, kcorr: bool = True
98	) -> float:
99	    """Band fluence integral [native*ms*Hz] x flux scale [Jy/native] -> E [erg].
100	
101	    (1+z) bandwidth k-correction (Zhang 2018, ApJ 867 L21) applied when kcorr=True.
102	    """
103	    factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + z) if kcorr else 1.0
104	    return 4.0 * np.pi * d_l_m**2 * i_raw * flux_scale * JY_MS_HZ_TO_SI * J_TO_ERG * factor

129	
130	    scale is None -> uncalibrated; the string "fluxcal" -> data-driven per-channel radiometer
131	    integral (fluence_fn(nick), already in Jy*ms*Hz); a float -> legacy native-units power-law
132	    integral times a single Jy-per-native scalar.
133	    """
134	    if scale is None:
135	        return None, False
136	    if scale == "fluxcal":

152	
153	    rows = []
154	    for nick in sorted(fits):
155	        z = zs.get(nick)
156	        if z is None or abs(z - PLACEHOLDER_Z) < 1e-6:
157	            continue  # no real host redshift -> cannot place a distance
158	        fp = fits[nick]

160	
161	        I_C = band_integral(fp["c0_C"], fp["gamma_C"], ref_C, nu1_C, nu2_C)
162	        I_D = band_integral(fp["c0_D"], fp["gamma_D"], ref_D, nu1_D, nu2_D)
163	
164	        I_C_jy, cal_C = _band_jy(s_C, I_C, nick, lambda n: joint_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz(n, "C"))
165	        I_D_jy, cal_D = _band_jy(s_D, I_D, nick, lambda n: joint_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz(n, "D"))
166	        calibrated = cal_C and cal_D
167	
168	        row = {
169	            "burst": nick,
170	            "z": z,
171	            "D_L_Mpc": COSMO.luminosity_distance(z).to(u.Mpc).value,
172	            "c0_C": fp["c0_C"],
173	            "gamma_C": fp["gamma_C"],
174	            "c0_D": fp["c0_D"],
175	            "gamma_D": fp["gamma_D"],
176	            "I_CHIME_native_ms_Hz": I_C,  # band fluence integral, NATIVE units
177	            "I_DSA_native_ms_Hz": I_D,
178	            "calibrated": calibrated,
179	        }
180	        if I_C_jy is not None:
181	            row["I_CHIME_jy_ms_hz"] = I_C_jy
182	        if I_D_jy is not None:
183	            row["I_DSA_jy_ms_hz"] = I_D_jy
184	        if calibrated:

187	            e_C0 = band_energy_erg(I_C_jy, 1.0, d_l_m, z, kcorr=False)
188	            e_D0 = band_energy_erg(I_D_jy, 1.0, d_l_m, z, kcorr=False)
189	            # Per-band fractional error: c0 posterior width (statistical) (+) absolute-scale
190	            # systematic (SEFD+beam, lognormal sigma = ln10*dex). Bands independent -> quadrature.
191	            err = {}
192	            for tag, e_band in (("C", e_C), ("D", e_D)):
193	                f_stat = joint_c0_gamma(nick, tag)[2]  # c0 fractional posterior width
194	                f_sys = np.log(10.0) * BAND_SYS_DEX[tag]
195	                err[tag] = e_band * np.hypot(f_stat, f_sys)
196	            row.update(

201	                E_iso_erg=e_C + e_D,  # legitimate: both bands now in Jy
202	                E_iso_erg_no_kcorr=e_C0 + e_D0,
203	                E_iso_erg_err=float(np.hypot(err["C"], err["D"])),
204	            )
205	        rows.append(row)
206	    return rows

247	def _tex_pow(x: float) -> str:
248	    r"""Render a float as a\times10^{b} for LaTeX."""
249	    if x <= 0 or not np.isfinite(x):
250	        return r"\mathrm{n/a}"
251	    exp = int(np.floor(np.log10(x)))
252	    mant = x / 10**exp
253	    return rf"{mant:.2f}\times10^{{{exp}}}"
254	
255	
256	def _tex_val_err(x: float, dx: float) -> str:
257	    r"""Render x +/- dx sharing one mantissa exponent: (a \pm b)\times10^{c}."""
258	    if x <= 0 or not np.isfinite(x):
259	        return r"\mathrm{n/a}"
260	    exp = int(np.floor(np.log10(x)))
261	    return rf"({x / 10**exp:.2f} \pm {dx / 10**exp:.2f})\times10^{{{exp}}}"
262

264	def latex_pending() -> str:
265	    """LaTeX stub written while the flux calibration is missing (no fake energies)."""
266	    return r"""% Auto-generated by analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py -- do not hand-edit.

268	\subsection{Isotropic-equivalent energies}
269	\label{sec:burst-energies}
270	
271	Isotropic-equivalent burst energies are pending absolute flux calibration. The
272	joint CHIME--DSA fit constrains each band's fluence spectrum only in the native
273	units of its input dynamic spectrum, and CHIME and DSA are not placed on a common
274	flux standard, so the per-band amplitudes are not directly comparable and may not
275	be summed into an energy. Converting to physical $\mathrm{Jy\,ms}$ requires each
276	telescope's system-equivalent flux density and primary-beam response at the burst
277	position (Andersen et~al.\ 2023 and the baseband CHIME/FRB catalog update for
278	CHIME; Law et~al.\ 2024 for DSA-110). Once those scales are supplied, the energy
279	follows $E_{\mathrm{iso}} = (4\pi D_L^2(z)/(1+z))\,[\,s_C\!\int F_C\,d\nu +
280	s_D\!\int F_D\,d\nu\,]$ with the $(1+z)$ bandwidth k-correction.
281	"""

283	
284	def latex_section(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
285	    body = []
286	    for r in rows:

288	            f"  {r['burst'].capitalize()} & ${r['z']:.4f}$ & ${r['D_L_Mpc']:.0f}$ & "

290	            f"${_tex_val_err(r['E_iso_erg'], r['E_iso_erg_err'])}$ \\\\"
291	        )
292	    table_body = "\n".join(body)
293	    return rf"""% Auto-generated by analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py -- do not hand-edit.
294	\subsection{{Isotropic-equivalent energies}}
295	\label{{sec:burst-energies}}
296	
297	For each sightline with a spectroscopic host redshift we estimate the
298	isotropic-equivalent burst energy directly from the joint CHIME--DSA fit,
299	without extrapolating either band's spectrum beyond where it is constrained.
300	The joint fit returns a per-band spectral amplitude and index,
301	$F_X(\nu) = c_{{0,X}}\,(\nu/\nu_{{\mathrm{{ref}},X}})^{{\gamma_X}}$, which we put on
302	an absolute scale with each telescope's flux calibration $s_X$
303	($\mathrm{{Jy}}$ per native unit) and integrate over its own observing
304	band---CHIME over $0.400$--$0.800\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$ and DSA over
305	$1.311$--$1.499\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$,
306	%
307	\begin{{equation}}
308	E_{{\mathrm{{iso}}}} = \frac{{4\pi D_L^2(z)}}{{1+z}}\left[
309	  s_C\!\int_{{\nu_1^{{C}}}}^{{\nu_2^{{C}}}} F_{{\mathrm{{CHIME}}}}(\nu)\,d\nu
310	  + s_D\!\int_{{\nu_1^{{D}}}}^{{\nu_2^{{D}}}} F_{{\mathrm{{DSA}}}}(\nu)\,d\nu
311	\right],
312	\label{{eq:eiso}}
313	\end{{equation}}
314	%
315	with $D_L(z)$ from the fiducial \textit{{Planck}}\,2018 cosmology, the $(1+z)$
316	bandwidth k-correction applied, and
317	$1\,\mathrm{{Jy\,ms\,Hz}} = 10^{{-29}}\,\mathrm{{J\,m^{{-2}}}}$. Bursts whose hosts
318	lack a spectroscopic redshift are omitted. This band-restricted integral
319	constrains the energy released \emph{{within the observed spectral envelope}}: it
320	avoids the large, model-dependent extrapolation that a single power law fit
321	across the full $0.4$--$1.5\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$ span would require, at the cost of not
322	counting flux in the unobserved $0.8$--$1.3\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$ gap (so the values are
323	lower limits on the $0.4$--$1.5\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$ energy).
324	
325	\begin{{table}}
326	\centering
327	\caption{{Isotropic-equivalent energies of the co-detected FRBs, integrated over
328	the CHIME ($0.4$--$0.8\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$) and DSA ($1.31$--$1.50\,\mathrm{{GHz}}$) bands
329	from the joint scattering fit and put on an absolute scale with each band's flux
330	calibration. $\gamma_C,\gamma_D$ are the per-band spectral indices;
331	$E_{{\mathrm{{iso}}}}$ includes the $(1+z)$ k-correction. The quoted $1\sigma$
332	uncertainty combines the per-band $c_0$ posterior width with the absolute-scale
333	systematic (SEFD and primary-beam, $\sim\!0.25$ dex CHIME, $\sim\!0.20$ dex DSA),
334	added in quadrature across the two bands.}}
335	\label{{tab:burst-energies}}
336	\begin{{tabular}}{{lccccc}}
337	\hline\hline
338	Burst & $z$ & $D_L$ [Mpc] & $\gamma_{{C}}$ & $\gamma_{{D}}$ & $E_{{\mathrm{{iso}}}}$ [erg] \\
339	\hline
340	{table_body}
341	\hline
342	\end{{tabular}}
343	\end{{table}}
344	"""
345	
346	
347	def _check() -> None:
348	    # 1. closed-form band integral must match a dense numeric quadrature
349	    nu1, nu2, ref = 0.4e9, 0.8e9, 0.6e9
350	    for c0, g in ((2.0, -3.4), (0.18, -4.95), (1.0, -1.0), (3.0, 0.5)):
351	        nu = np.linspace(nu1, nu2, 200_001)
352	        num = np.trapezoid(c0 * (nu / ref) ** g, nu)
353	        ana = band_integral(c0, g, ref, nu1, nu2)
354	        assert abs(ana - num) / abs(num) < 1e-6, (c0, g, ana, num)
355	
356	    # 2. oracle: flat spectrum (gamma=0, c0=1) over a known band, scale=1, gives the
357	    #    analytic energy; (1+z) divides it; doubling the flux scale doubles it.
358	    i_flat = band_integral(1.0, 0.0, ref, nu1, nu2)
359	    assert abs(i_flat - (nu2 - nu1)) < 1e-3, i_flat  # int 1 dnu = bandwidth
360	    e0 = band_energy_erg(i_flat, 1.0, d_l_m=1.0, z=0.0)
361	    assert abs(e0 - 4.0 * np.pi * (nu2 - nu1) * JY_MS_HZ_TO_SI * J_TO_ERG) < 1e-6 * e0
362	    assert abs(band_energy_erg(i_flat, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) - e0 / 2.0) < 1e-9 * e0  # (1+z)=2
363	    assert abs(band_energy_erg(i_flat, 2.0, 1.0, 0.0) - 2.0 * e0) < 1e-9 * e0  # linear in scale
364	
365	    # 3. the gate itself, both directions (inject scales; independent of the live config)
366	    assert not any("E_iso_erg" in r for r in compute(scales={"C": None, "D": 1.0})), (
367	        "partial calibration leaked an energy"
368	    )
369	    cal_rows = compute(scales={"C": 1.0, "D": 1.0})
370	    assert cal_rows and all("E_iso_erg" in r for r in cal_rows), "calibrated run emitted no energy"
371	    r = cal_rows[0]
372	    assert abs(r["E_iso_erg"] - r["E_iso_erg_no_kcorr"] / (1.0 + r["z"])) < 1e-9 * r["E_iso_erg"]
373	    # and the live config must not be half-set (would silently drop one band's flux)
374	    live = flux_scales()
375	    assert (live["C"] is None) == (live["D"] is None), (
376	        "telescopes.yaml: calibrate both bands or neither"
377	    )
378	    print("self-check OK: integral matches quadrature; energy oracle, k-correction, and gate exact")
379	
380	
381	def main() -> None:
382	    if "--check" in sys.argv:
383	        _check()
384	        return
385	
386	    rows = compute()
387	    if not rows:
388	        sys.exit("no bursts with both a real redshift and a joint c0/gamma fit")
389	
390	    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
391	    (OUT_DIR / "burst_energies.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2))
392	    calibrated = rows[0]["calibrated"]
393	    tex = latex_section(rows) if calibrated else latex_pending()
394	    (OUT_DIR / "burst_energies.tex").write_text(tex)
395	
396	    print(markdown_table(rows))
397	    print(
398	        f"\nN = {len(rows)} bursts.  "
399	        f"Skipped: placeholder z=1.0 (freya/mahi/johndoeii) and any sightline "
400	        f"without a joint c0/gamma fit (e.g. casey)."
401	    )
402	    if not calibrated:
403	        print(
404	            "\n*** UNCALIBRATED: configs/telescopes.yaml has no flux_jy_per_unit for "
405	            "one or both bands. ***\n"
406	            "The columns above are band fluence integrals in NATIVE .npy units -- NOT "
407	            "energies, NOT comparable across bands, NOT to be quoted. Supply "
408	            "flux_jy_per_unit (Jy per native unit, from each telescope's SEFD + beam "
409	            "response at the burst position) for BOTH bands to emit E_iso. See "
410	            "analysis/burst_energies/CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md."
411	        )
412	    print(f"\nWrote {OUT_DIR / 'burst_energies.json'}")
413	    print(
414	        f"Wrote {OUT_DIR / 'burst_energies.tex'} ({'energy table' if calibrated else 'calibration-pending stub'})"
415	    )
416	
417	
418	if __name__ == "__main__":
419	    main()
420

It is on the **live E_iso route**:\n  `joint_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz(nick, \"D\")` → `dsa_sigma_jy(…, beam_gain)`\n  (`flux_cal.py:288-290`). 13	def test_dsa_calibrated_but_gate_closed(monkeypatch):
14	    # D via the model-based integral, C still uncalibrated -> gate closed (no summed energy), but
15	    # the DSA band's Jy*ms*Hz integral is still surfaced on the row.

23	def test_both_bands_emit(monkeypatch):
24	    # Phase 7: both bands routed through the model-based radiometer integral ("fluxcal") -> the gate

29	    )

32	    assert rows and all("E_iso_erg" in r for r in rows)
33	    r = rows[0]

1. **Absolute-scale cross-check covers 3 sightlines, not all.** `test_joint_band_fluence_matches_catalog_scale`
   compares the model-based DSA fluence to the Law+2024 catalog for **oran (0.99×), zach (1.27×), and
   whitney (2.15×)** — the only co-detections with a published catalog fluence in the repo. The other
   DSA-band fluences (isha, phineas, wilhelm, hamilton, chromatica) rely on the radiometer model
   (measured beam + coherent-beam SEFD) **without an independent catalog anchor**. The factor-of-3
   test band is a sanity gate, not a tight constraint. Treat the absolute scale as validated to ~2×
   for the 3 anchored bursts and model-trusted (no external check) for the rest.

2. **Untested high model fluences exist but do not enter E_iso.** Some bursts carry large model-based
   band-average fluences (mahi ≈ 468, freya ≈ 156 Jy·ms) with no catalog comparison. These are
   **excluded from the energy table** because they lack a well-constrained host redshift (the
   `z = 1.0000` placeholder flag → skipped, `calculate_burst_energies.py:156`), so they cannot bias
   the published energies — but they flag that the per-sightline scale is not uniformly verified.

3. **Redshift scope.** The E_iso table is restricted to sightlines with a real (non-placeholder) host
   redshift; sources whose redshift is unknown or poorly constrained (freya, mahi, johndoeii) are
   omitted. The per-source redshift quality (spectroscopic vs photometric) is inherited from the
   galaxy-search `TARGETS` list and is **not** independently flagged here — any sightline later found
   to have only a photometric/uncertain redshift should be demoted or annotated in the table.

**Net:** the energies are correct given the model, catalog-anchored to ~2× for oran/zach/whitney, and
band-restricted lower limits throughout. The manuscript and any energetics claim should state the
absolute scale is catalog-validated for the 3 anchored bursts rather than implying uniform validation.

## Review: `feat/energetics-followups` (worktree `flits-energetics`)

**Verdict: the diff is clean. No correctness bugs found.** All four intended changes are behavior-preserving as claimed; the new test passes; the energy self-check passes. I tried to break each one and could not.

### Scope note (flag)
The prompt says "four small changes," but `git diff` shows **five** modified tracked files — the fifth is `tests/test_burst_energies_fluxcal.py` (a new test, `test_z_provenance_flags_unpublished_hosts`, +9 lines), which is a legitimate companion to change 3, not a stray edit. There are also **two untracked docs** that don't appear in `git diff` but are part of the branch intent: `docs/rse/specs/plan-energetics-followups.md` and `docs/rse/specs/research-energetics-followups.md`. The prompt's change 4 referenced `docs/rse/specs/*energetics-followups.md` so these are expected. Branch is `[behind 4]` from origin/main — informational only. **No genuinely stray/unrelated change in the diff.**

### Non-issues checked and cleared

**Change 1 — `lru_cache` on `load_power_beam` (`analysis/dsa_beam.py:57`)**
- (a) **No mutation of cached arrays.** Only consumer of the returned `(fz, th, ph, P)` is `beam_gain` (`dsa_beam.py:79-81`), which feeds them to `scipy.interpolate.RegularGridInterpolator`. I inspected scipy 1.16.3: `_check_values` returns `P` unchanged (it's already float from `np.zeros`, so no `astype` copy and no in-place write); `__call__` never writes to `self.values`. The grids are all ascending (freq 1.2–1.6, θ 0–180, φ 0–360), so the `np.flip(values, _descending_dimensions)` branch isn't triggered — and `np.flip` returns a view without mutating the source anyway. No caller anywhere else (`flux_cal.py`, `refit_calibrated.py`, `plot_bandpass_check.py`) touches `load_power_beam` directly; they all go through `beam_gain`.
- (b) **Cache key is hashable and stable.** `DEFAULT_BEAM` is a module-level `PosixPath` constant; `Path` is hashable; the live route (`dsa_sigma_jy` → `beam_gain(...)`) never passes an explicit `path`, so it's a single cache slot.
- (c) **No correctness change vs reload-every-call.** Same arrays returned; only the disk read is amortized.
- (d) **`maxsize=2` is fine** — slightly generous (1 would suffice for the single default path) but harmless and leaves headroom for an explicit-path test.

**Change 2 — `if valid.any():` guard (`analysis/flux_cal.py:261-264`)**
- **Provably behavior-preserving in the normal case:** I ran 2000 randomized some-valid inputs; new output `== `old output every time (`equal_nan` exact).
- **All-masked case is safe:** old code produced all-False `valid` *with* an "All-NaN slice" RuntimeWarning (`ns > 1e-6*nan` → all-False); new code returns the input all-False `valid` *without* the warning — identical value, warning suppressed. Downstream in `joint_band_fluence_jy_ms_hz`, all-False `valid` makes `fz`/`amp_sn` empty and `np.trapezoid(empty, empty)` returns `0.0` — the correct, safe contribution for a fully-RFI-masked band.

**Change 3 — `Z_PROVENANCE` + `row["z_src"]` (`analysis/calculate_burst_energies.py:74-83, 194`)**
- **No row missing from the dict.** `compute()` emits rows for `sorted(fits)` minus placeholder z=1.0. 18	**No correctness issues found.** Each change is the smallest correct size and nothing touches the fit-validation contract or the physics kernel. Details below.
19	
20	### `dsa_beam.py` — `@lru_cache` on `load_power_beam` ✅
21	The cache is safe:
22	- **Key is hashable** (`path`, defaults to the `DEFAULT_BEAM` `Path`). `maxsize=2` comfortably covers a `str` vs `Path` spelling of the same path.
23	- **Returned arrays are never mutated.** I traced every consumer (`beam_gain`, `_check`, `plot_bandpass_check.py`, `refit_calibrated.py`, `flux_cal.dsa_sigma_jy`). `beam_gain` only feeds `P` into a `RegularGridInterpolator` (read-only); nothing writes back. So sharing the cached cube across calls is correct.
24	- Holding ~345 MB alive for process lifetime is the intended trade and matches the `~6160×` reload it removes.
25	
26	One scope note (not a request): the cache eliminates the *file read*, but `beam_gain` still rebuilds the `RegularGridInterpolator` on every call (`dsa_sigma_jy` calls it once per channel). That's pre-existing and out of scope here — flagging only so the remaining per-channel cost is on record.
27	
28	### `flux_cal.py` — empty-`valid` guard ✅
29	`if valid.any():` is genuinely behaviour-preserving. When `valid` is all-`False`, `ns[valid]` is empty → `np.nanmedian` would warn and return `nan` → `ns > 1e-6*nan` is all-`False` → `valid & …` stays all-`False`. The guarded version short-circuits to the same all-`False` `valid` without the empty-slice warning. Identical output, one fewer spurious warning.
30	
31	### `calculate_burst_energies.py` — `Z_PROVENANCE` / `z_src` ✅
32	This is the right direction for rigor: surfacing redshift provenance and explicitly flagging `hamilton`/`chromatica` as `spec-provisional` guards against an unpublished `z` being read as catalog-grade — consistent with the no-rationalization stance in the validation contract. The `.get(nick, ("unknown", ""))` fallback is safe for any non-energetics nick.
33	
34	Minor (no change needed): the second tuple element (source string) is never read in code — only `quality` becomes `z_src`. It's referenced in `CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md`/specs as provenance documentation, so keeping it as data is reasonable rather than dead weight.
35	
36	### Test ✅
37	`test_z_provenance_flags_unpublished_hosts` pins both the coverage (all 8 hosts present) and the exact provisional set — it would catch a silent demotion or a typo'd nick.
38	
39	### Physics / validation contract
40	Nothing in this PR alters scattering models, bounds (τ, α, τ·Δν), the frequency-ascending convention, or the PASS/MARGINAL/FAIL gates. The energetics path is calibration metadata only. The deliberately-deferred float/fluxcal gate tightening is a reasonable call given it's tested.

1	\section{The Dispersion and Scattering Budget}
2	\label{sec:budget}
3	
4	% Core methods section. The observed DM decomposes as
5	%   DM_obs = DM_MW,ISM + DM_MW,halo + <DM_cosmic>(z) + DM_intervening + DM_host,
6	% with DM_MW,ISM from NE2001/YMW16 (pygedm), DM_MW,halo a 40 pc/cm^3 prior
7	% (Yamasaki & Totani 2020), <DM_cosmic>(z) the Macquart relation
8	% (Macquart et al. 2020; f_IGM=0.84, chi_e=0.875), and DM_intervening a two-phase
9	% (hot mNFW + clumpy cool) CGM column for each intersecting foreground galaxy,
10	% reported raw and capped at b = 0.1 R_vir (the galaxy-interior regime).
11	%
12	% Scattering: measured tau_1GHz from nested-sampling fits (quality-gated on
13	% reduced chi^2, with R^2/normality informational only), compared against the
14	% predicted intervening tau from a thin-screen two-phase model.
15	
16	\subsection{Dispersion Measure Decomposition}
17	\label{sec:dm}
18	
19	The observed dispersion measure of each co-detection separates into Galactic,
20	cosmological, host, and (where the sightline intersects a foreground galaxy)
21	intervening contributions \citep{CordesChatterjee2019},
22	\begin{equation}
23	\mathrm{DM_{obs}} = \mathrm{DM_{MW}} + \langle\mathrm{DM_{cosmic}}\rangle(z)
24	+ \mathrm{DM_{int}} + \mathrm{DM_{host}},
25	\label{eq:dmbudget}
26	\end{equation}
27	with the Galactic term $\mathrm{DM_{MW}} = \mathrm{DM_{MW,ISM}} +
28	\mathrm{DM_{MW,halo}}$ split between disk and halo. We estimate the disk
29	contribution $\mathrm{DM_{MW,ISM}}$ from the NE2001 \citep{CordesLazio2002} and
30	YMW16 \citep{YMW2017} electron-density models and adopt a
31	$\sim$40\,pc\,cm$^{-3}$ Milky-Way halo prior \citep{YamasakiTotani2020}. The
32	cosmological mean $\langle\mathrm{DM_{cosmic}}\rangle(z)$ follows the Macquart
33	relation \citep{Macquart2020}. For the sightlines that cross a foreground
34	galaxy we model the intervening circumgalactic column $\mathrm{DM_{int}}$ as a
35	two-phase (hot modified-NFW plus clumpy cool) medium, taking the mNFW gas
36	profile from \citet{ProchaskaZheng2019}. Such intervening halos can imprint
37	measurable dispersion and, where the gas is turbulent, scattering on FRB
38	sightlines \citep{Ocker2021}, although an individual quiescent halo may instead
39	yield only an upper limit on its scattering contribution \citep{Prochaska2019}.
40	The residual after the modeled terms are removed is attributed to the host.
41	
42	\subsection{Intervening Foreground Galaxies and Clusters}
43	\label{sec:foreground}
44	
45	The intervening term $\mathrm{DM_{int}}$ is sourced only where a sightline
46	actually intersects foreground circumgalactic or intracluster gas, so we first
47	establish which candidate systems along the twelve sightlines are genuinely in
48	the foreground. Each candidate is cross-matched against the DESI Legacy Imaging
49	Survey DR9 with \citet{Zhou2021} photometric redshifts, DESI DR1 spectroscopic
50	redshifts, the NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED), and PS1-STRM
51	\citep{Beck2021}---by coordinate match (morphology and redshift) and, for the
52	PS1-classified halos, by direct \texttt{objID} lookup. We label a candidate
53	\emph{confirmed} foreground when its best catalog redshift lies below the FRB
54	host redshift, \emph{background} when at or above it, and \emph{inconclusive}
55	when the redshift straddles the host within $1\sigma$, the host lacks a
56	spectroscopic redshift, or no trustworthy redshift exists (a PS1-STRM
57	\texttt{UNSURE} classification or extrapolated photo-$z$). Of the 49 candidates
58	in Table~\ref{tab:foreground}, 29 are confirmed foreground, 7 are background,
59	and 13 remain inconclusive; the photometric redshifts in the source compilation
60	are superseded by the catalog values reported here. Only one of the 15 clusters
61	has an impact parameter inside its own $R_{500}$, so for the rest the sightline
62	does not pierce the intracluster medium and the cluster contributes negligibly
63	to $\mathrm{DM_{int}}$.
64

67	\subsection{Scattering Attribution}
68	\label{sec:scattering}
69	
70	We measure the pulse-broadening time and its frequency scaling from the
71	co-detected dynamic spectra and compare them against the scattering predicted
72	by each candidate screen: the Milky-Way ISM, an intervening circumgalactic
73	medium, or a host galaxy, where the host can dominate the scattering of a
74	heavily broadened burst \citep{Ocker2022}. The fits are produced by the
75	\texttt{dsa110-FLITS} pipeline (\texttt{pipeline/}).
76

124	
125	\subsubsection{The joint two-band fit}
126	\label{sec:jointfit}
127	
128	A single-band scattering fit cannot separate the scattering index $\alpha$ from
129	the scattering time, because the pulse broadening
130	$\tau(\nu)=\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}\,(\nu/1\,\mathrm{GHz})^{-\alpha}$ enters a
131	single band only through its value at that band's frequency: one band fixes the
132	product, not the slope. Co-detection breaks this degeneracy. We fit the
133	CHIME/FRB ($\sim$0.4--0.8\,GHz) and DSA-110 ($\sim$1.4\,GHz) dynamic spectra
134	\emph{simultaneously} with a shared sightline pair
135	$(\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}},\alpha)$ and per-telescope pulse parameters (arrival
136	time $t_0$, intrinsic width $\zeta$, and a residual dispersion
137	$\delta\mathrm{DM}$). The $\sim$1\,GHz lever arm between the bands measures
138	$\alpha$ directly: the ratio of the two scattering times pins the slope, while
139	the shared normalization $\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}$ pins its value at 1\,GHz. With
140	$\alpha$ held at the Kolmogorov value $4.4$ \citep{Rickett1990}, the two bands
141	instead return $\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}$ estimates that disagree by up to an
142	order of magnitude for the same sightline---evidence that $\alpha\neq4.4$ along
143	these lines of sight.
144	
145	\begin{figure}
146	  \centering
147	  \includegraphics[width=0.95\columnwidth]{pbf_shapes}
148	  \caption{Pulse-broadening function (PBF) shapes used in the joint fit. A Gaussian
149	  intrinsic pulse convolved with a thin-screen exponential PBF (green) versus
150	  power-law-spectrum PBFs with density index $\beta=3.00$ and $\beta=11/3$
151	  (Kolmogorov). Smaller $\beta$ yields a heavier $t^{-\beta/2}$ tail; $\beta\to4$
152	  recovers the exponential \citep[\S11.2]{Cordes2025}.}
153	  \label{fig:pbf_shapes}
154	\end{figure}
155	
156	\begin{figure*}
