159	  \caption{Band-dependent PBF preference for FRB~wilhelm. \emph{Left:} change in
160	  log-evidence relative to the exponential PBF versus power-law index $\beta$ (best
161	  single-component, per band). CHIME (400--800\,MHz) mildly prefers a Kolmogorov
162	  tail ($\Delta\ln Z=+6.2$ at $\beta=11/3$); DSA (1.2--1.5\,GHz) rejects
163	  heavier-than-exponential tails monotonically. \emph{Right:} joint CHIME+DSA
164	  evidence (C1D1). A \emph{per-band} PBF (CHIME power-law, DSA exponential) beats the
165	  all-exponential model by $\Delta\ln Z=+4.0$ ($\sim6\sigma$), whereas a global
166	  power-law loses $84$. The two bands require different PBFs.}
167	  \label{fig:pbf_evidence}
168	\end{figure*}

170	\subsubsection{Gain-marginalized likelihood}
171	\label{sec:gainmarg}
172	
173	The per-channel amplitude of an FRB spectrum is unknown and strongly modulated
174	by scintillation; carried as a free spectral envelope it leaves correlated
175	structure in the fit residuals and invalidates a $\chi^2$ goodness-of-fit test.
176	We therefore marginalize the per-channel gain analytically. With a Gaussian
177	prior on the gain the per-channel evidence is available in closed form (a
178	matched-filter likelihood), and the recovered gain absorbs both the burst
179	spectrum and the scintillation pattern. This removes the spectral and
180	scintillation structure from the residual, so that the reduced $\chi^2$ and the
181	lag-1 residual autocorrelation become meaningful quality gates, and it lowers
182	the sampled dimensionality. We
183	sample the posterior by nested sampling \citep{Skilling2004}, as implemented in
184	\texttt{dynesty} \citep{Speagle2020}, and quality-gate each fit on its reduced
185	$\chi^2$ and residual whiteness, treating $R^2$ and residual normality as
186	informational.
187	
188	\subsubsection{Multiple temporal components}
189	\label{sec:multicomp}
190	
191	Some bursts comprise more than one temporal sub-component, a common feature of
192	the resolved FRB population \citep{Hessels2019, Pleunis2021}. An unmodeled
193	second component is partially absorbed by a single scattered pulse---as a steeper slope
194	and a larger scattering time---and so biases the inferred $\alpha$. We extend
195	the likelihood to $N$ temporal components per band, each contributing its own
196	$(t_0,\zeta)$ while $(\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}},\alpha)$ remain shared across both
197	bands and all components, and we select the number of components per band by
198	Bayesian evidence. Because the evidence normalization differs between likelihood
199	variants, the component counts are compared on a single matched grid in which
200	even the one-component model is evaluated through the multi-component
201	likelihood, so that evidence differences are meaningful. Component arrival times
202	within a band are ordered and separated by a data-derived minimum spacing,
203	keeping the fit identifiable at every prior sample. A clean single-component
204	co-detection in our sample, for which the joint fit returns
205	$\alpha=4.48\pm0.04$ with white residuals, validates the method; a
206	multi-component case is presented in Section~\ref{sec:results-alpha}.
207	% Validating clean case = burst internally labelled "freya" (swap to TNS name).

1	\subsection{Time-of-Arrival Crossmatching}
2	\label{sec:toa}
3	
4	Before attributing the dispersion and scattering budgets we verify that the
5	twelve events are genuine co-detections---the same burst seen by both
6	facilities, with arrival times consistent under the cold-plasma dispersion law
7	and the geometric light-travel delay between the sites. The wide baseline
8	between CHIME/FRB (400--800\,MHz) and DSA-110 ($\sim$1.4\,GHz) makes the
9	co-detections a test of the $1/\nu^2$ dispersion scaling and of the relative
10	timing alignment of the two facilities \citep{Lorimer2007, Thornton2013}.
11	
12	\subsubsection{Delay model}
13	
14	We translate the arrival times at the two central frequencies to a common
15	reference frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{ref}}=400$\,MHz. The cold-plasma dispersion
16	delay is
17	\begin{equation}
18	\Delta t_p = K_{\mathrm{DM}}\,\mathrm{DM}
19	\left(\frac{1}{\nu_{\mathrm{ref}}^2}-\frac{1}{\nu_{\mathrm{obs}}^2}\right),
20	\label{eq:dmdelay}
21	\end{equation}
22	with $K_{\mathrm{DM}} = 4.148808\times10^{3}\,\mathrm{MHz^2\,pc^{-1}\,cm^3\,s}$.
23	The geometric light-travel difference between the observatories is
24	\begin{equation}
25	\tau_{\mathrm{geo}} = \frac{(\mathbf{p}_2-\mathbf{p}_1)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{s}}}{c},
26	\label{eq:geodelay}
27	\end{equation}
28	where $\mathbf{p}_1$ and $\mathbf{p}_2$ are the GCRS position vectors of CHIME
29	and DSA-110 and $\hat{\mathbf{s}}$ is the unit vector toward the source. The
30	timing residual $\mathcal{R}=\Delta\tau_{\mathrm{obs}}-\tau_{\mathrm{geo}}$ is
31	the difference between the frequency-corrected inter-site offset and the
32	predicted geometric delay; a residual of zero indicates perfect agreement.
33	
34	\subsubsection{Residuals and systematics}
35	
36	Across the sample the residuals (Figure~\ref{fig:toa_resid}) have a mean of
37	$2.42$\,ms, a standard deviation of $3.06$\,ms, and a median of $1.88$\,ms,
38	consistent with the combined timing uncertainties of the two instruments, which
39	are dominated by coarse time resolution and pulse-width variation. A systematic
40	search for correlations between the residuals and burst properties
41	(Figure~\ref{fig:toa_sys}) finds none that reach significance: the residual is
42	uncorrelated with DM ($r=0.14$, $p=0.67$) over the observed range
43	$262$--$959$\,pc\,cm$^{-3}$, confirming the adopted $1/\nu^2$ scaling and the
44	value of $K_{\mathrm{DM}}$; the correlations with FWHM ($r=0.48$, $p=0.11$) and
45	combined measurement uncertainty ($r=0.49$, $p=0.11$) are moderate but not
46	significant, as expected since wider bursts time less precisely; and a
47	suggestive anti-correlation with epoch ($r=-0.54$, $p=0.07$) warrants monitoring
48	for long-term clock or baseline drift as the sample grows. The per-burst
49	properties and residuals are listed in Table~\ref{tab:toa}.
50	
51	\begin{figure}
52	\centering
53	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{toa_crossmatch_analysis_premium.png}
54	\caption{Time-of-arrival residuals for the twelve co-detections. Left: residual
55	(measured $-$ geometric) per burst, colored by DM, with the median $1\sigma$
56	timing uncertainty ($\pm2.5$\,ms) shaded. Right: residual versus DM with a
57	linear fit ($r=0.14$).}
58	\label{fig:toa_resid}
59	\end{figure}
60	
61	\begin{figure*}
62	\centering
63	\includegraphics[width=0.85\textwidth]{systematics_check_matrix.png}
64	\caption{Systematic correlation search. Residuals versus DM, FWHM, combined
65	measurement uncertainty, and epoch (MJD), with Pearson $r$ and trend lines. No
66	correlation reaches significance ($p<0.05$).}
67	\label{fig:toa_sys}
68	\end{figure*}
69	
70	\begin{deluxetable}{lrrrr}

72	\label{tab:toa}}
73	\tablehead{\colhead{Burst} & \colhead{DM} & \colhead{MJD} & \colhead{FWHM} &
74	\colhead{Residual} \\
75	\colhead{} & \colhead{(pc\,cm$^{-3}$)} & \colhead{} & \colhead{(ms)} &
76	\colhead{(ms)}}

{

  "content": "\\section{Observations and Sample}\n\\label{sec:obs}\n\nOur sample is the twelve fast radio bursts detected simultaneously by CHIME/FRB\n\\citep{CHIMEFRB2018} at $0.4$--$0.8$\\,GHz and by DSA-110 \\citep{Law2024} at\n$\\sim$1.4\\,GHz between 2022 February and 2024 February (MJD $59617$--$60369$).\nThe defining asset of the sample is that each burst is seen twice across a\n$\\sim$1\\,GHz frequency baseline, which---as developed in\nSection~\\ref{sec:jointfit}---breaks the degeneracy between the scattering time\nand its spectral index that defeats any single-band fit. The bursts span a\ndispersion measure range of $262$--$960$\\,pc\\,cm$^{-3}$; their nicknames, TNS\ndesignations, epochs, widths, and time-of-arrival residuals are listed in\nTable~\\ref{tab:toa}. We report all twelve, noting per sightline the level at\nwhich each quantity is constrained rather than imposing a single detection\nthreshold.\n\n\\subsection{Dynamic spectra and reduction}\n\\label{sec:data}\n\nFor each co-detection we analyze a pair of total-intensity dynamic spectra---one\nper facility---derived from the CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 baseband recordings\n(24 spectra in total; provenance and array geometry in\n\\texttt{DATA\\_SOURCES.md} of the companion \\texttt{dsa110-FLITS} archive). Each\nspectrum is loaded with its frequency axis standardized to ascending order and\nits per-channel bandpass normalized, so the fitted amplitudes are free of the\nband-edge rolloff. All fits, quality gates, and figures in this paper are\nproduced by the open \\texttt{dsa110-FLITS} pipeline (\\texttt{pipeline/}), which\nwe reference throughout for reproducibility. We do not catalog the fine\nbaseband morphology of each burst here; the only morphological distinction the\nanalysis depends on---whether a burst resolves into more than one temporal\ncomponent---is treated where it matters, in the multi-component fit of\nSection~\\ref{sec:multicomp}.\n\n\\subsection{DSA-110 scattering measurements}\n\\label{sec:obs-scatt}\n\nEvery DSA-110 burst yields a $1.4$\\,GHz scattering constraint---a pulse-broadening\ntime $\\tau_{1\\,\\mathrm{GHz}}$ and, where the diffractive scale is resolved, a\ndecorrelation bandwidth---which we measure against the NE2001 Galactic\nprediction along each sightline. Eleven of the twelve sightlines have a joint\nCHIME--DSA scattering fit; three of those (FRB~20221203A, FRB~20230325A,\nFRB~20240229A) fail the reduced-$\\chi^2$ quality gate and their scattering times\nare withheld, and four sightlines whose scattering is too weak to resolve return\nonly an upper limit on $\\alpha$ (the fit rails at the prior bound). The fitted\nvalues, their quality flags, and the comparison against the predicted\ncontributions are presented in Section~\\ref{sec:budget}; here we note only that\nthe measurements exist and span from sightlines consistent with the Galactic\nfloor to FRB~20221203A, whose resolved diffractive scale sits roughly five times\nbelow the NE2001 prediction.\n\n\\subsection{Foreground-galaxy search}\n\\label{sec:obs-fg}\n\nTo establish which sightlines could carry an intervening dispersion or\nscattering contribution, we searched each of the twelve fields for foreground\ngalaxies and clusters, cross-matching candidates against the DESI Legacy Imaging\nSurvey DR9 with \\citet{Zhou2021} photometric redshifts, DESI DR1 spectroscopic\nredshifts, the NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database, and PS1-STRM \\citep{Beck2021}.\nThe search returns 49 candidate systems---34 galaxy halos and 15 clusters---along\nnine of the twelve sightlines (three fields yield no candidate). For each\ncandidate we record the proper impact parameter (12--280\\,kpc for the halos;\nclusters by $b/R_{500}$) and the best available redshift and its provenance\n(spectroscopic or photometric); the full catalog is Table~\\ref{tab:foreground}.\nSpectroscopic host redshifts are available for nine of the twelve bursts\n($z=0.043$--$0.51$), while three (FRB~20230325A, FRB~20240122A, FRB~20230814B)\ncarry only a placeholder redshift and are excluded from any distance-dependent\nquantity. We measure no host stellar masses; the only masses entering the\nanalysis are the halo-mass proxies of the intervening systems used by the\ncircumgalactic dispersion model (Section~\\ref{sec:dm}), whose confidence we flag\nper system. The verdict logic that classifies each candidate as foreground,\nbackground, or inconclusive, and the resulting dispersion budget, follow in\nSection~\\ref{sec:budget}.\n\n\\input{sections/toa.tex}\n"
}

Found it. The TNS name encodes each burst's date (FRB YYYYMMDD…), so each MJD can be checked against its own row. Top 7 match; bottom 5 are scrambled:

| row (nickname) | TNS date | MJD→UTC | |
|---|---|---|---|
| zach…freya (7) | — | — | ✅ all match |
| johndoeII | 2023-08-14 | **2024-02-29** | ✗ (casey's date) |
| hamilton | 2023-09-13 | **2023-08-14** | ✗ (johndoeII's date) |
| mahi | 2024-01-19 | **2023-09-13** | ✗ (hamilton's date) |
| chromatica | 2024-02-03 | **2024-01-22** | ✗ |
| casey | 2024-02-29 | **2024-02-03** | ✗ (chromatica's date) |

**The issue:** in `scratch/codetection/bursts.csv`, the `mjd` column is misaligned by one row for the bottom 5 bursts — each MJD belongs to a neighbor, not the nickname it sits next to. It's a near-clean one-row rotation **except** one MJD lands on **2024-01-22**, which matches no claimed TNS date. The nearest is mahi's `FRB 20240119A` — off by **3 days**. So either mahi's true designation is **FRB 20240122A** (the MJD says Jan 22) or that MJD is itself wrong.

**What's NOT affected:** the `z_spec` / γ / τ / position columns track the *nickname* correctly (verified hamilton z=0.302, chromatica 0.074, casey 0.287 against the budget), so the budget table, the figure, and everything just merged are clean. The scramble is confined to the `mjd` column of this one staging CSV. The manuscript ToA table (`toa.tex`) was built from a correct source.

**Why it blocks the nickname→TNS sweep:** mapping mahi→TNS is ambiguous (20240119A in the CSV vs 20240122A implied by the real MJD), and johndoeii is only medium-confidence. Stamping an unverified designation into a publication is the one thing worth blocking on.

**Fix needs one authoritative lookup:** un-rotate the `mjd` column to nicknames, then resolve mahi's true date against the DSA-110 detection log / TNS (19th or 22nd?). Want me to realign the CSV and chase down mahi's date?

Definitive. The TNS cone search at mahi's position returns **exactly one** FRB — and three independent quantities all agree:

- **FRB 20240122A** at 02:38:28.8 +71:04:12 (within CHIME's 26′×1.4° error box of mahi's 02:39:03.96 +71:01:04)
- **DM 959.58 pc/cm³** ≡ mahi's `DM_obs` = **960** in the budget — dead-on
- event time **2024-01-22 02:30:32 UTC = MJD 60331.10** — exactly the "anomalous" MJD from the scrambled column

So mahi = **FRB 20240122A**, not 20240119A. The 3-day discrepancy wasn't an MJD error — the *name* was wrong, and the real MJD (60331.10) was correct but parked in the wrong row. Verifying johndoeii (the other flagged one) the same way:

> AGENT

Both flagged bursts resolved against TNS — and **both had wrong names in the sheet:**

| nickname | sheet said | **TNS truth** | how confirmed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **mahi** | FRB 20240119A | **FRB 20240122A** | DM 959.58≡960, pos match (CHIME 26′ box), MJD 60331.10 = 2024-01-22 |
| **johndoeii** | FRB 20230814B | **FRB 20230814A** | DSA-110, pos 22:23:53.9 +73:01:33 sub-arcsec match, DM 696.35≡696, MJD 60170.36 |

And the MJD column is a clean **one-row cyclic rotation** across the bottom 5 rows — each nickname's true MJD is the value one row below it (casey wraps to the top). After un-rotating, every MJD matches its row's TNS date:

| nickname | corrected TNS | corrected MJD → date |
|---|---|---|
| johndoeii | FRB 20230814**A** | 60170.36 → 2023-08-14 |
| hamilton | FRB 20230913A | 60200.21 → 2023-09-13 ✓ |
| mahi | FRB 2024**0122**A | 60331.10 → 2024-01-22 |
| chromatica | FRB 20240203A | 60343.83 → 2024-02-03 ✓ |
| casey | FRB 20240229A | 60369.37 → 2024-02-29 ✓ |

The "3-day discrepancy" was a red herring — not an MJD error, just a wrong name (19th→22nd). **Data-integrity issue fully resolved; the nickname→TNS sweep is now unblocked** (all 12 verified). Recording the corrected map:

1	"""Burst metadata utilities for the scattering analysis pipeline.
2	
3	This module provides functions to load burst metadata from external sources
4	such as CSV files containing TNS names and other burst properties.
5	"""
6	
7	from pathlib import Path
8	from typing import Optional
9	import pandas as pd
10	
11	
12	# Cache for burst metadata to avoid re-reading CSV
13	_BURST_METADATA_CACHE = None
14	
15	
16	def load_burst_metadata(csv_path: Optional[Path] = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
17	    """Load burst metadata from CSV file.
18	    
19	    Parameters
20	    ----------
21	    csv_path : Path, optional
22	        Path to CSV file. If None, uses default location.
23	        
24	    Returns
25	    -------
26	    pd.DataFrame
27	        Burst metadata with columns: name, TNS, MJD, RA_deg, Dec_deg, etc.
28	    """
29	    global _BURST_METADATA_CACHE
30	    
31	    if _BURST_METADATA_CACHE is not None:
32	        return _BURST_METADATA_CACHE
33	    
34	    if csv_path is None:
35	        # Default to chimedsa_burst_specs.csv in repository root
36	        csv_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / 'chimedsa_burst_specs.csv'
37	    
38	    if not csv_path.exists():
39	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Burst metadata CSV not found: {csv_path}")
40	    
41	    _BURST_METADATA_CACHE = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
42	    return _BURST_METADATA_CACHE
43	
44	
45	def load_tns_name(burst_nickname: str, csv_path: Optional[Path] = None) -> str:
46	    """Load TNS name for a burst given its nickname.
47	    
48	    Parameters
49	    ----------
50	    burst_nickname : str
51	        Burst nickname (e.g., 'casey', 'freya')
52	    csv_path : Path, optional
53	        Path to CSV file. If None, uses default location.
54	        
55	    Returns
56	    -------
57	    str
58	        TNS name (e.g., 'FRB 20240229A') or nickname if not found
59	        
60	    Examples
61	    --------
62	    >>> load_tns_name('casey')
63	    'FRB 20240229A'
64	    >>> load_tns_name('freya')
65	    'FRB 20230325A'
66	    """
67	    try:
68	        df = load_burst_metadata(csv_path)
69	        # Case-insensitive lookup
70	        nickname_lower = burst_nickname.lower()
71	        match = df[df['name'].str.lower() == nickname_lower]
72	        
73	        if not match.empty:
74	            return match.iloc[0]['TNS']
75	        else:
76	            # Fallback to uppercase nickname if not found
77	            return burst_nickname.upper()
78	    except Exception as e:
79	        # If any error occurs, fallback to uppercase nickname
80	        print(f"Warning: Could not load TNS name for {burst_nickname}: {e}")
81	        return burst_nickname.upper()
82

commit ac5911686128f36ac44c33d041902c0fffee94c9
Author: Jakob Faber <jfaber@caltech.edu>
Date:   Tue Jun 23 15:02:27 2026 -0700

    Emit TNS designations from the budget generator and burst-metadata converter
    
    burst_metadata.load_tns_name() previously depended on chimedsa_burst_specs.csv, which is gitignored and absent from clean checkouts, so it silently fell back to the uppercased nickname. Adds a committed canonical _FALLBACK_TNS map (12 entries) carrying the two designations corrected against a TNS cone search (mahi 20240119A->20240122A, johndoeii 20230814B->20230814A), so the converter resolves correctly without the external CSV.
    
    sightline_budget.main() now relabels the budget DataFrame's name column nickname->TNS after the per-burst lookups complete, so the regenerated CSV, markdown table, and figure all emit TNS names -- keeping a future regeneration from reverting the manuscript's nickname->TNS sweep. Adds test_burst_metadata.py (3 tests) guarding the corrected map. The foreground_table.tex generator lives in an out-of-repo notebook and is not addressed here.

from scattering.scat_analysis.burst_metadata import load_tns_name

    assert load_tns_name("mahi") == "FRB 20240122A"  # was 20240119A
    assert load_tns_name("johndoeii") == "FRB 20230814A"  # was 20230814B


def test_load_tns_name_anchors_and_case_insensitive():
    assert load_tns_name("casey") == "FRB 20240229A"
    assert load_tns_name("Wilhelm") == "FRB 20221203A"
    assert load_tns_name("ZACH") == "FRB 20220207C"


def test_load_tns_name_unknown_falls_back_to_upper():
    assert load_tns_name("notaburst") == "NOTABURST"

=== full main() ===
def main():
    base_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
    results_dir = os.path.join(base_dir, "results")
    configs_dir = os.path.join(base_dir, "scattering", "configs", "bursts", "chime")
    bursts_dir = os.path.join(results_dir, "bursts")

    df = build_all_budgets(
        results_dir=results_dir, configs_dir=configs_dir, bursts_dir=bursts_dir, enrich=False
    )

    # Emit TNS designations (not internal nicknames) in the CSV, table, and figure.
    from scattering.scat_analysis.burst_metadata import load_tns_name
    df["name"] = [load_tns_name(n) for n in df["name"]]

    csv_path = os.path.join(results_dir, "sightline_dm_scattering_budget.csv")
    df.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)
    print(f"Wrote {csv_path}")

    md_path = os.path.join(results_dir, "sightline_dm_scattering_budget.md")
    with open(md_path, "w") as fh:
        fh.write("# FRB sightline DM & scattering budgets\n\n")
        fh.write(format_budget_table(df))
        fh.write("\n")
    print(f"Wrote {md_path}")

    fig = make_budget_figure(df)
    png_path = os.path.join(results_dir, "sightline_dm_scattering_budget.png")
    fig.savefig(png_path, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    print(f"Wrote {png_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

---

# AGENT CONFIGURATION: FLITS Fitting Code Development

**Status:** Complete Self-Contained Document for AI Agents

**Give this entire document to Claude/Gemini**

---

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

### The Problem

You (AI agent) frequently declare poor-quality fits as successful because:

- No quantitative ground truth to validate against
- Implicit success criteria
- Can't actually run code to verify
- Tend to rationalize failures

### The Solution

Follow a **deterministic validation framework** with:

1. **Level 1 GATES:** Convergence, physical bounds, covariance (mandatory)
2. **Level 2 CHECKS:** χ², R², residuals, uncertainties (determines quality)
3. **Level 3 PHYSICS:** Domain-specific validation (τ×Δν, α scaling)

### Success Metric

You have succeeded when:

- ✅ 95%+ of bad fits identified as FAILED
- ✅ 95%+ of good fits identified as PASSED
- ✅ All test suite tests pass
- ✅ No unphysical parameters slip through
- ✅ Failures reported explicitly (never rationalized)

---

## YOUR ROLE & CONSTRAINTS

### What You Are

**A scientific software engineer** developing numerical methods for radio astronomy. Your code must be:

- Correct (mathematically sound)
- Robust (handles edge cases)
- Transparent (fully auditable)
- Rigorous (validation built-in)

### What You Are NOT

- ❌ A code generation service
- ❌ A tool that trades correctness for convenience
- ❌ An agent that rationalizes poor results
- ❌ A system with silent failures

### Your Non-Negotiable Constraints

1. **MUST validate every fit** before declaring success
2. **MUST run test suite** before submitting code
3. **MUST provide evidence** (plots, metrics, logs)
4. **MUST report failures explicitly**
5. **MUST ask for help** when validation unclear

---

## VALIDATION FRAMEWORK: THREE LEVELS

### LEVEL 1: MANDATORY GATES

**Any gate failure = fit is FAILED (immediate stop)**

#### Gate 1.1: Convergence

```python
if not result.success:
    print("❌ MANDATORY GATE FAILED: Did not converge")
    # STOP - cannot use this fit
```

**Why:** If optimizer didn't converge, result is meaningless

#### Gate 1.2: Physical Bounds

**For τ (scattering timescale):**

- ❌ Invalid: τ ≤ 0 (negative time unphysical)
- ❌ Invalid: τ < 0.0001 ms (below resolution)
- ❌ Invalid: τ > 100 ms (never observed)
- ✅ Valid: 0.0001 < τ < 100 ms

**For α (frequency scaling):**

- ❌ Invalid: α ≤ 1.5 or α ≥ 6.0 (outside physical models)
- ✅ Valid: 1.5 < α < 6.0

```python
tau = result.x[0]
if not (0.0001 < tau < 100):
    print(f"❌ MANDATORY GATE FAILED: τ = {tau} out of bounds")
    # STOP
```

**Why:** Unphysical solutions mean optimizer hit constraints or model is wrong

#### Gate 1.3: Covariance Matrix

**Rule:** Jacobian must be well-conditioned (invertible, not singular)

```python
u, s, vt = np.linalg.svd(result.jac)
condition_number = s[0] / s[-1]
if condition_number > 1e6:
    print(f"❌ MANDATORY GATE FAILED: Ill-conditioned (cond={condition_number:.2e})")
    # STOP - solution is non-unique
```

"""Validation thresholds for FLITS fitting.

Re-exports the single source of truth in ``flits.fitting.VALIDATION_THRESHOLDS``.
"""

from flits.fitting.VALIDATION_THRESHOLDS import *  # noqa: F401,F403

######## flits/fitting/VALIDATION_THRESHOLDS.py ########
"""Validation thresholds for FLITS fitting."""

# MCMC Convergence
MCMC_AUTOCORR_NSTEPS_FACTOR = 50
MCMC_BURN_IN_FACTOR = 5.0
MCMC_ACC_FRAC_MIN = 0.2
MCMC_ACC_FRAC_MAX = 0.9
MCMC_MIN_EFFECTIVE_SAMPLES = 100

# Physical Parameter Bounds
DM_MIN = 1e-3
DM_MAX = 3000
AMP_MIN = 0.01
AMP_MAX = 10000
WIDTH_MIN = 1e-4
WIDTH_MAX = 1000

# Likelihood Thresholds
RED_CHI_SQ_CATASTROPHIC = 100

# Residual Validation
RESIDUAL_NORMALITY_PVALUE = 0.05
RESIDUAL_BIAS_SIGMA_THRESHOLD = 3.0
RESIDUAL_AUTOCORR_DW_MIN = 1.0
RESIDUAL_AUTOCORR_DW_MAX = 3.0

# Chi-Squared Thresholds
CHI_SQ_RED_EXCELLENT_MIN = 0.8
CHI_SQ_RED_GOOD_MAX = 1.5
CHI_SQ_RED_MARGINAL_MAX = 3.0
CHI_SQ_RED_SUSPICIOUSLY_LOW = 0.3

# R-Squared Thresholds
R_SQ_EXCELLENT_MIN = 0.95
R_SQ_GOOD_MIN = 0.85
R_SQ_MARGINAL_MIN = 0.70
R_SQ_POOR_MIN = 0.50

# Parameter Uncertainty Thresholds
PARAM_UNCERTAINTY_GOOD_MAX = 0.3
PARAM_UNCERTAINTY_ACCEPTABLE_MAX = 0.5
PARAM_UNCERTAINTY_MARGINAL_MAX = 1.0

# Physics Constraints
TAU_DELTANU_MIN = 0.1
TAU_DELTANU_MAX = 2.0
TAU_DELTANU_THIN_SCREEN = 0.159
TAU_DELTANU_EXTENDED = 1.0

ALPHA_KOLMOGOROV = 4.0
ALPHA_GOOD_MIN = 3.0
ALPHA_GOOD_MAX = 5.0
ALPHA_MARGINAL_MIN = 2.0
ALPHA_MARGINAL_MAX = 6.0

export const meta = {
  name: "fit-verify",
  description:
    "Adversarial pre-publication verification of FLITS scattering fit results. Fans out one verifier agent per *_fit_results.json, each told to TRY TO REFUTE the fit's PASS claim against the runtime 3-level fit-quality gate (burstfit.py classify_fit_quality), then aggregates to confirmed-PASS / MARGINAL / FAIL with reasons. A separate agent does the judging so the fitter's own self-preferential bias cannot pass its own work.",
  phases: [
    "discover: glob the results tree for *_fit_results.json fit artifacts",
    "verify (parallel, adversarial): one verifier per fit, each attempts to REFUTE the PASS claim against the exact 3-level gate cut points",
    "aggregate: synthesize verdicts into confirmed-PASS / MARGINAL / FAIL with per-fit reasons and a publication-readiness summary",
  ],
};

// Results path or glob to verify. Edit this constant to retarget the run.
// Default matches the canonical per-burst fit artifact produced by the
// scattering pipeline anywhere under the repo.
const TARGET = "**/*_fit_results.json";

// The FLITS fit-quality contract, verbatim from the runtime classifier
// (scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit.py classify_fit_quality, ~L1342-1386;
// constants L67-70) plus the Level-1 physical gates and Level-3 physics
// consistency. This is the AUTHORITATIVE rubric — the doc/VT files disagree on
// several cuts and the runtime code intentionally overrides them. Every verifier
// is judged ONLY against these runtime cut points.
const GATE_CONTRACT = `
AUTHORITATIVE FLITS FIT-QUALITY CONTRACT (runtime classify_fit_quality in
scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit.py — this is what actually fires; the
AGENT_CONFIGURATION doc and VALIDATION_THRESHOLDS.py disagree and are SUPERSEDED).

LEVEL 1 — physical / convergence gates (ANY failure => FAIL, regardless of chi2):
  - fit must have CONVERGED (no optimizer failure / non-finite parameters).
  - tau (scattering timescale, ms): valid only if 0.0001 < tau < 100.
      FAIL if tau <= 0, tau < 0.0001 (below time resolution), or tau > 100 (never observed).
  - alpha (scattering index): Level-1 hard gate valid only if 1.5 < alpha < 6.0.
  - covariance / Jacobian must be non-singular (condition number < ~1e6).

LEVEL 2 — goodness of fit (drives the PASS/MARGINAL/FAIL flag):
  Reduced chi-square (chi2_red), constants CHI_SQ_RED_SUSPICIOUSLY_LOW=0.3,
  CHI_SQ_RED_GOOD_MAX=1.5, CHI_SQ_RED_FAIL_MAX=10.0:
    - PASS     : 0.3 <= chi2_red <= 1.5  (AND all Level-1 gates pass).
    - MARGINAL : 1.5 < chi2_red <= 10.0,  OR  chi2_red < 0.3
                 (suspiciously low — noise likely OVERestimated).
    - FAIL     : chi2_red > 10.0 (catastrophic), OR chi2_red non-finite.
  NOTE: the 3.0 cut (CHI_SQ_RED_MARGINAL_MAX in VALIDATION_THRESHOLDS.py) is DEAD
  in the live classifier — do NOT use 3.0 as a boundary. The doc's "PASS up to
  3.0" is WRONG for the runtime; PASS ceiling is 1.5.

  R-squared and residual-normality p-value are INFORMATIONAL ONLY. They NEVER
  flip the flag. A low weighted R2 (< 0.70) is EXPECTED for low-S/N bursts and
  must NOT be cited as a refutation of a PASS — at most an informational note.

LEVEL 3 — physics consistency (a violation here => FAIL, overriding a Level-2 PASS):
  - tau x Delta-nu_d product (GHz*ms; convert Delta-nu MHz->GHz via *1e-3):
      valid only if 0.1 < tau*dnu < 2.0; otherwise the measurements are
      inconsistent => FAIL. Reference: thin-screen 1/(2*pi)=0.159, extended
      medium=1.0; assign the nearer model (closer to 0.159 => thin screen,
      closer to 1.0 => extended medium).
  - alpha physics consistency: Kolmogorov reference alpha=4.0. FAIL if
      alpha < 2.0 or alpha > 6.0. PASS-consistent if 3.5 <= alpha <= 4.5;
      otherwise allowed but flagged MARGINAL (deviates from Kolmogorov).

FIGURE-REVIEW GATE (repo commit 0f4fa17 forces this): a numeric PASS is NOT
sufficient. The fit must have emitted diagnostic figures (data-vs-model,
residuals, histogram, Q-Q) AND they must have been visually assessed. A fit that
claims PASS with no evidence of figure emission/review is NOT confirmed-PASS.
`;

def classify_fit_quality(
    chi2_reduced: float,
    r_squared: float | None = None,
    normality_pvalue: float | None = None,
) -> tuple[str, list]:
    """Classify fit quality from chi2_reduced (PASS / MARGINAL / FAIL).

    The reduced chi-squared is the primary, trustworthy gate when the noise is
    well estimated: a value near 1 means the model fits to within the noise. The
    noise-weighted R^2 is deliberately NOT a gate here -- for faint (low-S/N)
    bursts the signal variance is small relative to the noise, so R^2 is low even
    for a correct model (a fit at chi2_red ~ 1 can have R^2 well below 0.5).
    Treating R^2 < 0.5 as a hard failure (the previous behavior) spuriously
    rejected good faint-burst fits. R^2 and the residual-normality p-value are
    reported as informational notes only; note that at the ~10^4-pixel sample
    sizes here the Shapiro normality p-value is ~0 even for excellent fits.

    Returns (flag, notes) where flag is "PASS", "MARGINAL", or "FAIL".
    """
    notes: list = []
    if chi2_reduced is None or not np.isfinite(chi2_reduced):
        return "FAIL", ["Non-finite chi2_red"]

    if chi2_reduced > CHI_SQ_RED_FAIL_MAX:
        flag = "FAIL"
        notes.append(f"Catastrophic chi2_red ({chi2_reduced:.1f})")
    elif chi2_reduced > CHI_SQ_RED_GOOD_MAX:
        flag = "MARGINAL"
        notes.append(f"Elevated chi2_red ({chi2_reduced:.2f})")
    elif chi2_reduced < CHI_SQ_RED_SUSPICIOUSLY_LOW:
        flag = "MARGINAL"
        notes.append(f"Suspiciously low chi2_red ({chi2_reduced:.2f}); noise may be overestimated")
    else:
        flag = "PASS"

    # Informational only -- these do NOT change the flag.
    if r_squared is not None and np.isfinite(r_squared) and r_squared < R_SQ_MARGINAL_MIN:

Read enough to ground the plan. Key findings:

**Authoritative gate = the runtime `classify_fit_quality`** (`burstfit.py:1362`), which takes scalar χ²_red: **PASS ≤ 1.5, MARGINAL ≤ 10, FAIL > 10** — plus Level-1 bounds (α∈(1.5,6.0), τ∈(1e-4,100)) and Level-3 α-physics (FAIL if α<2 or >6). The doc's "PASS up to 3.0" is **dead** — `fit-verify.js` states the runtime supersedes it. ⇒ reuse `classify_fit_quality`, don't re-implement (DRY/ponytail).

**No re-fit needed to gate:** `{burst}_joint_fit.json` has α/τ/bounds, `{burst}_joint_ppc.json` has `chi2_chime`/`chi2_dsa`. Gate = join the two + apply cut points.

**The α rails are a prior-edge artifact:** `alpha_bounds=[1.0, 6.0]` in the fits, but the physical floor is 1.5. whitney/oran/johndoeII pile at ~1.4 **with good χ² (~1.1)** — i.e. the data prefers unphysically-shallow scaling, meaning the "tail" is likely intrinsic width / a sub-component, **not** a scattering detection. Re-fitting with an α≥1.5 floor would just rail at 1.5 — it won't rescue them.

**τ×Δν Level-3 not evaluable** (no per-sightline scintillation bandwidth) → report N/A, don't FAIL on it.

**Reuse, don't build:** `classify_fit_quality`, the `fit-verify.js` adversarial workflow, the `figure-reviewer` agent on `dsa_figs/*_fitquality.png`.

Proposed phases: (1) deterministic gate script → verdict table; (2) `fit-verify` adversarial re-check; (3) figure review; (4) reconcile `results.tex`; (5) *conditional* α-rail re-fits.

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""List every co-detected burst's joint-fit quality metrics -> why 3 of 12 pass."""
import glob, json, os
RUNS = os.environ.get("FLITS_RUNS", "/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs")
rows = []
for fp in sorted(glob.glob(f"{RUNS}/data/joint/*_joint_fit.json")):
    b = os.path.basename(fp).replace("_joint_fit.json", "")
    d = json.load(open(fp))
    pc = d.get("percentiles", {})
    al = pc.get("alpha", {}).get("median")
    # hunt for goodness / whiteness fields wherever they live
    flat = json.dumps(d)
    gof = d.get("goodness_of_fit") or d.get("gof") or {}
    # common metric names
    def grab(*names):
        for n in names:
            for src in (d, gof, d.get("gate", {}) or {}):
                if isinstance(src, dict) and n in src:
                    return src[n]
        return None
    rows.append({
        "burst": b,
        "alpha": round(al, 2) if al else None,
        "verdict": grab("verdict", "classification", "flag", "gate_verdict"),
        "lag1": grab("lag1", "lag1_autocorr", "temporal_lag1", "dw"),
        "chi2_C": grab("chi2_red_C", "chi2_C", "redchi_C"),
        "chi2_D": grab("chi2_red_D", "chi2_D", "redchi_D"),
        "topkeys": [k for k in d.keys() if k not in ("percentiles", "samples")],
    })
print(f"{'burst':12s} {'alpha':>6s} {'verdict':>12s} {'lag1':>10s} {'chi2_C':>8s} {'chi2_D':>8s}")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['burst']:12s} {str(r['alpha']):>6s} {str(r['verdict']):>12s} "
          f"{str(r['lag1']):>10s} {str(r['chi2_C']):>8s} {str(r['chi2_D']):>8s}")
print(f"\nN bursts = {len(rows)}")
print("sample topkeys:", rows[0]["topkeys"] if rows else None)

PASS-consistent in\n    # the Kolmogorov window; otherwise MARGINAL). tau x dnu not evaluable here.\n    if alpha < 2.0 or alpha > 6.0:\n        l3 = \"FAIL\"\n    elif KOLM_LO <= alpha <= KOLM_HI:\n        l3 = \"PASS\"\n    else:\n        l3 = \"MARGINAL\"\n\n    final = _worst(l1, l2, l3)\n    if l1_fail:\n        reason = \"L1 \" + \"; \".join(l1_fail)\n    elif l2 == \"FAIL\":\n        reason = \"L2 catastrophic \" + l2_note\n    elif final == \"FAIL\":\n        reason = f\"L3 alpha={alpha:.2f} unphysical\"\n    elif final == \"MARGINAL\":\n        bits = []\n        if l2 == \"MARGINAL\":\n            bits.append(\"L2 \" + l2_note)\n        if l3 == \"MARGINAL\":\n            bits.append(f\"L3 alpha={alpha:.2f} off Kolmogorov\")\n        reason = \"; \".join(bits)\n    else:\n        reason = \"all levels pass\"\n\n    return {\n        \"burst\": burst, \"alpha\": alpha, \"tau\": tau, \"rail\": rail,\n        \"chi2_chime\": cc, \"chi2_dsa\": cd,\n        \"l1\": l1, \"l2\": l2, \"l3\": l3, \"tau_dnu\": \"N/A (no dnu_d)\",\n        \"final\": final, \"reason\": reason,\n    }\n\n\ndef main():\n    jdir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / \"joint_json\"\n    rows = []\n    for fp in sorted(jdir.glob(\"*_joint_fit.json\")):\n        burst = fp.name.replace(\"_joint_fit.json\", \"\")\n        fit = json.loads(fp.read_text())\n        ppc_fp = jdir / f\"{burst}_joint_ppc.json\"\n        ppc = json.loads(ppc_fp.read_text()) if ppc_fp.exists() else None\n        v = gate_one(burst, fit, ppc)\n        rows.append(v)\n        worst_chi2 = None\n        if v[\"chi2_chime\"] is not None and v[\"chi2_dsa\"] is not None:\n            worst_chi2 = max(v[\"chi2_chime\"], v[\"chi2_dsa\"])\n        (jdir / f\"{burst}_joint_gate.json\").write_text(json.dumps({\n            \"burst\": burst, \"chi2_reduced\": worst_chi2,\n            \"chi2_chime\": v[\"chi2_chime\"], \"chi2_dsa\": v[\"chi2_dsa\"],\n            \"tau\": v[\"tau\"], \"alpha\": v[\"alpha\"], \"alpha_railed\": v[\"rail\"],\n            \"quality_flag\": v[\"final\"], \"notes\": [v[\"reason\"]],\n        }, indent=2))\n\n    cols = [\"burst\", \"alpha\", \"rail\", \"tau\", \"chi2_chime\", \"chi2_dsa\",\n            \"l1\", \"l2\", \"l3\", \"tau_dnu\", \"final\", \"reason\"]\n    out = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\n    with (out / \"joint_gate_verdicts.csv\").open(\"w\", newline=\"\") as fh:\n        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=cols)\n        w.writeheader()\n        w.writerows(rows)\n    md = [\"# Joint-fit quality verdicts (committed \" + jdir.name + \")\", \"\",\n          \"| \" + \" | \".join(cols) + \" |\", \"|\" + \"---|\" * len(cols)]\n    for r in rows:\n        md.append(\"| \" + \" | \".join(\n            f\"{r[c]:.3f}\" if isinstance(r[c], float) else str(r[c]) for c in cols) + \" |\")\n    n = {f: sum(r[\"final\"] == f for r in rows) for f in (\"PASS\", \"MARGINAL\", \"FAIL\")}\n    md += [\"\", f\"**{len(rows)} fits**: {n['PASS']} PASS / {n['MARGINAL']} MARGINAL / {n['FAIL']} FAIL.\"]\n    (out / \"joint_gate_verdicts.md\").write_text(\"\\n\".join(md) + \"\\n\")\n    print(\"\\n\".join(md))\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
}

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Posterior-predictive per-band check for the joint fits.

Rebuilds each band's FRBModel (same prep as run_joint_fit), evaluates the M3
model at the JOINT best-fit medians, and reports per-band reduced chi2 +
profile overlays. If the joint solution fits BOTH bands well (chi2~1), the
shared tau*nu^-alpha (and its alpha) is a real joint measurement. If one band
is poorly fit, the shallow alpha is a forced compromise between irreconcilable
bands, not a measurement.

  python joint_ppc.py <burst>
"""
import json, os, sys
import numpy as np

REPO = os.environ.get("FLITS_REPO", "/home/jfaber/flits/dsa110-FLITS")
RUNS = os.environ.get("FLITS_RUNS", "/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs")
sys.path.insert(0, f"{REPO}/scattering")
import yaml
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scat_analysis.config_utils import load_telescope_block
from scat_analysis.pipeline.io import BurstDataset
from scat_analysis.burstfit import FRBParams


def prepare(cfg_path, name, outdir):
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(cfg_path))
    tel = load_telescope_block(cfg["telcfg_path"], cfg["telescope"])
    ds = BurstDataset(cfg["path"], outdir, name=name, telescope=tel,
                      f_factor=int(cfg["f_factor"]), t_factor=int(cfg["t_factor"]),
                      outer_trim=float(cfg.get("outer_trim", 0.15)),
                      onpulse_crop=os.environ.get("FLITS_ONPULSE_CROP", "1") == "1",
                      onpulse_pad_factor=float(os.environ.get("FLITS_ONPULSE_PAD", "0.5")))
    m = ds.model
    m.dm_init = float(cfg.get("dm_init", 0.0))
    return m


def band_chi2(model, p, gain=False):
    mod = model(p, "M3")
    if gain:  # apply profiled per-channel gain: model = g_f * K_f
        g = model.gain_spectrum(p, "M3")
        mod = g[:, None] * mod
    noise = np.asarray(model.noise_std, dtype=float)
    if noise.ndim == 1:
        noise = noise[:, None]
    r = (model.data - mod) / np.where(noise > 0, noise, np.inf)
    valid = model.valid
    if valid is not None:
        valid = np.asarray(valid)
        r = r[valid] if valid.ndim == 1 else r[valid]
    r = r[np.isfinite(r)]
    chi2 = float(np.sum(r**2)); npix = int(r.size); dof = max(npix - 7, 1)
    return chi2 / dof, mod


def main():
    b = sys.argv[1]
    out = f"{RUNS}/data/joint"
    cC = f"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_chime_run.yaml"
    cD = f"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_dsa_run.yaml"
    mC = prepare(cC, f"{b}_chime", out)
    mD = prepare(cD, f"{b}_dsa", out)

    d = json.load(open(f"{out}/{b}_joint_fit.json"))
    p = {k: v["median"] for k, v in d["percentiles"].items()}
    tau, al = p["tau_1ghz"], p["alpha"]
    gain = bool(d.get("marginalize_gain", False))
    if gain:
        pC = FRBParams(c0=1.0, t0=p["t0_C"], gamma=0.0, zeta=p["zeta_C"],
                       tau_1ghz=tau, alpha=al, delta_dm=p["delta_dm_C"])
        pD = FRBParams(c0=1.0, t0=p["t0_D"], gamma=0.0, zeta=p["zeta_D"],
                       tau_1ghz=tau, alpha=al, delta_dm=p["delta_dm_D"])
    else:
        pC = FRBParams(c0=p["c0_C"], t0=p["t0_C"], gamma=p["gamma_C"], zeta=p["zeta_C"],
                       tau_1ghz=tau, alpha=al, delta_dm=p["delta_dm_C"])
        pD = FRBParams(c0=p["c0_D"], t0=p["t0_D"], gamma=p["gamma_D"], zeta=p["zeta_D"],
                       tau_1ghz=tau, alpha=al, delta_dm=p["delta_dm_D"])

=== hpcc-dev ===
#!/bin/bash
# HPCC FLITS persistent dev dashboard.
#
# Holds a compute node (sbatch job 'flits-dev'), runs a tmux session on it
# (shell + queue/acct + live-log panes), and attaches from iTerm via tmux control
# mode (-CC) so they render as NATIVE, colored, PERSISTENT iTerm panes. The node
# is yours until walltime; the tmux session survives laptop sleep/disconnect —
# reattach by re-running this. (tmux only works on compute nodes; the login nodes
# reap detached sessions, which is why we hold a node.)
#
# Usage: hpcc-dev            attach (submits the holder if none is running)
#        hpcc-dev --plain    attach with tmux drawing the panes (fallback if -CC misbehaves)
set -euo pipefail
SSH="ssh -o BatchMode=yes hpcc"
TMUXENV="export TMUX_TMPDIR=/home/jfaber/.tmux-tmp"
MODE="${1:-cc}"

if [ "$MODE" = "--release" ]; then
  $SSH "scancel -n flits-dev -u \$USER 2>&1; echo 'flits-dev released (cores freed, fairshare accrual stopped)'"
  exit 0
fi

node() { $SSH "squeue -h -n flits-dev -u \$USER -t RUNNING -o '%N'" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | tr -d ' '; }

NODE="$(node)"
if [ -z "$NODE" ]; then
  echo "no running flits-dev node — submitting the 16c/32G/12h holder..."
  $SSH 'sbatch -A radiolab ~/flits/holdnode.sbatch'
  for _ in $(seq 1 25); do sleep 6; NODE="$(node)"; [ -n "$NODE" ] && break; done
fi
[ -z "$NODE" ] && { echo "flits-dev node not up yet; re-run hpcc-dev in a minute."; exit 1; }
echo "flits-dev node: $NODE"

# ensure the tmux session/layout exists on the node (idempotent)
$SSH "ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $NODE 'bash ~/flits/bin/tmux-flits.sh'"

# The Mac can't ssh the compute node directly (it won't auth our key), but
# login->node works, so we nest: Mac -> hpcc(login) -> node. tmux -CC sequences
# flow back through both -t ptys to iTerm, which renders native panes.
if [ "$MODE" = "--plain" ]; then
  REMOTE="$TMUXENV; tmux attach -t flits"
else
  REMOTE="$TMUXENV; tmux -CC attach -t flits"
fi
MID="ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $NODE -t \"$REMOTE\""   # run on login node
LOCAL="ssh hpcc -t '$MID'"                                   # run on the Mac
# escape backslashes then double-quotes for the AppleScript string literal
ESC=$(printf '%s' "$LOCAL" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')

osascript <<OSA
tell application "iTerm2"
  set win to (create window with profile "HPCC")
  tell current session of win
    set name to "HPCC dev · $NODE"
    write text "$ESC"
  end tell
end tell
OSA
echo "attached to flits tmux on $NODE (mode: $MODE)"

=== hpcc-run ===
#!/bin/bash
# hpcc-run — run a command on the held flits-dev compute node, non-interactive.
# Brain stays local (Claude Code / Codex); this is the agent's hands on HPCC.
# Pairs with hpcc-dev (which holds the node + interactive tmux dashboard).
#
# Usage:
#   hpcc-run '<command>'          run on the held flits-dev compute node
#   hpcc-run --login '<command>'  run on the login node (light builds/tests only)
#
# The Mac can't ssh the compute node directly (key won't auth there), so node
# commands nest Mac -> hpcc(login) -> node, exactly as hpcc-dev documents.
set -euo pipefail
SSH="ssh -o BatchMode=yes hpcc"

if [ "${1:-}" = "--login" ]; then
  shift
  exec $SSH "$*"
fi

[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "hpcc-run: no command given" >&2; exit 2; }

NODE=$($SSH "squeue -h -n flits-dev -u \$USER -t RUNNING -o '%N'" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | tr -d ' ')
[ -n "$NODE" ] || { echo "hpcc-run: no running flits-dev node — run 'hpcc-dev' first to hold one." >&2; exit 1; }

# ponytail: base64 the command so arbitrary quotes/pipes survive the double SSH
# hop unmangled — naive nested-quoting (what hpcc-dev uses for fixed commands)
# breaks the moment an agent passes a command containing quotes.
CMD_B64=$(printf '%s' "$*" | base64 | tr -d '\n')
exec $SSH "ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $NODE 'echo $CMD_B64 | base64 -d | bash'"
```

> AGENT

Now it's fully explained — and there's a **third generation** I hadn't seen:

- **Scratch (06-19, `comps=[]`)** — single-model, bounds [1,6]. hamilton pinned at the **floor** 1.006±0.005; chromatica interior 3.98.
- **Committed (06-21, `comps=[c0_C,c0_D]`)** — `force_multi` multi-likelihood. hamilton pinned at the **ceiling** 5.99.
- **Latest (06-22, job 64459241)** — `--shared-zeta --alpha-lo 1.5 --alpha-hi 6.0` → wilhelm α=2.56, written to a **new** `wilhelm_joint_fit_sharedzeta.json`.

The smoking gun: **hamilton sits at opposite hard rails (floor vs ceiling) with tiny errors in the two runs** — same data, same bounds. α is multimodal/unconstrained per burst-pair; it rails wherever the model config points. Only **zach is robust** (3.3–3.7, tight, across both configs). logZ scales differ wildly (chromatica −10564 vs −44072) because `force_multi` changes the likelihood normalization — so the two generations' evidences aren't even comparable.

The campaign's *latest* direction (shared-zeta + raised α-floor 1.5) is the Phase-4 fix, already running. Checking how complete that third generation is — it may already be the canonical set:

> AGENT

Acronyms: PPC — Posterior-Predictive Check; lnZ — log Bayesian evidence.

Investigation complete. The divergence is **not** `force_multi` (my earlier guess) — it's the **per-band gain treatment**, and the logs prove it burst-by-burst.

## Root cause

Every committed fit was run with **explicit per-band gain** (gain fit as a free `c0_C`/`c0_D` amplitude). Every current scratch fit was re-run with **`--marginalize-gain`** ("per-channel gain marginalized, absorbs scintillation; 8-dim fit"). The two configs produce the α values exactly:

| burst | committed = explicit-gain α | scratch = marginalize-gain α | what marg does |
|---|---|---|---|
| zach | 3.66 ± .02 | 3.32 ± .01 | robust both ✓ |
| phineas | 3.58 ± .04 | 3.82 ± .04 | fine both ✓ |
| wilhelm | 2.69 ± .05 | 2.62 ± .04 | fine both ✓ |
| casey | (incomplete) | 2.56 ± .01 | fine ✓ |
| **chromatica** | **6.00 [EDGE]** | **3.98 ± .04** | **un-rails** ✓ |
| **freya** | **6.00 [EDGE]** | **4.48 ± .04** | **un-rails** ✓ |
| **mahi** | **5.53 [EDGE]** | **3.52 ± .16** | **un-rails** ✓ |
| **whitney** | **1.46 ± .06** | **3.75 ± .04** | **un-rails** ✓ |
| isha | 4.96 ± 2.6 [EDGE] | 4.68 ± .5 | tightens, still high |
| **hamilton** | 5.99 [EDGE] | 1.01 [EDGE] | both rail, *opposite* ✗ |
| **oran** | 1.44 [EDGE] | 5.96 [EDGE] | both rail, *opposite* ✗ |
| johndoeII | 1.37 ± .05 | 1.06 ± .04 | both unphysical ✗ |

Structurally confirmed: committed fits carry `c0_C`/`c0_D` (gain fitted); scratch fits have no `c0` (gain integrated out). The α numbers match their respective slurm logs exactly.

## What this means

1. **`--marginalize-gain` is the principled, better-behaved config.** It removes a gain–α degeneracy that was railing α to a prior edge. It un-rails chromatica/freya/mahi/whitney to physical, tightly-constrained interior values. (lnZ also jumps thousands — chromatica −44072→−10564 — but the analytic marginalization changes the likelihood normalization, so I'm *not* leaning on lnZ as the proof; the α un-railing is.)

2. **The repo committed the *inferior* explicit-gain set.** That's the actual bug behind the "everything's railed at 6" verdict table — the railing is largely a gain-treatment artifact, not the data.

3. **A real residual limitation survives even marginalize-gain:** hamilton (floor), oran (ceiling), johndoeII (unphysical-low), isha (broad) genuinely don't constrain α per sightline — hamilton/oran rail to *opposite* edges depending on config, the signature of an unconstrained, multimodal α. That's a true science result (these sightlines need the shared-α/lever-arm argument), not a config artifact.

4. The Jun-22 `--shared-zeta --alpha-lo 1.5` run (wilhelm only, α 2.69→2.56) is a further refinement in progress, not a completed generation.

Given the investigation, the canonical-set decision is now well-posed:

1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	"""Posterior-predictive per-band check for the joint fits.
3	
4	Rebuilds each band's FRBModel (same prep as run_joint_fit), evaluates the M3
5	model at the JOINT best-fit medians, and reports per-band reduced chi2 +
6	profile overlays. If the joint solution fits BOTH bands well (chi2~1), the
7	shared tau*nu^-alpha (and its alpha) is a real joint measurement. If one band
8	is poorly fit, the shallow alpha is a forced compromise between irreconcilable
9	bands, not a measurement.
10	
11	  python joint_ppc.py <burst>
12	"""
13	import json, os, sys
14	import numpy as np
15	
16	REPO = os.environ.get("FLITS_REPO", "/home/jfaber/flits/dsa110-FLITS")
17	RUNS = os.environ.get("FLITS_RUNS", "/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs")
18	sys.path.insert(0, f"{REPO}/scattering")
19	import yaml
20	import matplotlib
21	matplotlib.use("Agg")
22	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
23	from scat_analysis.config_utils import load_telescope_block
24	from scat_analysis.pipeline.io import BurstDataset
25	from scat_analysis.burstfit import FRBParams
26	
27	
28	def prepare(cfg_path, name, outdir):
29	    cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(cfg_path))
30	    tel = load_telescope_block(cfg["telcfg_path"], cfg["telescope"])
31	    ds = BurstDataset(cfg["path"], outdir, name=name, telescope=tel,
32	                      f_factor=int(cfg["f_factor"]), t_factor=int(cfg["t_factor"]),
33	                      outer_trim=float(cfg.get("outer_trim", 0.15)),
34	                      onpulse_crop=os.environ.get("FLITS_ONPULSE_CROP", "1") == "1",
35	                      onpulse_pad_factor=float(os.environ.get("FLITS_ONPULSE_PAD", "0.5")))
36	    m = ds.model
37	    m.dm_init = float(cfg.get("dm_init", 0.0))
38	    return m
39	
40	
41	def band_chi2(model, p, gain=False):
42	    mod = model(p, "M3")
43	    if gain:  # apply profiled per-channel gain: model = g_f * K_f
44	        g = model.gain_spectrum(p, "M3")
45	        mod = g[:, None] * mod
46	    noise = np.asarray(model.noise_std, dtype=float)
47	    if noise.ndim == 1:
48	        noise = noise[:, None]
49	    r = (model.data - mod) / np.where(noise > 0, noise, np.inf)
50	    valid = model.valid
51	    if valid is not None:
52	        valid = np.asarray(valid)
53	        r = r[valid] if valid.ndim == 1 else r[valid]
54	    r = r[np.isfinite(r)]
55	    chi2 = float(np.sum(r**2)); npix = int(r.size); dof = max(npix - 7, 1)
56	    return chi2 / dof, mod
57	
58	
59	def main():
60	    b = sys.argv[1]
61	    out = f"{RUNS}/data/joint"
62	    cC = f"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_chime_run.yaml"
63	    cD = f"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_dsa_run.yaml"
64	    mC = prepare(cC, f"{b}_chime", out)
65	    mD = prepare(cD, f"{b}_dsa", out)
66	
67	    d = json.load(open(f"{out}/{b}_joint_fit.json"))
68	    p = {k: v["median"] for k, v in d["percentiles"].items()}
69	    tau, al = p["tau_1ghz"], p["alpha"]
70	    gain = bool(d.get("marginalize_gain", False))
71	    if gain:
72	        pC = FRBParams(c0=1.0, t0=p["t0_C"], gamma=0.0, zeta=p["zeta_C"],
73	                       tau_1ghz=tau, alpha=al, delta_dm=p["delta_dm_C"])
74	        pD = FRBParams(c0=1.0, t0=p["t0_D"], gamma=0.0, zeta=p["zeta_D"],
75	                       tau_1ghz=tau, alpha=al, delta_dm=p["delta_dm_D"])
76	    else:
77	        pC = FRBParams(c0=p["c0_C"], t0=p["t0_C"], gamma=p["gamma_C"], zeta=p["zeta_C"],
78	                       tau_1ghz=tau, alpha=al, delta_dm=p["delta_dm_C"])
79	        pD = FRBParams(c0=p["c0_D"], t0=p["t0_D"], gamma=p["gamma_D"], zeta=p["zeta_D"],
80	                       tau_1ghz=tau, alpha=al, delta_dm=p["delta_dm_D"])
81	
82	    chiC, modC = band_chi2(mC, pC, gain=gain)
83	    chiD, modD = band_chi2(mD, pD, gain=gain)
84	    print(f"{b}: alpha={al:.2f} tau1={tau:.3f} | CHIME chi2/dof={chiC:.2f}  DSA chi2/dof={chiD:.2f}")
85	
86	    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4))
87	    for a, m, mod, nm, ch in [(ax[0], mC, modC, f"CHIME chi2={chiC:.2f}", chiC),
88	                              (ax[1], mD, modD, f"DSA chi2={chiD:.2f}", chiD)]:
89	        prof_d = np.nansum(m.data, axis=0); prof_m = np.nansum(mod, axis=0)
90	        a.plot(m.time, prof_d, "k", lw=0.8, label="data")
91	        a.plot(m.time, prof_m, "r", lw=1.2, label="joint model")
92	        a.set_title(f"{b} {nm}"); a.set_xlabel("time (ms)"); a.legend(fontsize=8)
93	    fig.suptitle(f"{b}: joint alpha={al:.2f}, tau_1GHz={tau:.3f} ms")
94	    fig.tight_layout()
95	    fp = f"{out}/{b}_joint_ppc.png"; fig.savefig(fp, dpi=110); print(f"  wrote {fp}")
96	    json.dump({"burst": b, "alpha": al, "tau_1ghz": tau,
97	               "chi2_chime": chiC, "chi2_dsa": chiD},
98	              open(f"{out}/{b}_joint_ppc.json", "w"), indent=2)
99	
100	
101	if __name__ == "__main__":
102	    main()
103

> AGENT

Array-zeta is supported: `_smearing_sigma` (burstfit.py:679) does `np.hypot(sig_dm, zeta)`, which broadcasts a per-channel `zeta` array element-wise against the per-channel DM-smear, as long as it's built on the same `freq` axis (exactly what `run_joint_fit` does). So the shared-zeta PPC branch is sound: build `zc = zeta_1ghz * mC.freq**x_zeta`, pass `zeta=zc`, `gain=True`.

> AGENT

Direct answer: **right now we're not — and that's a real gap the user is right to flag.**

The shared-zeta canonical set I just built is **all C1D1 (one temporal component per band)**. I confirmed it: every fit has `components_C=1, components_D=1`. Multi-component structure is unmodeled across the board.

And it demonstrably matters. The campaign explored component selection for **zach**, and the evidence is decisive:

| zach variant | α | lnZ | Δ vs C1D1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1D1 | 3.319 | 32965 | — |
| C1D2 | 3.332 | 33060 | +95 |
| **C2D1** | **2.755** | 36577 | **+3612** |
| **C2D2** | **2.762** | 37734 | **+4769** |

Adding a second **CHIME** sub-pulse is favored by ΔlnZ ≈ **+3600**, and it drops α from **3.32 → 2.76**. That's exactly the bias CLAUDE.md documents ("unmodeled sub-components bias α high, zach 3.3→2.7") — now reproduced. So our canonical zach (C1D1 shared-zeta, **α=3.00**) is biased high; the evidence-preferred value is **~2.76**. oran also has a C1D2 variant (α=2.07 vs C1D1 5.74) — another large component-driven shift.

Two structural problems beyond zach:
1. **Only zach was systematically tested** for sub-components; the other 10 were never run at C2, so we don't know who else is biased.
2. **shared-zeta and multi-component aren't wired together** — the gain-recovery block is gated `... and not multi`, and `joint_ppc.py` builds exactly one `FRBParams` per band, so it can't PPC a multi-component fit as written. Composing them needs code work, not just a re-run.

So "adopt shared-zeta C1D1 as canonical" silently ships a known α-high bias for any multi-component burst. How do you want to handle it?

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/scratch/worktrees/flits-gate/analysis/scattering-refit-2026-06/component_gallery.py",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python\n\"\"\"Per-burst component-screening gallery: CHIME | DSA, each a dedispersed\nwaterfall (freq x time, on-pulse cropped) over its frequency-collapsed profile.\nNo model overlay -- this is for COUNTING temporal sub-components by eye before\ndeciding C1 vs C2 fits. Reuses the exact data prep as run_joint_fit/joint_ppc.\n\n  python component_gallery.py <burst>\n\"\"\"\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport yaml\n\nimport matplotlib\n\nmatplotlib.use(\"Agg\")\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\nREPO = os.environ.get(\"FLITS_REPO\", \"/home/jfaber/flits/dsa110-FLITS\")\nRUNS = os.environ.get(\"FLITS_RUNS\", \"/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs\")\nsys.path.insert(0, f\"{REPO}/scattering\")\nfrom scat_analysis.config_utils import load_telescope_block\nfrom scat_analysis.pipeline.io import BurstDataset\n\n\ndef prepare(cfg_path, name):\n    cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(cfg_path))\n    tel = load_telescope_block(cfg[\"telcfg_path\"], cfg[\"telescope\"])\n    ds = BurstDataset(\n        cfg[\"path\"],\n        f\"{RUNS}/data/joint\",\n        name=name,\n        telescope=tel,\n        f_factor=int(cfg[\"f_factor\"]),\n        t_factor=int(cfg[\"t_factor\"]),\n        outer_trim=float(cfg.get(\"outer_trim\", 0.15)),\n        onpulse_crop=os.environ.get(\"FLITS_ONPULSE_CROP\", \"1\") == \"1\",\n        onpulse_pad_factor=float(os.environ.get(\"FLITS_ONPULSE_PAD\", \"0.5\")),\n    )\n    return ds.model\n\n\ndef panel(axw, axp, m, title):\n    d = np.asarray(m.data, float)  # (freq, time), freq ascending\n    t = np.asarray(m.time, float)\n    # downsample freq for display only if very tall\n    step = max(1, d.shape[0] // 512)\n    disp = d[::step]\n    vmax = np.nanpercentile(disp, 99.5)\n    axw.imshow(\n        disp,\n        aspect=\"auto\",\n        origin=\"lower\",\n        extent=[t[0], t[-1], 0, d.shape[0]],\n        cmap=\"viridis\",\n        vmin=np.nanpercentile(disp, 5),\n        vmax=vmax,\n    )\n    axw.set_title(title)\n    axw.set_ylabel(\"freq chan\")\n    prof = np.nansum(d, axis=0)\n    axp.plot(t, prof, \"k\", lw=0.9)\n    axp.axhline(0, color=\"0.6\", lw=0.5)\n    axp.set_xlabel(\"time (ms)\")\n    axp.set_ylabel(\"flux (a.u.)\")\n    axp.margins(x=0)\n\n\ndef main():\n    b = sys.argv[1]\n    mC = prepare(f\"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_chime_run.yaml\", f\"{b}_chime\")\n    mD = prepare(f\"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_dsa_run.yaml\", f\"{b}_dsa\")\n    fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 6), gridspec_kw={\"height_ratios\": [2, 1]})\n    panel(ax[0, 0], ax[1, 0], mC, f\"{b}  CHIME (400-800 MHz)\")\n    panel(ax[0, 1], ax[1, 1], mD, f\"{b}  DSA (1.31-1.50 GHz)\")\n    fig.suptitle(f\"{b}: component screen -- count temporal sub-pulses per band\", y=1.0)\n    fig.tight_layout()\n    fp = f\"{RUNS}/data/joint/{b}_components.png\"\n    fig.savefig(fp, dpi=120, bbox_inches=\"tight\")\n    print(f\"wrote {fp}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
}

Viewed all 12. My read (CHIME | DSA, distinguishing a true 2nd pulse from a scattering tail):

| burst | CHIME | DSA | my call | corroborating |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **zach** | 1 (+subtle) | **2** (main + ~12 ms bump) | **multi** | C2 evidence ΔlnZ +3600 |
| **whitney** | **2–3?** (sub-bumps ~1.5–2.5 ms) | 1 (noisy) | **multi-CHIME?** | floor-rail + config-flip |
| **phineas** | 1–2? | **2** (main + ~3.5 ms) | **multi-DSA?** | DSA χ²=2.19 |
| **isha** | 1 (noisy) | **2?** (main + shoulder) | multi-DSA? | DSA χ²=3.64 |
| **mahi** | 1 (noisy) | **2?** (main + shoulder) | multi-DSA? | DSA χ²=3.70 |
| **johndoeII** | 1 + tail | **2?** (main + ~1.4 ms) | multi-DSA? | floor-rail |
| **oran** | messy/low-S/N | **2?** (main + shoulder) | multi-DSA? | C1D2 variant α=2.07 |
| casey | 1 clean | 1 (noisy) | single | — |
| chromatica | 1 clean | 1 (drift) | single | clean PASS |
| freya | 1 clean | 1 clean | **single (control)** | PASS |
| hamilton | 1 narrow | low-S/N | single (DSA unconstrained) | floor-rail = low S/N, not components |
| wilhelm | 1 + tail | 1 broad | single | DSA χ² = shape, not 2nd pulse |

The hard call on the 6 "DSA 2?" bursts: those shoulders could be a genuine second sub-pulse **or** a scattering tail (one component) — the eye can't separate them, which is exactly where the numerical C1D1-vs-C1D2 evidence decides.

Your turn — go through them and give me your counts (especially: real 2nd pulse vs tail on the DSA shoulders, and whether whitney's CHIME is 2–3 components). I'll then run the matching multi-component fit per burst and confirm with ΔlnZ + the α shift.

onclick=\"dlAll()\">&#11015; Download ALL annotated</button>\n <button onclick=\"copyAll()\">&#10697; Copy all counts</button>\n</div>\n<div id=\"help\">Click a panel where you see a component &mdash; Annotate the multi-component ones, then <b>Download ALL annotated</b> and send the PNGs back (or <b>Copy all counts</b> and paste).</div>\n<div id=\"stage\"><img id=\"img\"><canvas id=\"cv\"></canvas></div>\n<script>\nconst BURSTS = __DATA__;\nconst SPLIT = 0.5;\nlet cur = 0;\nconst marks = {};\nconst img = document.getElementById('img'), cv = document.getElementById('cv'), ctx = cv.getContext('2d');\n\nfunction load(){\n  const b = BURSTS[cur];\n  marks[b.name] = marks[b.name] || [];\n  img.onload = () => { cv.width = img.clientWidth; cv.height = img.clientHeight; redraw(); };\n  img.src = b.data;\n  document.getElementById('title').textContent = (cur+1)+'/'+BURSTS.length+'  '+b.name;\n}\nfunction arrow(c, x, y, band, n, scale){\n  const col = band==='CHIME' ? '#4ea3ff' : '#ff7b4e';\n  const L = 30*scale, H = 14*scale;\n  c.strokeStyle = col; c.fillStyle = col; c.lineWidth = 2.2*scale;\n  c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(x, y-L); c.lineTo(x, y-H*0.4); c.stroke();\n  c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(x-6*scale, y-H); c.lineTo(x, y-H*0.3); c.lineTo(x+6*scale, y-H); c.closePath(); c.fill();\n  c.font = 'bold '+(15*scale)+'px system-ui'; c.textBaseline='bottom';\n  c.fillText(band[0]+n, x+5*scale, y-L);\n}\nfunction tally(ms){ const cc={CHIME:0,DSA:0}; ms.forEach(m=>cc[m.band]++); return cc; }\nfunction redraw(){\n  ctx.clearRect(0,0,cv.width,cv.height);\n  ctx.strokeStyle='rgba(255,255,255,0.18)'; ctx.setLineDash([5,5]);\n  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(cv.width*SPLIT,0); ctx.lineTo(cv.width*SPLIT,cv.height); ctx.stroke();\n  ctx.setLineDash([]);\n  const ms = marks[BURSTS[cur].name]; const cc={CHIME:0,DSA:0};\n  ms.forEach(m=>{ cc[m.band]++; arrow(ctx, m.x*cv.width, m.y*cv.height, m.band, cc[m.band], 1); });\n  document.getElementById('nc').textContent = 'CHIME '+cc.CHIME;\n  document.getElementById('nd').textContent = 'DSA '+cc.DSA;\n}\ncv.addEventListener('click', e=>{\n  const r = cv.getBoundingClientRect();\n  const x = (e.clientX-r.left)/cv.width, y = (e.clientY-r.top)/cv.height;\n  marks[BURSTS[cur].name].push({x, y, band: x<SPLIT?'CHIME':'DSA'});\n  redraw();\n});\nfunction undo(){ (marks[BURSTS[cur].name]||[]).pop(); redraw(); }\nfunction clearMarks(){ marks[BURSTS[cur].name]=[]; redraw(); }\nfunction next(){ cur=(cur+1)%BURSTS.length; load(); }\nfunction prev(){ cur=(cur-1+BURSTS.length)%BURSTS.length; load(); }\ndocument.addEventListener('keydown', e=>{\n  if(e.key==='ArrowRight') next(); else if(e.key==='ArrowLeft') prev();\n  else if(e.key==='u') undo(); else if(e.key==='c') clearMarks();\n});\nfunction renderNatural(b){\n  const im = new Image(); im.src = b.data;\n  const tmp = document.createElement('canvas');\n  tmp.width = im.naturalWidth || img.naturalWidth; tmp.height = im.naturalHeight || img.naturalHeight;\n  const tc = tmp.getContext('2d'); tc.drawImage(im, 0, 0);\n  const scale = tmp.width/ (cv.width||tmp.width);\n  const ms = marks[b.name]||[]; const cc={CHIME:0,DSA:0};\n  ms.forEach(m=>{ cc[m.band]++; arrow(tc, m.x*tmp.width, m.y*tmp.height, m.band, cc[m.band], Math.max(1,scale*0.9)); });\n  return tmp.toDataURL('image/png');\n}\nfunction dl(href, name){ const a=document.createElement('a'); a.href=href; a.download=name; a.click(); }\nfunction dlSlide(){ const b=BURSTS[cur]; dl(renderNatural(b), b.name+'_annotated.png'); }\nfunction dlAll(){ BURSTS.forEach((b,i)=> setTimeout(()=> dl(renderNatural(b), b.name+'_annotated.png'), i*350)); }\nfunction copyAll(){\n  let out = 'burst | CHIME | DSA | marks (band@x_frac of full image)\\\\n';\n  BURSTS.forEach(b=>{ const ms=marks[b.name]||[]; const cc=tally(ms);\n    const pos = ms.map(m=> m.band[0]+'@'+m.x.toFixed(3)).join(' ');\n    out += b.name+' | '+cc.CHIME+' | '+cc.DSA+' | '+pos+'\\\\n'; });\n  navigator.clipboard.writeText(out).then(()=>alert('Copied counts for all bursts. Paste them back to me.'),\n    ()=>{ prompt('Copy this:', out); });\n}\nload();\n</script></body></html>\n\"\"\"\n\nout = SCREEN / \"component_deck.html\"\nout.write_text(HTML.replace(\"__DATA__\", DATA))\nprint(f\"wrote {out}  ({out.stat().st_size//1024} KB, {len(bursts)} slides)\")\n"

  "command": "cd /Users/jakobfaber/Developer/scratch/worktrees/flits-gate/analysis/scattering-refit-2026-06/component_screen/annotated\npython3 - <<'PY'\nimport numpy as np\nfrom PIL import Image\nimport glob, os\n\n# arrow colors from the deck: CHIME #4ea3ff=(78,163,255), DSA #ff7b4e=(255,123,78)\nCH=np.array([78,163,255]); DS=np.array([255,123,78])\nSPLIT=0.5  # left half = CHIME panel, right = DSA\n\ndef clusters(xs, gap=18):\n    if len(xs)==0: return []\n    xs=sorted(xs); groups=[[xs[0]]]\n    for x in xs[1:]:\n        if x-groups[-1][-1]<=gap: groups[-1].append(x)\n        else: groups.append([x])\n    # keep clusters with enough pixels (a real arrow, not a stray)\n    return [int(np.mean(g)) for g in groups if len(g)>=12]\n\norder=[\"zach\",\"whitney\",\"phineas\",\"isha\",\"mahi\",\"johndoeII\",\"oran\",\"casey\",\"chromatica\",\"freya\",\"hamilton\",\"wilhelm\"]\nprint(f\"{'burst':11s} | CHIME marks (x_frac) | DSA marks (x_frac)\")\nprint(\"-\"*70)\nresults={}\nfor b in order:\n    f=f\"{b}_annotated.png\"\n    if not os.path.exists(f): continue\n    im=np.asarray(Image.open(f).convert(\"RGB\")).astype(int)\n    H,W,_=im.shape\n    dch=np.abs(im-CH).sum(2)<60   # tolerance\n    dds=np.abs(im-DS).sum(2)<60\n    # arrow x positions = columns where these colors appear\n    ch_cols=np.where(dch.any(0))[0]\n    ds_cols=np.where(dds.any(0))[0]\n    # weight by count per column to cluster\n    ch_x=[x for x in ch_cols for _ in range(dch[:,x].sum())]\n    ds_x=[x for x in ds_cols for _ in range(dds[:,x].sum())]\n    cC=clusters(ch_x); cD=clusters(ds_x)\n    # CHIME arrows should be in left half, DSA in right (sanity), but report by COLOR\n    fc=[f\"{x/W:.3f}\" for x in cC]; fd=[f\"{x/W:.3f}\" for x in cD]\n    results[b]=(len(cC),len(cD))\n    print(f\"{b:11s} | {len(cC)}: {' '.join(fc):28s} | {len(cD)}: {' '.join(fd)}\")\nprint(\"\\n=== summary (your visual component counts) ===\")\nfor b in order:\n    if b in results: print(f\"  {b:11s} CHIME={results[b][0]}  DSA={results[b][1]}\")\nPY",

1	# Research: Multi-component joint-fit evidence kernel & N=1 commensurability (issue #37)
2	
3	---
4	**Date:** 2026-06-22
5	**Author:** AI Assistant
6	**Status:** Active
7	**Related Documents:** GitHub issue #37 (follow-ups from the auto-review of PR #36, merged as `3688be8`)
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Research Question
12	
13	Document, as it exists today, the multi-component gain-marginal evidence path in the
14	joint CHIME+DSA scattering fit: how `_gain_marginal_multi_band` computes per-band
15	log-evidence, how component count routes the single vs multi path through
16	`fit_joint_scattering`, how the single-component `log_likelihood_gain_marginal`
17	differs, where the gain-prior variance `s2` is set or profiled, the `dt_min`
18	handling, the `n_supported`/`frac_culled` denominators, and the current test
19	coverage. Framed by the four code items in issue #37.
20	
21	## Executive Summary
22	
23	The multi-component evidence kernel `_gain_marginal_multi_band`
24	(`scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit_joint.py:190-362`) computes a per-channel
25	linear-Gaussian gain-marginal evidence for one band: N temporal component kernels
26	per channel, per-component gains `g ~ N(0, s2 I_N)` integrated analytically, summed
27	over valid channels. It uses the FULL data normalization
28	`-0.5*T*ln(2*pi*sigma^2)` and a proper finite-variance Occam term
29	`-0.5*ln det(I_N + (s2/sigma^2) M)`. The quadratic divisor is `sigma^2` (the
30	docstring records that the spec's `sigma^4` was a transcription slip, verified
31	against the brute Gaussian evidence via Woodbury).
32	
33	The single-component `log_likelihood_gain_marginal`
34	(`scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit.py:728-765`) is a different estimator: a flat
35	(improper) prior on the per-channel gain, giving the matched-filter / F-statistic
36	marginal `-0.5*chi2min - 0.5*ln(S_kk) + 0.5*ln(2*pi*sigma^2)`. Its Occam term is
37	`-0.5*ln(S_kk)` (improper) rather than the proper `ln det(I + (s2/sigma^2) M)`, so
38	its additive scale differs from the multi path. This is the commensurability gap
39	issue #37 item 1 describes.
40	
41	**Headline finding (state of the code vs. the issue): issue #37 is largely already
42	implemented.** The N>1 gate the issue asks to remove has been replaced by a
43	`force_multi` flag plus per-call `gain_s2`, and the regression tests item 2 asks
44	for already exist (and exceed the requested minimum). See "#37 status against
45	current code" below. The research phase's value here is precisely this: it shows
46	that planning/implementing #37 as written would re-do work that already landed.
47	
48	## Scope
49	
50	**What This Research Covers:**
51	- `_gain_marginal_multi_band` evidence math, conditioning guard, and diagnostics.
52	- The single vs multi vs other-mode routing in `fit_joint_scattering`.
53	- The single-component `log_likelihood_gain_marginal` flat-prior path.
54	- `gain_s2` plumbing and the `s2=None` ML-profiling path.
55	- `dt_min` derivation and the `n_supported`/`frac_culled` denominators.
56	- Current test coverage of the kernel.
57	
58	**What This Research Does NOT Cover:**
59	- Whether the design is correct or optimal (documentarian only — no critique).
60	- The dynesty sampler internals, the non-gain joint likelihoods beyond routing.
61	- The scintillation GP path (`log_likelihood_gain_marginal_gp`) beyond noting it
62	  shares the flat temporal statistics.
63	
64	## Key Findings
65	
66	### Finding 1 — Multi-component evidence kernel `_gain_marginal_multi_band`
67	
68	**Relevant Files:**
69	- `scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit_joint.py:190-362` — the kernel.
70	- `scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit_joint.py:197-237` — docstring stating the math.
71	
72	**How It Works:**
73	1. Build the per-component unit kernels `Ks` of shape `(N, F, T)` by calling the
74	   forward model with `c0=1, gamma=0` for each component
75	   (`burstfit_joint.py:244-250`).
76	2. Per channel form the sufficient statistics: `S_dd = sum_t d^2` (F,),
77	   `b = sum_t d*K` (F, N), `M = sum_t K_i*K_j` (F, N, N)
78	   (`burstfit_joint.py:255-257`).
79	3. Per-channel marginal evidence (gains integrated analytically):
80	   `ln Z_f = -0.5*[S_dd/sigma^2 - b^T (M + (sigma^2/s2) I)^-1 b / sigma^2]
81	   - 0.5*T*ln(2*pi*sigma^2) - 0.5*ln det(I_N + (s2/sigma^2) M)`
82	   (`burstfit_joint.py:303-307` for the well-conditioned branch). The first line
83	   is the data fit, the second is the FULL data normalization, the third is the
84	   proper Occam penalty (grows with N and s2).
85	4. **Eigenvalue conditioning guard** (`burstfit_joint.py:259-281`): per channel,
86	   eigendecompose `M`; a channel is `ok` (full-rank-N) when
87	   `min_eig/max_eig >= eig_rel_floor` (default `1e-6`). A supported-but-ill-
88	   conditioned channel (`cull`) falls back to a **rank-1 proper evidence on the top
89	   eigenpair** (`burstfit_joint.py:310-327`), not the gain=0 baseline — the inline
90	   note explains that at large fixed `s2` the gain=0 baseline would *reward* a
91	   degenerate merge, so the rank-1 fallback keeps a merge Occam-penalized. A
92	   genuinely unsupported channel (no signal) gets the gain=0 baseline
93	   `-0.5*S_dd/var - 0.5*T*ln(2*pi*var)` (`burstfit_joint.py:286`).
94	5. Returns `(lnZ, diag)`; `lnZ = sum_f ln Z_f` (`burstfit_joint.py:328, 350`).
95	
96	### Finding 2 — `s2` (gain-prior variance): fixed or ML-profiled
97	
98	**Relevant Files:**
99	- `scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit_joint.py:330-348` — the `s2 is None` branch.
100	
101	**How It Works:**
102	- If a float `s2` is passed, it is used fixed (`burstfit_joint.py:347-348`).
103	- If `s2 is None`, `s2` is profiled by 1-D bounded ML over `log s2`
104	  (`scipy.optimize.minimize_scalar`), anchored on the data amplitude scale
105	  `var(ahat)` where `ahat = b/diag(M)` (`burstfit_joint.py:330-346`). The issue
106	  notes this profiled value is a profile/empirical-Bayes Z, not a clean marginal,
107	  hence its recommendation to fix `s2` for cross-N model selection.
108	- `s2` flows in from `fit_joint_scattering(gain_s2=...)` →
109	  `_JointLogLikelihoodGainMulti(s2=gain_s2)` (`burstfit_joint.py:872`) →
110	  `_gain_marginal_multi_band(..., s2=self.s2)` (`burstfit_joint.py:785-786`).
111	
112	### Finding 3 — Single-component path `log_likelihood_gain_marginal` (the contrast)
113	
114	**Relevant Files:**
115	- `scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit.py:728-765`.
116	
117	**How It Works:**
118	- Builds the single unit kernel `K`, forms `S_dd, S_dk, S_kk` per channel
119	  (`burstfit.py:751-757`).
120	- Flat-prior matched-filter marginal:
121	  `ln L_f = -0.5*(S_dd - S_dk^2/S_kk)/sigma^2 - 0.5*ln(S_kk) + 0.5*ln(2*pi*sigma^2)`
122	  (`burstfit.py:761-764`). The Occam term is `-0.5*ln(S_kk)` (improper, flat), in
123	  contrast to the multi path's proper `-0.5*ln det(I + (s2/sigma^2) M)`. This is
124	  the additive-scale difference between a 1-component `lnZ` from this path and a
125	  ≥2-component `lnZ` from the multi path.
126	- `log_likelihood_gain_marginal_gp` (`burstfit.py:781-...`) shares the identical
127	  temporal matched-filter statistics and falls back to this flat path verbatim
128	  when `delta_nu_d_MHz is None` (`burstfit.py:814-815`).
129	
130	### Finding 4 — `dt_min` derivation and `n_supported`/`frac_culled` denominators
131	
132	**Relevant Files:**
133	- `scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit_joint.py:874-886` — `dt_min` derivation.
134	- `scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit_joint.py:352-361` — the diagnostics NB.
135	
136	**How It Works:**
137	- `dt_min` (min component time separation enforced by the ordered prior transform):
138	  if `None`, computed as `max` over the two bands of `3 * median(|diff(time)|)`
139	  (`burstfit_joint.py:876-881`). The inline comment (`:874-875`) says "the binding
140	  constraint is the tighter (smaller-dt) band's resolution," while the code takes
141	  `max(dts)` (the coarser band's 3-sample floor). The single scalar `dt_min` is
142	  applied to both bands' `t0` groups via `_JointPriorTransformOrdered`
143	  (`burstfit_joint.py:883-886`); there is no per-band `dt_min`.
144	- `n_supported` vs `frac_culled`: an explicit NB comment (`burstfit_joint.py:352-355`)
145	  records that they use DIFFERENT denominators. `n_supported = count(ok)` counts only
146	  well-conditioned (full-rank-N) channels; `frac_culled = mean(~ok)` also counts
147	  rank-1-fallback channels as culled, so `n_supported != (1 - frac_culled) * F`
148	  in general (`burstfit_joint.py:356-360`).
149	
150	### Finding 5 — Test coverage of the kernel
151	
152	**Relevant Files:**
153	- `tests/test_gain_marginal_multi_band.py:1-276` — 8 tests, all targeting
154	  `_gain_marginal_multi_band` via a duck-typed `_FakeModel` with prescribed kernels.
155	
156	**What It Covers:**
157	- `test_brute_force_woodbury` (`:103-124`) and `test_brute_force_woodbury_varied`
158	  (`:127-140`, seeds 0/7/42, N=3) — total `lnZ` equals an independent brute-force
159	  Gaussian evidence `-0.5 d^T Sigma^-1 d - 0.5 ln det(2 pi Sigma)`,
160	  `Sigma = sigma^2 I + s2 K^T K`, to `rtol=1e-9`. This is issue #37 item 2(a).
161	- `test_label_swap_invariance` (`:143-164`) — permuting component order leaves
162	  `lnZ` unchanged to `rtol=1e-12`. This is issue #37 item 2(b).
163	- `test_rank1_fallback_on_collinear_channel` (`:167-212`) — a collinear channel
164	  triggers the rank-1 fallback; checks `frac_culled = 1/F`, `n_supported = F-1`,
165	  brute-force equality, and that the culled channel sits strictly below its gain=0
166	  baseline. This is issue #37 item 2(c).
167	- `test_s2_profiling_finds_interior_optimum` (`:215-246`) — the `s2=None` ML path
168	  beats fixed `s2` and lands on an interior optimum.
169	- `test_no_valid_channels_returns_neg_inf` (`:249-258`) and
170	  `test_valid_mask_subsets_channels` (`:261-275`) — boundary contracts.
171	
172	## Component Interactions
173	
174	**Routing flow (`fit_joint_scattering`, `burstfit_joint.py:815-905`):**
175	1. `multi = bool(force_multi) or components_C > 1 or components_D > 1`
176	   (`burstfit_joint.py:864`).
177	2. If `multi`: build `JOINT_PARAM_NAMES_GAIN_MULTI`, the gain-multi prior spec, and
178	   `loglike = _JointLogLikelihoodGainMulti(..., n_C, n_D, s2=gain_s2)`
179	   (`burstfit_joint.py:866-873`); derive `dt_min`; use the ordered prior transform
180	   (`:874-886`).
181	3. Else, in priority order: `shared_zeta` → `marginalize_gain_gp` →
182	   `marginalize_gain` → plain joint (`burstfit_joint.py:887-902`).
183	4. `_JointLogLikelihoodGainMulti.__call__` (`burstfit_joint.py:776-788`) unpacks
184	   `theta` into per-band component params and calls `_gain_marginal_multi_band` once
185	   per band, summing `lnZ_C + lnZ_D` (independent noise → additive evidence).
186	
187	```
188	fit_joint_scattering(components_C, components_D, force_multi, gain_s2, dt_min)
189	   │  multi = force_multi OR n_C>1 OR n_D>1
190	   ├─ multi ─> _JointLogLikelihoodGainMulti(n_C, n_D, s2=gain_s2)
191	   │              └─ per band: _gain_marginal_multi_band(params, ["M3"]*n, s2)
192	   │                              └─ proper N(0,s2) prior, full norm, proper Occam
193	   └─ not multi ─> shared_zeta / gain_gp / gain / plain
194	                      └─ FRBModel.log_likelihood_gain_marginal  (flat improper prior)
195	```
196

207	## Edge Cases and Constraints
208	
209	- All-invalid band → `(-inf, frac_culled=1.0, n_supported=0)`
210	  (`burstfit_joint.py:241-242`); tested.
211	- Collinear/near-merged kernels → rank-1 fallback, not gain=0
212	  (`burstfit_joint.py:281, 310-327`); tested on the exactly-collinear case.
213	- `s2=None` profiling returns a profile/empirical-Bayes Z, not a clean marginal —
214	  relevant if `lnZ` is used for cross-N model selection (issue #37 item 1 caveat).

Confirmed: `run_joint_fit.py` doesn't expose `--gain-s2`, so all rungs (mine + the existing zach ladder) **profile s2 per rung → empirical-Bayes / profile-Z**, not a clean fixed-s2 marginal. 

Implication for the count decision:
- **Decisive ladders** (dlnZ ≫ 10, e.g. zach's +3612): profile-Z is robust — s2 profiling is a 1-D optimization contributing O(ln) corrections, not thousands of nats. Conclusion stands.
- **Marginal rungs** (dlnZ ~ few): profile-Z contamination could flip it → those need a fixed-`gain_s2` re-run to be rigorous.

So: let the profile-Z ladders finish (already running, informative), then fix-`s2` re-run *only* the marginal decisions. That needs a small `--gain-s2` arg added to `run_joint_fit.py` (the underlying `fit_joint_scattering` already takes `gain_s2`). Checking poll progress:

Status — your question answered + campaign in flight:

**How we're handling multi-component, concretely:**

1. **Your visual census is the input** (5 multi: hamilton C5, zach C2/D3, phineas C3/D3, johndoeII C2/D2, whitney C2; 7 single). Saved to `component_census.md`.

2. **Numerical confirmation running now** — 25 HPCC jobs, an evidence ladder per multi-burst (climb each band C1→Cmax) plus a C2 null-check on the 3 ambiguous singles (isha/mahi/oran). All in the `marginalize_gain` multi-component family at standardized `α∈[1.5,6.0]`, `--force-multi` C1D1 baselines so lnZ is normalization-matched across rungs.

3. **One rigor caveat I surfaced** (from `.agents/research-multicomponent-joint-evidence.md`): the gain-prior variance `s2` is ML-profiled per rung → empirical-Bayes/profile-Z, not a clean marginal. Fine for decisive ladders (zach's C2 wins by +3612 nats — far beyond any profiling artifact), but **marginal rungs** (e.g. hamilton's 4th/5th component, phineas's 3rd) will get a fixed-`gain_s2` re-run to confirm. I'll add `--gain-s2` to `run_joint_fit.py` only if the ladders show a marginal decision.

What each fit yields directly is lnZ + α — so the ladder confirms counts without needing PPCs. Expect the per-burst dlnZ table + α-trajectory (does α drop as components are added, removing the high-α bias?) when the jobs land. Waiting on the poller.

> AGENT

Bayesian evidence ratios, not BIC. Precisely:

**Metric:** each fit's `log_evidence` is the marginal likelihood lnZ = ln∫L(θ)π(θ)dθ, computed by **dynesty nested sampling** (it integrates likelihood over the prior; `run_joint_fit.py:174`). Component support = the **log Bayes factor** lnB = lnZ(N+1) − lnZ(N), judged on the **Kass & Raftery (1995)** scale (≈Jeffreys): 2lnB <2 bare / 2–6 positive / 6–10 strong / **>10 very strong**. dynesty also returns the evidence uncertainty (~0.5 nat/fit), so every dlnZ carries a real error bar:

| burst | rung | dlnZ ± err | Kass–Raftery |
|---|---|---|---|
| zach | C2D1 | +3618 ± 0.8 | overwhelming |
| isha | C2D1 | +536 ± 0.6 | very strong |
| johndoeII | C2D1 | +208 | very strong |
| johndoeII | C2D2 (2nd DSA) | **+6.7 ± 0.7** | strong (modest) |
| oran | C2D1 | +179 | very strong |
| mahi | C2D1 | **−291** | **disfavored** → single |
| whitney | C2D1 | **+1.5 ± 0.7** | weak (2lnB≈3, boundary) |

**Why evidence, not BIC:** BIC (which this repo *does* use — but only for the single-telescope emcee fits, `burstfit_modelselect.fit_models_bic`, where you have a posterior but no Z) is the *asymptotic* approximation −2lnZ ≈ −2lnL_max + k·ln(n). The joint nested fits give Z **directly**, and the Occam penalty is the exact Bayesian one: the gain-marginal kernel integrates the per-channel gains under a proper N(0,s²) prior → a `−½ ln det(I + (s²/σ²)M)` term that grows with component count (`burstfit_joint.py`). So an unhelpful component is penalized by the marginal likelihood itself — no k·ln(n) surrogate needed. Strictly better than BIC when you can afford the evidence integral.

**The caveat that makes whitney's +1.5 not yet final:** s² is ML-*profiled* per rung → these are empirical-Bayes (profile-Z), not clean marginals. Irrelevant at +3618; but whitney's +1.5 could be entirely profiling freedom. So whitney (and any rung landing in 2lnB ≲ 6) gets the **fixed-`gain_s2`** re-run — which converts profile-Z into a genuine Bayes factor — before I call it.
